The People

From Lafferty's opening roster:

Hilary Ardri, the Computerized Fish Tycoon and his wife Jane Chantal Ardri, an artist in all the arts.
Leo Parisi, Boy Wonder and Nuclear Scientist, and his wife Perpetua Parisi, the daughter of the Panteras.
Gorgonius Pantera, the piano-maker of the German Alps, and his wife Monika Pantera, who doesn't have to be anything except Monika.
John Barkley Towntower, the second best mathematician in the world, and the best ventriloquist, and his much too close associate Solomon Izzersted, the best mathematician in the world and sometimes ventriloquist's figure.
Denis Lollardy, the most famous forger in the world.
Caesar Oceano, the tycoon of the Strange Cargoes World-Wide Shipping Company, and his partner Prince Leonardo the Great the Golden Panther.
Laughter-Lynn Casement, who was born twice, her births sixteen years apart.
Drusilla Evenrood, an East Sussex Lady.
Mary Brandy Manx, the Mayor of Port Saint Mary on the Isle of Man.
Hieronymous Talking-Crow, a pan-scientist.
"These Fifteen persons are known as the Group of Twelve. Some of them are spares."

The Ardri HouseholdLake Tenkiller, Oklahoma

Hilary Ardri
Deceased
The Computerized Fish Tycoon
In an unreal world, the amount of fish that may be taken out of a lake has no connection with the amount of fish in the lake.
Residence
Lake Tenkiller, eastern Oklahoma
Description
"A rusty-colored man, red-haired all over his body (an Esau man). He stood an even two meters tall and was very thick in the arms and shoulders and chest. Blue-eyed when he gazed out over the land, green-eyed when he gazed over the ocean."
Computer
Inhabited by a poltergeist friend
Key Insight
Discovered the world is unreal through his fish business: "In an unreal world, the amount of fish that may be taken out of a lake has no connection with the amount of fish in the lake."
Fate: Dies at Lecco during the Night of Strangulation (Ch. 9), killed by the suffocating nightmares that ravage the world—attributed by Charles Fort's ghost to the "hundred-and-nine-year locusts."
Jane Chantal Ardri
Transformed
Artist in All the Arts / Jane Chantal High-Queen
We have lived too long in too airtight a world! We need air, we need to lift the lid to the coffin of a real world!
Also Known As
Jane Galatea (after resurrection); Jane Hunting-Horn; Jane Chantal High-Queen
Description
"Fuzzily beautiful"; a huntress "always and in everything, but she was a fuzzy and somewhat lazy huntress, one who was seldom in a hurry."
Computer
Joyeuse Vice-Reine, housed in an invisible hunting-horn that hangs on a rafter
Art
Uses her computer "only for the tedious and difficult things in art"—bronze-casting, massive sculpture, heavy drama—while she does "all the artistic parts."
Fate: Murdered at the end of the Monday feast at Sora (Ch. 4) by a nine-foot quill "driven into her mouth that was now a mouth no longer, and speared through her entire body." Rewritten by Atrox and returns as nine-year-old Jane Galatea (Ch. 6). Eventually becomes El-Khatar Giant and accepts the title "High-Queen."

The Izzersted-Towntower SymbiosisBroken Arrow, Oklahoma

Solomon Izzersted
Giant
The Best Mathematician in the World / The Smallest Man in the World
Solomon is very hard to like, but he is easy to love.
Nature
Originally "a grotesque, brilliant growth on the belly" of John Barkley Towntower—a parasitic being who dominated his host through superior mathematics and will. "I'm the only one I know to whom the phrase 'he's all head' would really apply."
Parentage
Son of Iofel the Trickster Angel, "the most ethnic of the angels"
Residence
Broken Arrow, Oklahoma
Key Trait
"Solomon is very hard to like, but he is easy to love."
Abilities
Learned all mathematics by interpreting his host's "perturbations of throat and belly muscles" during silent reading. "So I know all the mathematics that he knows, and all further mathematics that I have developed in the privacy of my own world."
Physical Description
After liberation, becomes "a bouncing, baseball-sized head-being" with "a spherical grin" and "multi-depth face."
Fate: Reborn when Prince Leonardo tears him from John Barkley's body (Ch. 8)—"born From the Panther's Teeth." Renews his youth in Foinse na n'Og. Projects himself as the 100-foot "Riant Giant" via pantograph. But: "The successor to the Top Giant is never the new Top Giant: he's the new Bottom Giant." Assigned as the Patagonian Giant—"the lowest and least." His business card: "SOLOMON IZZERSTED THE PATAGONIAN GIANT. I DO FUTURES."
John Barkley Towntower
Deceased
The Second Best Mathematician / The Best Ventriloquist
John Barkley himself had never done a mean thing in his life.
Relationship to Solomon
Host body and primero ego to Solomon. Solomon forced John to legally change his name to "Solomon Izzersted."
Profession
Ventriloquist and world-class mathematician; performed with Solomon in music halls
Fate: Murdered by Prince Leonardo the Great (Ch. 8), who "bit out his stomach"—the act that freed Solomon as an independent being.

The Parisi VillaSora, in the Apennine foothills

Leo Parisi
Deceased
Boy Wonder and Nuclear Scientist
The atoms are no more than empty boxes... Someone has short-changed me. Great God of the Atoms, You have short-changed me!
Residence
Villa at Sora, Italy, "in the foothills of the Apennine Mountains"
Description
"Still a teenager" but "one of those who remembered where he had been... he lived but a short day's travel from that wonderful place, to the East." A "twice-born youth" who "did come into the world trailing clouds of glory."
Key Insight
"The atoms are no more than empty boxes... They lack detail. They contain only such scribbles as a three-dimensional cartoonist might make... Someone has short-changed me. Great God of the Atoms, You have short-changed me!"
Discovery
Finds a nine-foot-long feather belonging to Atrox Fabulinus, "stained with blood and gore"—"a shaft of reality" whose atoms are "finely detailed, as the atoms of the whole universe are supposed to be, and commonly aren't."
Fate: Killed in a rock slide at Lecco (Ch. 9) along with Laughter-Lynn Casement and Saint Faunus. Last words: "Goodbye, Perpetua; every minute of it was fun." His wife refuses to clear the rocks: "Leo wasn't meant to grow up. Now he can be a Boy Genius forever."
Perpetua Parisi
Survived
Daughter of the Panteras / Practitioner of Behavioristic Logic
Leo wasn't meant to grow up. Now he can be a Boy Genius forever.
Parents
Gorgonius and Monika Pantera (seventh daughter of Gorgonius; Monika is his seventh wife)
Marriage
Wife of Leo Parisi
Ability
Uses "Behavioristic Logic" to predict events
Musical Work
Composed Monday at Sora for Thirteen Player Pianos—"Enchanting, enchanting!" but "a bit slight... it would not have sustained three hundred and five pianos."
Childhood
"She climbed up here to see me one summer when she was yet a young girl," the Alpine Giant recalls. They played Old Maid together. When Perpetua asks if playing cards with the snow kept him from getting lonesome, the Giant replies: "Only you could do that."
Fate: Survives as a widow. Refuses to have the rock slide cleared: "Leo wasn't meant to grow up. Now he can be a Boy Genius forever." Present at Klavierschloss for the mourning and at the final confrontation with Solomon.

Giant
The Piano-Maker of the German Alps
I have never seen a baseball.

Klavierschloss (Piano Castle) in the German Alps
Longevity
Has lived across three centuries
Compositions

Monika Pantera
Survived
Keeper of 1,001 Keys
Who doesn't have to be anything except Monika.

Klavierschloss with Gorgonius
Description
"Who doesn't have to be anything except Monika." Has purple eyes.

The Lecco EstateWhere the Adda flows from Lake Como

Denis Lollardy
Top Giant
The Most Famous Forger in the World
When a check is large enough the borderline between the genuine and the forged disappears.
Name
Should perhaps be "Lombardy" (his coat-of-arms shows the Lombardy Poplar, motto "Awaken to Laughter"). "Lollard" once meant both "mumbler" and "forger."
Residence
Estate at Lecco, Italy, "where the river Adda flows out of Lake Como." Features gardens in French, English, Italian, Moravian, Aragonese, Armenian, Persian, Arabian, Japanese, Welsh, and Irish styles.
The Craft
"His work was neither mumbled nor generally in the cheap-jack manner of a forger. All of his work was illuminating and surpassing, masterful, be-geniused, shining stuff." Forges in Latin, Low Latin, Tuscan, Old French, Old Italian, Spanish, Cataline, Old High Dutch, Icelandic, Demotic Greek, Coptic, Arabic, Ladino, Ghees, Amharic, Middle Armenian. Also in marble, bronze, terra cotta, mosaic, gold, chased silver. "And the forged checks, big ones, resounding ones. He understood a principle that many forgers never learn, that when a check is large enough the borderline between the genuine and the forged disappears."
Masterworks
The Laughing Christ of Creophylus ("better than the original—it worked miracles"); the Armenian Gospel of the Childhood of Jesus Christ; "Mandrake the Magician, purported to be by William Shakespeare" ("the greatest drama ever written"). The Pope jokes: "God just does not have the ability to author anything that good."
Expertise
"The world's greatest authority on three-dimensional pantographic projection"
Fate: Becomes successor to the Timbuktu Giant, which—due to the rotation of positions—makes him the actual Top Giant: "The successor to the Top Giant is never the new Top Giant: he's the new Bottom Giant. The position rotates." Accepts reluctantly: "I'll be a Scribbling Giant, but only because I feel it to be my duty."

Strange Cargoes Worldwide ShippersCaesar Oceano & Partner

Caesar Oceano
Giant
Shipping Magnate
I bet I could hit it a mile.
Business
Strange Cargoes World-Wide Shipping Company
Ships
The Holy Mary and others, visited during the undersea expedition (Ch. 6)
Partner
Prince Leonardo the Great (the Golden Panther)
Signature Object
A fungo baseball bat—"The wood is so lively and resilient that it will drive a baseball an extraordinary and unaccountable distance."
Fate: Becomes the Sanrio Giant. Takes a final swing at Solomon's baseball-sized head with his fungo bat at the novel's end.
Prince Leonardo the Great
Hanged
The Golden Panther / The Strange Man
I want to do something for mankind, but there is so little time.
Arrival
Delivered to Caesar Oceano's doorstep in a large crate (Ch. 3). Tag: "To Caesar Oceano, on his name day, from Gorgonius and Monika Pantera"—but the Panteras deny sending it. "I come from the Exterior Darkness," Leonardo says, "and the carrier was the Strange Cargoes Worldwide Shippers."
Identity
"I am a Black Panther who happens to have a golden mark on me everywhere except this one bar on my forehead. The distinction is important, for I am the titular ruler of all the Black Panthers in the world."
Character
Establishes the Green Pasture Counselling Service: "a soothing voice speaking out of the soft darkness to the sound of gently falling waters. And he did ease many tired and troubled souls, but he seemed not to ease his own."
Shadow
"A scraggly black panther, a rough and slightly runty beast, a hard-luck cat... Nevertheless it was an astute and deadly shadow. Deadly, deadly, deadly!"
Fate: The Murderer. Kills Jane Chantal (quill through mouth), Atrox (quill through neck), Roderick Outreach, and John Barkley Towntower (bites out stomach). Hanged by the townspeople of Port Saint Mary. On the gallows, shifts between Panther form and the Strange Man. His twin wives—a golden-dark lady and a female black panther, both "of the changing cat-clan"—wait below: "The Mystery of Evil was on him and we could do nothing."

The IndependentsScattered across the world

Laughter-Lynn Casement
Deceased
The Goose-Egg Girl / A North Sea Person
Now look at yourself in the big glass. You are the most beautiful girl in the world. —Yes, that's true, mother, I am.
Double Birth
Born first in Gaire Castle, Dublin. Then: "I was in a Shoga boarding school for fifty-five years. But by the count of the common world I was in there only a single day and night." Emerged sixteen years later from a giant goose egg: "Now look at yourself in the big glass. You are the most beautiful girl in the world." "Yes, that's true, mother, I am."
Heritage
Partly "of the Kabouter blood" through her father Fernand Kabouter Casement. The Casement family motto: "The Best of Both Worlds." Lived half of each year in Gaire Castle, half at Oosterend.
The Name
"Laughter-Lynn was given that name because of the infectious laugh that she evinced before she was twelve hours old. And yet Laughter was an old family name in her mother's line."
Art
Great paintings: Earth and Ocean and Sunshine, Earth and Ocean and Mist, Earth and Ocean and Drowned People; fantasy series The World on the Inside of a Goose-Egg.
Profession
"One of the most respected marine biologists and under-earth biologists, and under-mind biologists in the world."
Fate: Killed in a rock slide at Lecco (Ch. 9). "She is now with the deferred saints in the iron meadows of Purgatory. It will be good to have somebody with an infectious laugh like hers in that blessed-bleak place for a while." Her buried laughter still wells up "like silver music."
Drusilla Evenrood
Giant
An East Sussex Lady
All East Sussex ladies can make fire come out of their finger-tips, but most of them conceal this talent.
Residence
Evenrood Manor, East Sussex
Abilities
Can make fire come from her fingertips ("All East Sussex ladies can make fire come out of their finger-tips, but most of them conceal this talent"). Carries the phobic Giant Atrox across the moat on her back (Ch. 5).
Servant
Myrtle Mobley, whom Drusilla stops from opening her pre-dug grave
Proposal
Proposes "para-biology" for the dream world (Ch. 3)

Mary Brandy Manx
Giant
Meara of Port Saint Mary
All sea goddesses, of whatever seas anywhere in the world, are exactly sixteen years old.
Residence
Port Saint Mary, Isle of Man—"twenty-nine miles from Ireland, thirty-one miles from England, and twenty-one miles from Scotland. But the miles to Scotland are very long miles because of the treacherous currents and the howling winds."
Description
"A handsome woman with brandy-colored hair and eyes the color of those of a Manx cat." Named for her "brandy voice"—"that mellow and slightly strained voice that she got from shouting at the gulls, terns, loons, and other sea-and-shore birds on her own island shore. Those birds will not answer you, you know, unless you shout at them."

"Seven yards of linen and of wool cloth went into it." Worn for ballooning and swimming. And all sea goddesses, of whatever seas anywhere in the world, are exactly sixteen years old."
Age
"The oldest member of the Group of Twelve... on the sunny side of sixty by only two years. But sometimes, in two special cases, she was only sixteen years old."

Explains "the solid ones vs. the rarified ones": "They are the canaille, they are the lumpenproletariat... But try to get along without them." Announces that the world is dying from "lack of input" (Ch. 8).
Fate: Becomes the Illacrove Giant. Charges Solomon with bribing the Ifrit at the novel's end: "And shall I tell the rest of them here how small that bribe was?"

Deceased
A Pan-Scientist
I will not survive. I will be the scapegoat. That is my role.
Identity
Initially thought to be a pen-name of Leo Parisi's, but: "We are different persons, and we have met only once." Author of A Complete Rewriting of Human Biology discussing the larvae-state humans.
Role
Interviews the corpse/spirit of Alexander the Great alongside Leo Parisi in the library catacombs at Sora (Ch. 4). Alexander confirms that "reality must be earned" and calls Atrox "altogether second class."

"I will not survive. I will be the scapegoat. That is my role."

Countess Maude Grogley
Ally
Mother of Laughter-Lynn / One of the One Hundred Holy Snakes of Ireland
The Patrick did not expel quite all the snakes from Ireland.
Residence
Gaire Castle (East of Laughter Castle), Dublin, in the inner suburb of Lastoir de Gaire—"much older than Dublin which had engulfed it a few centuries ago. The people of this inner suburb were the original Irish who are older than the Irish."
Career
Wrote for Dublin newspapers; was a foreign correspondent in Italy, Palestine, the Low Countries, and the United States. Author of Observations of Things Both Before and After the Beginning of the World.
Secret Nature

The Giants

"But I am one of the Pillars Who Sustain the World, so I am able to say that our full complement of Pillars is twenty-one, and they are in three groups of seven each. There are Seven Saints to insure the rectitude of the world, Seven Technicians to insure the technology of the world, and Seven Scribbling Giants to write the scenarios and histories for the world."

—Der Alpenriese

The Twenty-One Pillars

The world is sustained by twenty-one Pillars in three groups of seven. When a Pillar dies, the world "stumbles a bit" until replacement is found. If two or more fail at once, "the world will stagger and nearly fall." The novel takes place during a "Changing of the Aeons" when the Giants are "in the ascendancy"—and a new Head Giant must be found or "the world will not be able to survive."

The Seven Saints

"The Saints are the easiest to replace; there are always plenty of competent saints in the world."

The Seven Technicians

"The Technicians are only slightly more difficult to replace; the difficulty is in selecting from an overabundance of them."

The Seven Scribbling Giants

"But the trouble is with Giants. These must often endure in their onerous jobs for very many years, hoping in vain for replacements so that they may be allowed to die."

The Giant Succession

As the old Giants die, each sends a messenger asking the Group of Twelve to provide replacements. The succession unfolds across the novel:

Dying Giant Successor Final Position
Atrox Fabulinus Solomon Izzersted Patagonian Giant (Bottom—rotation rule)
Hsiang Giant Drusilla Evenrood Hsiang Giant
Illacrove Giant Mary Brandy Manx Illacrove Giant
El-Khatar Giant Jane Chantal High-Queen El-Khatar Giant
Der Alpenriese (Alpine) Gorgonius Pantera Alpine Giant
Sanrio Giant Caesar Oceano Sanrio Giant
Timbuktu Giant Denis Lollardy Top Giant (last to accept = Top)

The Rotation Rule

Solomon assumes that replacing Atrox (the former Top Giant) makes him the new Top Giant. But as Gorgonius reveals:

"The successor to the Top Giant is never the new Top Giant: he's the new Bottom Giant. The position rotates. The successor to the Timbuktu Giant is the Top Giant now. And that successor is, yes, Denis Lollardy."

The last Giant to accept giantship becomes the new Top Giant. Denis was the last to accept (after Caesar accepted the Sanrio position), so "it was then that the Wave of Reassurance passed through all the people, reassurance and hope and relief." Solomon's business cards reading "TOP GIANT OF THE WORLD" are destroyed by Drusilla's fire-fingers; only those reading "SOLOMON IZZERSTED THE PATAGONIAN GIANT. I DO FUTURES" survive.

Atrox Fabulinus

The "Roman Rabelais," Top Giant and chief of the Seven Scribbling Giants who write the world's scenarios. Dead for "a little over fifteen hundred years" yet still producing new chapters distributed by the mysterious "Concerned Circus for the Distribution of New Atrox Chapters."

The Hundred-and-One Tests

Atrox's chapter "The Web of Validity" provides one-hundred-and-one tests to determine whether one is dreaming. Hilary applies thirty of them and concludes he is "thirty times dreaming."

Murder at the Sky Studio

Atrox appears as an outline at the Monday feast at Sora, drinks from a nine-gallon cup, and warns the group about mocking him. He later appears in the flesh at Oosterend, writing in the Sky Studio—a glass room "like a large head atop a long corkscrew neck," built by Saint Joseph the Carpenter atop Laughter-Lynn's house.

During the midnight murder-hour on Wednesday, Atrox is killed: "He had been speared by [his own nine-foot quill] through the back of his neck as he slumped over in his sleep, and the big quill came out through his mouth. They hadn't realized before just how big Atrox was. More than half of that nine-foot-length of spear-and-quill was in his neck and head."

The Ghost of Atrox

After death, Atrox's outline is evoked multiple times by Jane and others, growing increasingly weary: "How is a poor dead giant to get any sleep in his miserable earth with that girl-woman Jane evoking me?" He refuses to approve Solomon as his replacement until finally, exhausted: "Let the small pipsqueak Solomon be my replacement then and become the lowest and least of the seven scribbling giants. Let it be done! And don't wake me from death again or I'll get nasty!" Then "the flimsy outline of Atrox disappeared forever."

Der Alpenriese (The Alpine Giant)

The Alpine Giant dwells in "the strange cave on this very mountain" near Klavierschloss. He remembers when young Perpetua "climbed up here to see me one summer when she was yet a young girl" and they played Old Maid together. When Perpetua asks if playing with the snow kept him from getting lonesome, he says: "Only you could do that."

When his messenger Otto comes to Gorgonius asking for a replacement, Der Alpenriese delivers extensive wisdom about the nature of Giants: "It takes twelve hours for a replacement giant to begin to feel his giantness. This makes things hard for these latterday giants. But you will yet grow."

He debates Mary Brandy about the authorship of Moby-Dick: "I am a Scribbling Giant and I know something about the scribblers' trade, of sources and of authorship, of true hands and of false. I say that it was the whale who wrote the book."

His final act is to have Gorgonius "fill your stomach and chest and throat with laughter" and blow it through his body apertures: "Gorgonius, you are the Alpine Giant now. Compose the funeral march, if you can compose anything besides comedy."

The Ifrit and "Habemus Gigantem"

Monika Pantera possesses both the forged Aladdin's Lamp (made by Denis) and the true Aladdin's Lamp. When she rubs the true lamp, the Ifrit emerges and cries "Habemus Gigantem!"—"We Have a Giant!"—announcing that the world's energy is restored.

Solomon bribes the Ifrit to identify him as the "Riant Giant" (the Laughing Giant), but Mary Brandy exposes the deception: "Shall I tell them, Solomon, what a cheap-skate you were to take advantage of a poor Ifrit who didn't know one coin from another?" The true moment of restoration came when Denis accepted giantship, not Solomon's pantographic projection.

The Hundred-and-Nine-Year Locusts

The ghost of Charles Fort, evoked by Monika, explains the strangulation nightmares plaguing the world:

"The main answer is that the troubles are caused by the hundred-and-nine-year locusts. They call them that because they come every hundred-and-nine years. They're invisible. And moreover they're decapods and so are not true locusts at all. But they feed on the daily-life-elixir and diminish it so much that the world and its peoples suffer from the deprivation."

Fort warns that "the locust plague and the other plagues are a mortal danger to the world only if they carry over into the second week, so it is written in the Book of Jasher."

The Sussex Wraiths (The "Seven New Giants")

In Chapter 7, "Casual English Intellectuals" from the Royal Observatory discover a dead giant goose on the beach at East Sussex. Seven of them fight over its nine-foot feathers and declare themselves the "Seven New Giants."

Their leader Roderick Outreach proclaims: "We are the Seven Giants who will henceforth write the world! Atrox is dead, and the other six giants are tired and wishing for death. Well, we write them dead now." The ghost of Atrox responds: "The Feathers are no good no use / Unless they come from living Goose."

Just before midnight, Roderick is murdered by the Strange Man (Prince Leonardo). The surviving Sussex Wraiths return as bat-winged apparitions claiming to be "angels or messengers sent out to effect the writs of the New Giants. We are the motivation of the world. We are the future of the world." But the narrator dismisses them: "Nah, they lied. They were bats."

The Week of Tottering Terror

"The Group of Twelve has been selected to provide extraordinary and onerous service to the world without thought of their own personal comfort."

—The Concerned Circus

Prelude: Before the Journey

Chapters 1–3 establish the world, introduce the Group of Twelve, and set the crisis in motion before the physical journey begins.

Chapter 1 "Are We Dreaming?"
Oklahoma
▼

"But I am one of the Pillars Who Sustain the World, so I am able to say that our full complement of Pillars is twenty-one, and they are in three groups of seven each. There are Seven Saints to insure the rectitude of the world, Seven Technicians to insure the technology of the world, and Seven Scribbling Giants to write the scenarios and histories for the world."

—Der Alpenriese
Summary

Hilary Ardri reads Atrox Fabulinus's new chapter "The Web of Validity," containing "one-hundred-and-one tests to determine whether one is dreaming." Applying thirty tests to himself, he concludes: "I'm dreaming. By the thirty tests that I have applied to myself, I'm thirty times dreaming." He and his wife Jane Chantal—artists living in eastern Oklahoma—decide to raise the question with their mysterious "Group of Twelve."

The chapter proves the world's unreality through Hilary's Computerized Lake-Fish Company, which delivers excellent fish to three thousand Oklahoma stores despite there being no fish in the lake and Hilary having no fishing license. His computer, inhabited by a friendly poltergeist, simply programs fish into existence: "In an unreal world, the ambient is never restrictive."

The chapter introduces Solomon Izzersted—actually two persons in one body: the ventriloquist John Barkley Towntower and a sentient growth on his belly named Solomon, who learned mathematics by interpreting John's silent vocalizations. Jane Chantal mediates their partnership, and they become "the greatest advocacy mathematicians in the world," mathematically proving the world's unreality.

Characters Introduced
Hilary Ardri Jane Chantal Ardri Solomon Izzersted John Barkley Towntower Myron McMasters Joyeuse Vice-Reine (computer)
Key Scenes
  • Breakfast with Atrox: Hilary and Jane discuss the "Hundred-and-One Tests" delivered by the mysterious "Concerned Circus for the Distribution of New Atrox Chapters"
  • The Fish Business: Myron McMasters from the F&G Department cannot explain how Hilary delivers fish without fishing—proof the world operates on unreal principles
  • Jane Chantal's Art: Her computer Joyeuse Vice-Reine, housed in a hunting-horn, handles "the tedious and difficult things in art" while Jane does "all the artistic parts"
  • The Happy Artist Test: "If you ever meet a happy artist in any of the arts, fall back and regroup... for you will have stumbled into an unreal world"
  • Solomon's Origin: Born as "a dark and sullen growth" on John Barkley's belly, Solomon learned to scream "My name is Solomon Izzersted!" before John could talk
  • The Partnership: Jane Chantal mediates between the mutually-hating Solomon and John Barkley, creating the world's greatest mathematical team
Key Quotes
"To be real is to be unique. To be unreal is to be common. And the odds in favor of the world being unreal are prohibitive. There is only one chance in all infinity of it being real. But there are a billion billion and ongoing billions of chances of it being unreal."
"When you have a good thing going, don't ask questions."
—Ardri family motto
"Solomon is very hard to like, but he is easy to love."
—Jane Chantal Ardri
Thematic Seeds
Unreality Duality Computers & Poltergeists The Happy Artist Mathematical Proof
Chapter 2 "Camel's Nose"
Multiple Locations
▼

"The trouble with giants is not their stealing and eating whole herds of cattle and flocks of sheep and leaving the people destitute. Worse than this is their wanton destruction. They come with their long elephant ears and hear everything. They come with their long moist camel noses that can smell every detail and they learn every private thing about the people of a place."

—Erasthenos of Patmos, Of Wanton Giants
Summary

"It is plain by now that Atrox Fabulinus has intruded his slurpy wet Camel's nose into the tent of this account and soon will own the place." With this metafictional warning, the chapter introduces more members of the Group of Twelve while deepening the mystery of the Giant's involvement in their lives.

Laughter-Lynn Casement "remembers emerging from a giant goose egg" as a nubile young girl—sixteen years after her actual birth. She spent fifty-five years in a Shoga boarding school (which occupied only "a single day and night" of ordinary time), living underground as "a Goblin, a Kabouter, a Shoga, a Kobald, a Troll, a Fairy, a Monkey-Face." The chapter weaves in excerpts from fictional scholarly works explaining the Shoga as "human larvae"—persons who pass through an awkward stage underground before emerging as geniuses.

Leo Parisi, the teenage nuclear scientist, discovers "a feather that is three meters or nine feet long" with "blood and gore on the quill end." He knows its atoms will be "finely detailed, as the atoms of the whole universe are supposed to be, and commonly aren't"—a "shaft of reality" proving someone has been murdered. The chapter also introduces Gorgonius Pantera, the piano-maker who has lived in three centuries and builds player pianos from slow-growing Klavierholtz, and his wife Monika who possesses one thousand and one keys to their Alpine castle.

Characters Introduced
Laughter-Lynn Casement Leo Parisi Perpetua Parisi Gorgonius Pantera Monika Pantera Countess Maude Grogley Fernand Kabouter Casement
Key Scenes
  • The Goose Egg Birth: Laughter-Lynn emerges from a giant goose egg cocoon after fifty-five years as a Shoga—compressed into one night of ordinary time
  • The Bloody Feather: Leo finds a nine-foot feather, "blood and gore on the quill end"—proof of murder with a shaft of properly-detailed reality
  • The Empty Atoms: Leo rants that atoms "contain only rough schematics of even rougher schematics"—the universe is shoddily made
  • Behavioristic Logic: Perpetua predicts Leo's actions by arranging breakfast items; she even claims to influence God with silk strips
  • Piano Castle: Gorgonius has 700 player pianos made from Klavierholtz; needs to extend his life by a thousand years to complete his work
  • The 1001 Keys: Monika must kill an Alpine Eagle and wake Wife Number Three from death to forge a key for certain rooms
  • Atrox's Scriptorium: Monika knows the room in Piano Castle where Atrox "sat and wrote his ever-new chapters"
Key Quotes
"The atoms are empty boxes. They lack detail. They contain only such scribbles as a three-dimensional cartoonist might make."
—Leo Parisi
"Every person living through the human-larval state subsequently becomes a genius; and every genius of the human species will have gone through this human-larva state."
—Hieronymous Talking-Crow, A Complete Rewriting of Human Biology

Chapter 3 "Strange Cargo"
Multiple Locations
▼

"'Forget not to entertain strangers, for some have thus entertained angels unaware.' But I have an early Greek text in which the wording was 'Forget not to entertain strangers whether men or giants or waifs or even dogs or wilder beasts'... I believe that angels can and often do come among us in the forms of giants and waifs and bears and wolves and dogs. So entertain them and feed them if they come to you, but do not entertain them uncritically. I believe that angels come to us under these forms, but I believe that devils come to us under these forms much more often."

—Atrox Fabulinus, New Chapters Found at Sora
Summary

Prince Leonardo the Great arrives at Caesar Oceano's doorstep in a large crate, purportedly from Gorgonius and Monika Pantera—who deny sending it. The Golden Panther speaks: "I come from the Exterior Darkness." Together, Caesar and Leonardo take over the Strange Cargoes Worldwide Shippers. But Leonardo grows moody: "I want to do something for mankind, but there is so little time." He establishes the Green Pasture Counselling Service to ease "tired and troubled souls"—though he cannot ease his own.

The chapter completes the roster of the Group of Twelve: Drusilla Evenrood, the shrill-voiced biologist of East Sussex; Denis Lollardy, the master forger whose works are "too good" (his Laughing Christ of Creophylus actually works miracles, terrifying him); and Mary Brandy Manx, the sixty-year-old Mayor of Port Saint Mary who becomes sixteen when swimming in the Spanish Depths or ascending past a mile in her balloon.

The crisis arrives: "Seven of our magic Group of Twelve have received gunshot wounds (none of them fatal) within the last hour." Each believes they were shot by their shadow. Hilary counts "fourteen or fifteen entities that are shadowing our Group of Twelve... alien to us and surely organized. So there is organization out there." Leonardo himself is "terribly bitten and mauled" by his own shadow—a "scraggly black panther" that is "deadly, deadly, deadly!"

Characters Introduced
Caesar Oceano Prince Leonardo the Great Drusilla Evenrood Denis Lollardy Mary Brandy Manx Hieronymous Talking-Crow (mentioned) The Shadows

  • Strange Cargo: Leonardo arrives in a crate "from the Exterior Darkness" via Strange Cargoes Worldwide Shippers
  • Green Pasture Counselling: Leonardo becomes "a soothing voice speaking out of the soft darkness" to ease troubled souls
  • The Laughing Christ: Denis's forgery works genuine miracles—curing melancholy, fixing a Roman lady's horrible nose—terrifying him
  • The Seven Shootings: All twelve members are shot (non-fatally) by their shadows within an hour; Mary Brandy heals hers with gull-oil
  • Mary Brandy's Transformations: She becomes a sixteen-year-old sea goddess at the Spanish Depths, or a low-sky goddess above a mile
  • Leonardo Mauled: His shadow—a "scraggly black panther"—attacks him: "Deadly, deadly, deadly!"
  • "Organization Out There": Hilary realizes the fourteen or fifteen shadows are "alien to us and surely organized"

"I come from the Exterior Darkness."
—Prince Leonardo the Great
"The fourteen or fifteen entities that are shadowing our Group of Twelve are alien to us and are surely organized. So there is organization out there. And there is alienism outside of our dream."
—Hilary Ardri
"Since we live in a Forgers' World, maybe we should make a King of that master forger Denis."
—Hilary Ardri

The Journey Begins: Monday to Wednesday

Chapters 4–6 take the Group from Italy to Ireland to the Netherlands. The first two murders occur; reality theories multiply.

Chapter 4 "Monday at Sora"
Sora, Italy
♪ †1
▼
Location

Villa of Leo & Perpetua Parisi, near Sora in the Apennine foothills, sixty miles east of Rome. The villa contains a catacomb library where "any vessel of knowledge or information that you wish, whether of book-scroll or truth-in-wine or spirit-of-the-dead, will come immediately to your hand if only you reach for it"—catalogued under the RYHFIAIIT system ("Reach Your Hand For It And It Is There").

Music

♪ Monday at Sora for Thirteen Player Pianos, composed by Perpetua Parisi. Set to play "for twenty-four hours"—but the pianos are buried with the villa and will play "until the end of the world."

Summary

The Group assembles in the flesh for the first time at the Parisi villa for a midnight feast. Their "private video-world-conference" is tapped by thousands, then millions, generating worldwide panic as observers apply Atrox's tests: "We are only a dream and the world is only a dream." Strangely, 80% of the audience pass as wide-awake—"those of inferior minds, the canaille, the lumpenproletariat... They are the solid ones. We rarified ones are those filled with air."

Old neighbors Gioia and Timore warn that Atrox is furious—he "has already come to consider you as stingy and miserly people and he repents that he has made you." They bring a nine-gallon drinking cup and a plate fit for a giant. Denis Lollardy and Solomon Izzersted conjure the transparent outline of Atrox, who eats eels from a funnel and drinks from the massive cup. But the real Atrox is also present—"Who is mocking me? You are mocking me with this outline to your death."

In the catacombs, Hieronymous Talking-Crow interviews Alexander the Great, who explains that "reality is not something that one has the right and title to. It is something that must be earned." Alexander dismisses Atrox: "His mind is altogether second class." Jane Chantal is revealed as the hoaxer who projected Atrox's outline—and Atrox threatens: "Woman, you mock me and you burlesque me at your peril. Persist in this and you will have seen your last midnight."

Key Scenes
  • The Worldwide Panic: Millions test themselves with Atrox's 101 tests; panic spreads: "We can't wake up because there is nothing to wake up to"
  • The Nine-Gallon Cup: Old Gioia brings a cup "that is a cup" for the giant—"When the Atrocious Giant is angry you may not feel it in your big house, but his anger cracks the walls and ceilings of my little house under the mountain"
  • The Giant's Outline: Jane Chantal projects an illusory Atrox while Solomon provides the voice—but the real Atrox appears and speaks in "a third giant voice, one of tired and ragged strength"
  • Alexander's Interview: "All deserts are unreal... If you conquer one such land, what have you conquered? And if you die there of the unreality disease, you are really dead"
  • The Haunted House Warning: Jane Chantal insists "We must all stay together in this horrible place lest we be picked off and killed one by one"—but they laugh her to scorn
  • Jane Chantal's Murder: At the twenty-third hour, Jane screams "like an arrow"—then the scream rises beyond human hearing. She is found "speared clear through" by a nine-foot quill
  • The Earthquake: The villa is buried by earthquake and land-slide; they escape via a 1,200-year-old world terminal to Dublin
Deaths

Jane Chantal Ardri — speared through the mouth by nine-foot quill, "driven into her mouth that was now a mouth no longer, and speared through her entire body and coming out below"

Key Quotes
"Reality is not something that one has the right and title to. It is something that must be earned. And I never spent much time in unreal lands."
—Alexander the Great
"His mind is altogether second class. But we can't all be Alexanders, can we?"
—Alexander on Atrox
Thematic Elements
Mockery & Consequence Reality Must Be Earned Haunted House The First Murder
Chapter 5 "Tuesday at Gaire Castle"
Dublin, Ireland
♪
▼
Location

Gaire Castle (East of Laughter Castle), Dublin, Ireland. "Castle Gaire cannot be seen from any of the five streets that encircle it, nor from the air above it. It is a large pentagon-shaped building which has been mistaken for a large pentagon-shaped hill for the last several centuries." One hundred shops back directly into the Castle, each paying a shilling a day in rent.

Music

♪ Tuesday at Gaire Castle for Three Perpetual Player Harps, composed by Gorgonius Pantera. Set to play "till the world ends, less one day"—the Countess always hedges her bets.

Summary

The Group arrives "bloodied and battered" from the ancient world terminal, which "dropped us so rudely into the street"—the mechanism "twelve hundred years too old to be a terminal at all." The Archangel Isradel stands on a street corner, disguised as a bronze statuette; "his eyes blink every seventeen minutes." They enter through Donohoe's Groggery, one of the hundred shops surrounding the hidden castle.

Countess Maude Grogley, Laughter-Lynn's mother, welcomes them: "All of you are marooned East of Reality, and you are questing to find your way back to Reality." She receives mythical visitors every Tuesday: the Morning Giant, the Morning Angel, the Ogre-Sioga, and Saint Brandon. The Morning Angel opines that "Death is but a minor episode in life. I surely wouldn't count it among the ten great turning-points of my life."

Saint Brandon explains the lens-shaped earth—"about eighteen hundred miles in diameter, about a hundred miles thick at its center"—which floats on the spherical earth "which is less than cloud-thin when seen correctly." Atrox arrives but cannot cross the moat alone; Drusilla Evenrood carries him across on her back, fulfilling her childhood dream. Atrox works to "un-murder" Jane Chantal, producing transparent figures that collapse "like punctured balloons" until finally producing something more solid.

Key Scenes
  • The Archangel Isradel: "Angels commonly move so slowly that people don't realize that they're alive"—people used to tie their horses to him as a hitching post
  • Countess Maude's Welcome: "Whatever your experiments and researches, you can carry them out here. We do have facilities for everything. Every cupboard in the Castle is full of facilities"
  • The Morning Visitors: The Morning Giant proposes to Mary Brandy; the Ogre-Sioga explains "there are two sides to the world, the inside and the outside"
  • Saint Brandon's Cosmography: He sailed to "the very edge of the lens-shaped or real world" and gazed into the void; the spherical world below was "no more than wispy clouds and gouts of mist"
  • Drusilla Carries Atrox: She fulfills her childhood legend by carrying the phobic giant across the moat—he weighs "a hundred stone or more" and pays her a Roman silver sestertius
  • Atrox Rewrites Jane: He produces transparent Jane-figures that collapse, each "a little bit more Jane-like. And a little more solid"
  • The Laughing Christ Dispute: Atrox claims Denis stole the statue; Denis insists he forged it: "You buried him in your mind. And I found him there"
Deaths

No deaths this day

Key Quotes
"Death is but a minor episode in life. I surely wouldn't count it among the ten great turning-points of my life."
—The Morning Angel
"If he killed Jane Chantal your wife, then he will just have to un-kill her. He'll have to bring her back to life."
—Countess Maude Grogley
Thematic Elements
Lens-Shaped Earth East of Reality Un-Murder Giants' Phobias
Chapter 6 "Wednesday at Oosterend"
Oosterend, Netherlands
♪ †1
▼
Location

Laughter-Lynn's Sea-House, Oosterend, Terschelling Island, Netherlands. Features the Great Circular Stairway—"one of the Three Wonders of the house and one of the Seven Wonders of the World"—running from the Monsters' Den (two levels below the sea) to the unsupported Sky Studio. Built by Saint Joseph the Carpenter, who "can repair anything, anything."

Music

♪ Wednesday at Oosterend for Seven Steam Calliopes, composed by Gorgonius Pantera, orchestrated with help from Saint Joseph who converted the ordinary calliopes to player calliopes.

Summary

Atrox writes "Oosterend" on his parchment and the Group is transported instantly. They land "soft as the breast of a goose"—unlike the rough Irish shuttle. A strange creature runs up the beach singing "Who am I? Who am I?" It is Jane Galatea, nine years old, partially rewritten by Atrox. Her mouth is "twice as big as it should be"—Atrox says he made it too small before, "whereas it should have been twice as big to express me properly."

They tour the Circular Stairway, descending to Drowned Man Shoal where the dead complain "Nobody ever stops to talk with us anymore." They meet Okeanoids, Nereids, and Ocean-Giants who want a "non-water-soluble copy" of Atrox's tests. Caesar Oceano finds three Strange Cargoes ships; the group has tea-and-rum with the sea captains who explain that Caesar became an "instant billionaire" from the Ocean's lottery.

Saint Joseph arrives: "I will work for my evening meal. I can repair anything." He converts the seven steam calliopes to player calliopes. In the Sky Studio, Atrox explains: "You are a dozen or more from among the six thousand characters I have written to represent the six-billion persons who will have lived in the world after my death." At midnight, Atrox is murdered—speared through the back of the neck with his own quill, "and the big quill came out through his mouth."

Key Scenes
  • Jane Galatea Returns: A nine-year-old runs up the beach: "I don't want to be the way I was before. I want to be better than I was before"
  • The Drowned Dead: "We can't stand each other. Who could like old dead drowned and smelly people like ourselves?"
  • Ocean Philosophy: Sea-nymphs invite them to "come sit at our feet in our mansions and learn true philosophy"—but breathing apparatus "introduces a grotesque element"
  • The Ocean's Lottery: Caesar Oceano was selected by name to become an instant billionaire from the "festering accumulated gold of the ocean"
  • Saint Joseph's Repair: He fixes the calliopes after a meal of "Dutch bread and ewe-milk cheese and codfish"—as he once built the Circular Stairway during a half-hour nap
  • Atrox's Revelation: "I live yet in the year of restored salvation four hundred and fifty-three... I have now written the world to about the year two thousand"
  • The Murder: At midnight, horrible screaming—"somebody was dying in a much more violent way than would have been possible for Jane Chantal"
  • The Strange Man: A "young, handsome, fair, smiling, incredibly urbane man, bright of feature, open of soul, and covered with blood" appears and vanishes when the lights go out
Deaths

Atrox Fabulinus — "speared by it through the back of his neck as he slumped over in his sleep, and the big quill came out through his mouth. More than half of that nine-foot-length of spear-and-quill was in his neck and head."

Key Quotes
"You are a dozen or more from among the six thousand characters I have written to represent the six-billion persons who will have lived in the world after my death. You are sketches that I did not quite fill out."
—Atrox Fabulinus
"I will find the murderer and I will see him hanged on the gallows in my own town. We have a fine gibbet-gallows there... it hasn't been used in more than three hundred years. But it will be used this year, it will be used this week."
—Mary Brandy Manx
Thematic Elements
Characters in a Novel The Strange Man Saint Joseph Twice-Big Mouth

The Week Continues: Thursday to Saturday

Chapters 7–9 bring escalating deaths and world-failure as the "hundred-and-nine-year locusts" devour the world's input.

Chapter 7 "Thursday at East Sussex"
East Sussex, England
♪ †1
▼

"It appears, therefore, that life cannot be completely identified with the physical world around it." —Tocquet

"Day and night, aloft, from the high towers / And terraces, the Earth and Ocean seem / To sleep in one another's arms, and dream / Of waves, flowers, clouds, woods, rocks, and all that we / Read in their smiles and call reality." —Shelley

"Humankind cannot bear very much reality." —T.S. Eliot

Location

Evenrood Manor, East Sussex, England. Drusilla's country estate in "a leafy land of brown and red, / A pounding ocean that enthralls." The ocean is three miles away, "all downhill."

Music

♪ Thursday at East Sussex for Three Fiddles, composed by Gorgonius Pantera, played by the Ancient Fiddlers (twelve musicians rotating in shifts). Set to play "until the end of the world, less three days."

Summary

At Evenrood Manor, housemaid Myrtle Mobley has already begun opening Drusilla's grave: "I had just received the report that you had died on one of the Dutch reef-islands." In the Welsh hills, little Audrey Evenrood and Jane paint and project Atrox's ghost back into outline form—but he is only nine years old now, as Jane was when she first returned: "Back from outer cloud and cold / Day today I'm nine years old."

The "casual English Intellectuals" descend upon the Manor, smoking pipes and demanding the giant sinecures: "We believe that we are the most important group of futurologists who have ever lived... we believe that the future deserves the best." They dismiss Atrox's flickering outline as "trivial dead walking trash." Jane warns: "This house becomes a murder house now. All of you people must stay very close together."

Word comes that a giant goose—"the very scarce ones with the long wing feathers"—lies dead on the beach. The Intellectuals sprint for the shore: "Seven Sinecures! The genuine quills are the genuine scepters of office." Seven return with nine-foot feathers and declare themselves the New Giants: "We are the Seven Giants who will henceforth write the world!" But Atrox's ghost warns: "The Feathers are no good no use / Unless they come from living Goose." At midnight, Roderick Outreach—the self-proclaimed First New Giant—is speared to death by the Strange Man.

Key Scenes
  • Drusilla's Grave: Four spadefuls already turned; tag reads "Open grave here at eight o'clock this morning"
  • Atrox's Outline Revived: Audrey and Jane project and describe him back—"Giant back from die and dee / Tell us, tell how old you be?"
  • The Casual English Intellectuals: From Oxford, Cambridge, Edinburgh, Sandhurst—"brains in their pipes... they suck their brain thoughts out puff by puff"
  • The Giant Goose: Dead on the beach; seven fight to claim the feathers as "scepters of office"
  • Atrox's Warning: "The Feathers are no good no use / Unless they come from living Goose"
  • Leonardo's Ominous Words: "In a world that has gone strange, even one's closest neighbor and friend becomes a stranger"
  • Roderick's Murder: At midnight, the Strange Man strikes again; "speared to death with his nine-foot-long spear-quill driven into his mouth"
Deaths

Roderick Outreach — "First New Giant," murdered by the Strange Man; "speared to death with his nine-foot-long spear-quill driven into his mouth and emerging from the left lumbar region of his lower back"

Key Quotes
"The Feathers are no good no use / Unless they come from living Goose."
—Atrox's ghost
"Giantship cannot be claimed—must be legitimately inherited."
—Narrative implication

Illegitimate Succession Dead Feathers Professional vs. Amateur Murder House
Chapter 8 "Friday at Port Saint Mary"
Isle of Man
♪ †3
▼

"To sum up, I think that all suggested accounts of the origin of the Solar System are subject to serious objections. The conclusion in the present state of the subject would be that the system cannot exist."

—Harold Jeffres, 1970
Location

Port Saint Mary, Isle of Man, with neighboring Port Erin and Castletown. The three towns share a gallows at Spanish Head, "inspected every year and its readiness certified, though it hasn't been used in more than three hundred years."

Music

♪ Friday at Port Saint Mary for Three Hundred Hunting-Horns (and Three Penny-Whistles), performed all night to ward off the Strangulation Nightmares.

Summary

The Group arrives to bonfires and hubbub. The Dublin Morning Docket carries three articles by scientists—Hennessee, Delany, Monroney—cataloging the world's failures: "a clear decrease in local gravity, in the magnetic field of the world, in the coriolis force of the world... the bonding of the earth's pelt." The world is "being strangled to death by lack of input." John Barkley Towntower quietly prepares: "I know that this is my death-day... do you suppose there is any way that you can survive without me?"

That afternoon, Leonardo tears out John Barkley's stomach to free Solomon Izzersted. The townspeople hang Leonardo on the ancient gibbet. As he dies, he transforms: "the person hanging from the gallows-gibbet was no longer the Golden Panther. It was a man... young, handsome, fair, smiling (even in death), incredibly urbane." He is revealed as the murderer of Atrox, Jane (the first time), and Roderick: "Every Group of Twelve has its Judas."

Solomon bounces free—"the size of a baseball, and two-thirds of that was head"—crying "At last I'm free!" That night, the Night of Strangulation, bonfires and hunting-horns hold off the Sussex Wraiths while millions die worldwide in choking nightmares. Hieronymous Talking-Crow perishes: "He died in a shouting and strangling nightmare... 'I will be the scapegoat. That is my role.'"

Key Scenes
  • The Scientific Catalog: Hennessee lists failing forces—gravity, magnetism, radiocarbon influx, helium-4 efflux, earth's pelt bonding
  • John Barkley's Premonition: "I know that this is my death-day"—signs everything over to Solomon
  • Leonardo's Attack: He tears out John Barkley's stomach; townspeople hang him on the gibbet
  • The Transformation: Leonardo alternates between panther and Strange Man even in death
  • Solomon Freed: "Like a flea, I can jump more than twenty times my own height"
  • The Female Shadow: Leonardo's twin wives—"We were born twins. We are of the changing cat-clan. Each of us was brided to him"—keep vigil
  • Night of Strangulation: Three hundred hunting-horns, bonfires, penny-whistles; the Sussex Wraiths come ("bat-wings... claiming to be giants")
  • Hieronymous Dies: "He died in a shouting and strangling nightmare"—the scapegoat
Deaths

John Barkley Towntower — "Leonardo had bitten the whole and entire stomach out of John Barkley Towntower to get Solomon"

Prince Leonardo the Great — hanged on the gibbet-gallows; "Night and day he will hang there and change, until the end of the week or the world"

Hieronymous Talking-Crow — "shouting and strangling nightmare"—died as "the scapegoat"

Key Quotes
"Every Group of Twelve has its Judas, except that Leonardo stood a little bit outside of our strict count of twelve. And he had the Mark of Cain on him."
—Denis Lollardy
"The Group of Twelve had now lost to death at Port Saint Mary three persons... And still there were twelve of them."
—Narrative

Lecco, Italy

"Whether toward the time of the Judgement the Sun and Moon will be darkened in very truth?"

—Second Article of Question 73 on Supplement to the Summa Theologica, Aquinas
Location

Denis Lollardy's Estate, Lecco, Lombardy, "where the river Adda flows out of Lake Como." Features French, English, Italian, Moravian, Aragonese, Armenian, Persian, Arabian, and Japanese Gardens, plus Irish Gardens (newly written by Jane). Includes Denis's observatory and his collection of forgeries.

Music

♪ Saturday at Lecco for Seven Flutes, composed by Gorgonius Pantera, played by Cipriano Settiflauti ("Seven Flutes") and six unemployed friends.

Summary

Gorgonius confirms the astronomical readings: "There is no doubt that the stars, the moon, the sun have been darkened by as much as twelve percent." The Eleven are now reduced to Ten: Hilary Ardri died overnight "in a strangulation nightmare." An Arabian messenger brings Jane the El-Khatar Giant's offer; she accepts immediately: "I'm born for the job. I'm a camel's nose just like Atrox was." She changes her name from Ardri to "Ard-ban-rion"—High Queen.

They tour Denis's treasures: the matched originals-and-forgeries, the totem poles with imprisoned spirits, the microscope that reveals "whole invisible empires" inside atoms. They evoke Charles Fort's ghost, who explains the "hundred-and-nine-year locusts"—invisible decapods feeding on "daily-life-elixir." Fort: "Dying was one of the least important things in my life anyhow... I've been alive and I've been dead, but dead's a little bit better. It's more spacious."

The Laughing Christ statue rises from its burial cave; a lesser spirit emerges—Saint Faunus, "patron of merriment," a faun who lived a thousand years and was then canonized. Solomon plunges into the Fountain of Youth and emerges with eternal youth. But when Laughter-Lynn, Leo, and Faunus climb the mountain to strike new springs, a rock slide buries them. Leo's last words: "Goodbye, Perpetua; every minute of it was fun."

Key Scenes
  • The 12% Dimming: Stars, moon, sun darkened—"enough to extinguish life on Earth if continued as long as three years"
  • Jane Accepts Giantship: "I know almost everything about the gianting business... I'm born for the job"
  • Denis's Collection: The Laughing Christ, totem poles with trapped spirits, Monika claims the two dingy lamps
  • Charles Fort Evoked: "Abra dabra ookie ort, / Come and visit, Charley Fort"—explains the hundred-and-nine-year locusts
  • The Laughing Christ: Denis pulls it up by rope; Saint Faunus emerges as a lesser spirit
  • Solomon's Eternal Youth: Plunges into the Fountain of Youth—"any way he plunged into it would be nearly head-first, since he was mostly head"
  • The Rock Slide: Laughter-Lynn, Leo, and Faunus buried striking new springs; "the bonding of the earth's pelt has really weakened"
Deaths

Hilary Ardri — died in a strangulation nightmare during the night

Laughter-Lynn Casement — buried in the rock slide; "From laughter plowed into the earth / Will grow a thousand years of mirth"

Leo Parisi — buried in the rock slide; last words: "Goodbye, Perpetua; every minute of it was fun"

Saint Faunus — buried in the rock slide; "one brief moment of fear and sorrow before he was terminated"

Key Quotes
"Dying was one of the least important things in my life anyhow. The only difference is that I know more people now. I know the living and the dead."
—Charles Fort's ghost
"Goodbye, Perpetua; every minute of it was fun."
—Leo Parisi's last words

Beyond the Week: Sunday to Ninth Day

Chapters 10–12 move beyond the conventional week into extra-temporal days where "the dead and the living mingle on easy terms of friendliness."

Chapter 10 "Sunday at Klavierschloss"
German Alps
♪ †1
▼

"He who is throned in Heaven laughs" —Psalms

"Oh we buried Laughing Kelly in a box without a top. / 'You are dead now, man,' we told him, 'and that laughing's got to stop.'" —Irish Song

Location

Klavierschloss (Piano Castle), the high German Alps home of Gorgonius and Monika Pantera. The Alpine Giant (Der Alpenriese) lives in "the strange cave on the top of this very mountain."

Music

♪ Sunday at Klavierschloss for 399 Player Pianos, composed by Gorgonius Pantera—"by far the best he had ever done." He had "hoarded" these songs "in his mind and his genius for parts of the three centuries in which he had lived."

Summary

At the rock-slide, Countess Maude Grogley arrives via her eighth-century world terminal to mourn her daughter: "That brat never had any worries... She is now with the deferred saints in the iron meadows of Purgatory." The Nine don sackcloth and pour ashes over their heads; the priest says "the Mass for the World Mortally Sick and Perhaps Dying."

Otto, who lives higher up the mountain, brings word from Der Alpenriese: the Alpine Giant wishes to die and offers Gorgonius his position. Gorgonius accepts: "I'll take the position mainly to keep out the incompetents." On the snowy mountain peak, the giant gives the formula: "When even one of the Pillars of Wisdom who support the world dies, the whole world staggers until that Pillar is replaced."

Monika rubs her dingy lamp—Denis's forgery—and a forgery-Ifrit appears, eager to grant wishes. When she claims she needs nothing, the Ifrit is devastated: "I have crossed ten thousand years and a hundred million miles to serve you. And you don't want anything!" Solomon schemes with his New York agent about "vaudeville ballyhoo techniques" to promote a giant of his choosing. As midnight approaches, the Alpine Giant fills his lungs with air, dies, and is buried with a hunting-horn in his mouth. A hundred seconds later, the horn sounds—"but weakly, not at all loud."

Key Scenes
  • Sackcloth and Ashes: The Nine mourn in penance garments; "Mass for the World Mortally Sick and Perhaps Dying"
  • The Alpine Giant's Formula: "The world is supported by a number of lonely, devoted, and austere persons, the Pillars of Wisdom"
  • Gorgonius Accepts: "I'll take the position mainly to keep out the incompetents"
  • The Forgery-Ifrit: Denis's fake lamp produces a fake Ifrit; Monika asks only that he "bide with us for a while"
  • Solomon's Schemes: "I'll find the man for that job... The man for any job in the world can be found on the job markets"
  • Playing Cards With Death: Perpetua puts a deck in the Giant's hands—"you can whip out the deck of cards and challenge the other person to a game of Old Maid"
  • The Weak Hunting-Horn: Jane wrote that the Giant would blow his horn mightily after death—"but weakly, not at all loud"
Deaths

Der Alpenriese (Alpine Giant) — voluntary death after finding his replacement; buried with hunting-horn in mouth on "the first terrace just below the mountain crest"

Key Quotes
"When even one of the Pillars of Wisdom who support the world dies, the whole world staggers until that Pillar is replaced. When the number of the pillars is reduced by two or more, then there is catastrophe."
—Der Alpenriese
"There is no canonical requirement, no, Solomon. Only that the people should gaze up at him in awe and say 'Now there is a Giant.'"
—Der Alpenriese on giant qualifications

Legitimate Succession Sackcloth & Ashes Forgery vs. Original Vaudeville Ballyhoo
Chapter 11 "At the Eighth Day of the Week"
City of the Eighth Day
▼

"Eighth Day of the Week — this has been described as a Computerized State of Mind. It is both a time and a place and a condition, but it does not impinge on ordinary time or ordinary place... There are only about a million people in the world who know about and enjoy the Eighth Day of the Week."

—Intimations of Immortality in Early Computer Science, Diogenes Pontifex
Location

The City of the Eighth Day, a "cool and pleasant place where it is always afternoon." The Archangel Isradel stands as warden "East of Joy Garden." The city contains "an anthology of pleasant places" including the Irish Gardens from Lecco.

Summary

Solomon departs for New York "to be about my father's business"—Iofel the Trickster Angel. Jane rewrites the hunting-horn episode with greater power: "People will hear the hunting-horn at nights for many miles around." The Group enters the Eighth Day, guided by the Archangel Isradel—"Angels sometimes move so slowly that people don't realize that they're alive."

The remaining Giant positions fill rapidly: Caesar Oceano accepts the Sanrio Giant's mantle ("it was mind-to-mind between myself and the Sanrio Giant as he died"); Denis Lollardy becomes the Timbuktu Giant ("qualified as a giant in all other ways... the best possible forger in the world"). Monika rubs the genuine Aladdin's Lamp. The true Ifrit appears—"Oh, Oh, Oh, why do you have to look like that? Only once in a thousand years do I draw a lady with purple eyes"—and Monika wishes for the replacement of the Twenty-First Pillar.

Countess Maude transforms into a gold-and-green snake (she is one of "The One Hundred Holy Snakes of Ireland") and plunges into the Fountain of Youth. Solomon bounces multilocally between the Group and New York, scheming to project "my Giant!" with Denis's pantograph. At the Eighth Day's close, "a sudden wave of reassurance passed through all living people." The Ifrit cries: "Habemus Gigantem—We Have a Giant!" The new giant's title: the "Riant Giant" or "Laughing Giant."

Key Scenes
  • The Archangel Isradel: "The museum catalog that perpetually offers him for sale says that he is a Bronze Statue of an Angel with a Flaming Sword"
  • Giant Successions: Caesar accepts Sanrio; Denis accepts Timbuktu; Drusilla and Mary Brandy accept their mantles
  • The True Ifrit: Monika wishes for the replacement of "the Twenty-First Pillar of Righteousness, the chicken-head of all the pillars"
  • Countess Maude's Transformation: She is a were-snake; "The Patrick did not expel quite all the snakes from Ireland"
  • Dead and Living Mingle: "The dead seem a little more talented... 'Why worry about life?' they tell the living. 'It's only temporary.'"
  • "Habemus Gigantem": The wave of reassurance—"everything from the magnetism and gravitation of the world to the efflux of Helium-4 was once more right"
Deaths

No deaths this day — but the dead mingle freely with the living

Key Quotes
"The dead and the living mingle there on easy terms of friendliness and familiarity. The dead seem a little more talented... 'Why worry about life?' they tell the living. 'It's only temporary.'"
—Narrative on the Eighth Day

—The True Ifrit
