Painting by William-Adolphe Bouguereau (1825–1905). Among Denis Lollardy's forgeries: "Bouguereau's Youth; Courbet's The Stone Breakers; so many of the better-than-the-originals forgeries."
Bouncer
Nickname for Solomon Izzersted after he becomes a "bouncing, baseball-sized" head (following John Barkley Towntower's murder by Leonardo). The Alpine Giant addresses him: "I do not laugh at you now, Bouncer, I do not laugh at you." The name reflects both his physical bouncing and his aggressive self-promotion.
Brandon, Saint
Saint Brendan the Navigator (c. 484–c. 577). "Saint Brandon came in and found pleasant accommodation with Drusilla Evenrood" at Gaire Castle. "Saint Brandon also was a giant, a thing that is seldom mentioned." He sailed with pirates in his youth and speaks of traveling in "the Year of Restored Salvation Five Hundred and Fifty-Three." Discusses the real/unreal question and describes the world as a "lens-world" with a surface.
Brighton
English coastal city in East Sussex. A Chinese seaman arrives at Evenrood Manor looking "as if he had been walking for several hours, possibly from Brighton," bearing news that the Atrox Giant is dead and the Hsiang Giant seeks a replacement.
British
Of or pertaining to Great Britain. Drusilla Evenrood is described as "a British person" who is "a biologist in a wider sense than were several of the Group of Twelve."
British Columbia of Canada of North America
Canadian province, source of original totem poles that Denis Lollardy forged. "There were nine pair of matched originals-and-forgeries of totem poles. The originals were from British Columbia of Canada of North America. The forgeries were from the talented buck-bladed knife of Denis Lollardy."
British Library
National library of the United Kingdom. Referenced in the novel's publication information: "A CIP catalogue record for this book is available from the British Library."
Britishers
British people. One of the casual English Intellectuals exclaims "By George the Seventh, that's good!" upon hearing Thursday at East Sussex for Three Fiddles. The narration notes: "one of the Britishers admitted."
Britons
British people. Sandra Ott, one of the self-proclaimed new giantesses, dismissively warns: "all you lesser persons around here, whether Britons or Twelvers, you had better be quiet and stay out of the way. There is nothing easier for us than to write you out of the world."
Brittany in France
Region in northwestern France (ancient Amorica). Part of the Sioga-Kobald Belt: "Moravia, Brittany in France, Transylvania in the Balkans, Huesco in Spain, Epirus in Greece"—places where Little People and their kind dwell.
Brittany of France
See Brittany in France. "And in the America" suggests the Sioga presence extended across the Atlantic.
Broken Arrow Daily Ledger Overseas Edition
Oklahoma newspaper with international reach. Solomon Izzersted's local paper, published in Broken Arrow (near Tulsa). See Broken Arrow Ledger.
Broken Arrow Ledger
"One of the very few papers in the world" to report accurately on the Giant crisis and world situation. Solomon Izzersted uses it to promote his campaign for Top Giant with "vaudeville ballyhoo."
Bronx, New York
"My native town," says Charles Fort. He recalls its diverse population: "Jews, Irish, Italians, Blacks, and Germans coexisted with each other" in the Bronx of his youth. Fort (1874–1932) was indeed born in Albany but lived much of his life in the Bronx.
Brueghel's The Land of Cockayne
Painting by Pieter Brueghel the Elder (1567). One of Denis Lollardy's masterwork forgeries: "Brueghel's The Land of Cockayne; Bosch's The Ship of Fools; Honore's David and Goliath." The subject—a mythical land of plenty and idleness—resonates with the novel's themes of unreality and wish-fulfillment.
C
Caesar Strange Cargo Oceano
Full name/epithet of Caesar Oceano, emphasizing his connection to the Strange Cargoes shipping company. "Have you ever looked at the eyes of Caesar Strange Cargo Oceano?" suggests his slant-eyed appearance qualifies him for the Sanrio (Asian) Giant position.
Cain
Biblical figure, son of Adam and Eve. Referenced in the Genesis parallel: "And Cain went out from the Presence of the Lord and dwelt in the Land of Nod to the East of Eden." The novel connects this to Gaire (Laughter) as Eden's parallel. Also referenced regarding the Mark of Cain—Leonardo bears "the golden Mark of Cain all over him" (his golden coloring), which paradoxically protects murderers: "How many bad men have been spared because they bore the beautiful golden Mark of Cain!"
Caislean Sciotail
Irish: "Giggle Castle." Another name for Gaire Castle, emphasizing its laughter theme. Sciotail suggests giggling or tittering.
Caladium Music Hall
Dublin music hall on Show-House Lane. Donohoe the grogshop-man remembers: "John Barkley Towntower there and his talking belly-button. They did their act at the Caladium Music Hall up the street." Establishes the vaudeville history of Solomon/John Barkley.
California
American state. Mentioned by Gorgonius when contemplating wines: "I wonder what would happen if I thought of some of the modern wines of Hungary or France or California?"
Cambridge
English university town. The casual English Intellectuals come "from Peterhouse and Corpus Christi and Magdalene of Cambridge, from Balliol and Merton and All Souls and Somerville of Oxford."
Cambridge University Observatory
Astronomical institution. One of the places from which the casual English Intellectuals hail, listed with "the Royal Observatory at Edinburgh, Dunsink Observatory in Dublin, the University Observatory at Oxford, the Cambridge University Observatory, the Royal Military College at Sandhurst."
Camel's Nose
Chapter 2's title. From the epigraph by Erasthenos of Patmos: "The trouble with giants is not their stealing and eating whole herds of cattle... They come with their long moist camel noses that can smell every detail and they learn every private thing about the people of a place." Atrox Fabulinus "has intruded his slurpy wet Camel's nose into the tent of this account and soon will own the place." Later, Solomon claims: "I'm a camel's nose just like Atrox was. I like to" intrude into stories.
Canadian
Of or from Canada. Jane Chantal's computer can "find new Canadian Geese to rise from the lake in the morning and to make their turn-back when a furlong in the air to receive the shot."
Cardsharps
See Caravaggio's The Cardsharps. One of Denis Lollardy's masterwork forgeries at Lecco.
Carpenter, Joseph the
Saint Joseph, foster-father of Jesus. Appears as a spectral craftsman who built the Circular Stairway at Oosterend. Sea Captain Cornelius "knew him by the pipe that he had in his mouth. It was made with a Gouging Tool out of the very tag-end of a board. Those Galilean carpenters will not waste a thing." He repairs the steam calliopes for Wednesday at Oosterend.
Casement
Family surname of Laughter-Lynn and her father Fernand Kabouter Casement. "The Casement family motto was: The Best of Both Worlds"—referring to their dual Irish/Dutch-Friesian heritage.
Casement House at Oosterend
Laughter-Lynn's sea-house on Terschelling Island, described as "one of the Seven Wonders of the World." Features the Circular Stairway, the Sky Studio, and cellars that descend to the drowned-man realm beneath the sea.
Casement, Fernand Kabouter
Laughter-Lynn's father. Dutch-Friesian, lives on Terschelling Island in Oosterend. His middle name "Kabouter" means "goblin" or "little person" in Dutch, connecting him to the fairy-folk tradition.
Casement, Laughter-Lynn
"Born twice, births sixteen years apart, uncanny hinge of the group's laughter." Emerged from a giant goose egg as a nubile young girl after spending 55 years (one day world-time) in a Shoga boarding school. "A North Sea person," she divides her time between Gaire Castle (Ireland) and Oosterend (Terschelling). Given her name for "the infectious laugh that she evinced before she was twelve hours old." Killed Saturday in the rock slide at Lecco. "Goodbye, Perpetua; every minute of it was fun" are Leo's last words, but they apply to Laughter-Lynn's spirit.
Casement, Lynn
Shortened form of Laughter-Lynn Casement. See Casement, Laughter-Lynn.
Castle Gaire
"Cannot be seen from any of the five streets that encircle it." Located in Lastoir de Gaire, an inner suburb of Dublin. Home of Countess Maude Grogley. Houses "the oldest world terminal in the world"—an 8th-century, non-instantaneous, "jerky" transport system. Gaire in Shelta means "Laughter." Also called Caislean Sciotail (Giggle Castle).
Castle in the German Alps
See Klavierschloss. Home of Gorgonius and Monika Pantera.
Castletown
One of the three south-shore port towns on the Isle of Man, along with Port Erin and Port Saint Mary. Has its own "giant kettle of Old Cow Stew" and two white mules (eternally at enmity with Port Erin's black mules). Mayor: the Honorable Sean McEnglish.
Castletown, McEnglish of
See McEnglish, Sean. Mayor of Castletown who demands hangings and leads bonfires.
Cat, Leonard the
See Leonardo the Great. Emphasizes his feline nature: "Leonard the Cat had bitten the whole" stomach out of John Barkley Towntower.
Cat, Leonardo the Great the Big
Leonardo among the "big cats." He admits: "I am a pretty big cat. And if necessary I can be rough on dogs of all sizes." But Hilary points out his sketchiness: "You are not satisfactory as panther, leopard, puma, tiger, lion, nor as any of the big cats at all. You simply have no reality as one of the big cats."
Cataline
Catalan language. One of Denis Lollardy's forgery languages: "Latin, Low Latin, Tuscan, Old French, Old Italian, Spanish, Cataline, Old High Dutch, Icelandic, Demotic Greek, Coptic, Arabic, Ladino."
Cedraei
Ancient region of Arabia. According to Alexander the Great's testimony: "In nearer Asia, everything south of the Cedraei region of Arabia was unreal." Marks the boundary between the "real" and "unreal" ancient world.
Cellars of Genesis
Title of a work by Paul (The Python) Pemmican, quoted in the novel's research-computer compilation. Concerns antediluvian matters and "the correlation of ancient chronology."
Changing of the Aeons
The cosmic transition driving the novel's plot. From Der Alpenriese's epigraph: "Now there is a particular danger to the world, for we come to the Changing of the Aeons again; and the Giants will be in the ascendancy for the aeon that is now beginning, or (we pray that this is not so) the aeon that is not beginning." The crisis of finding replacement Giants before the old ones die.
Chantal High-Queen
Jane Chantal Ardri's title after becoming the El-Khatar Giant. "Painting and writing at a slab table"—she becomes a Scribbling Giant who can create reality through art.
Chanteclaire
See Jane Chanteclaire. One of the Ardri children, computer-named. Part of the naming sequence: "Jane Chanteclaire, Marie Rieuse, Anne Auclaire."
Charlemagne Cycle
The body of medieval literature about Charlemagne. Roderick Outreach argues it is fictional: "only a tall tale written by the Giant Atrox." See Charlemagne Episode.
Charlemagne Episode
The entire Carolingian era, which Roderick Outreach claims is invented: "The Charlemagne Episode fits illy into European history... contemporaries of Charlemagne never heard of him. Tear the whole Charlemagne Episode out of European history and it leaves no hole at all." One of many historical periods the novel suggests were written into existence by Scribbling Giants.
Charleroi
Solomon Izzersted's New York agent. "Buy it, Charleroi, buy it!" Solomon commands. Charleroi purchases a bankrupt New York publishing company for Solomon's promotional schemes: "Things can't get too lavish for me!"
Charles Fort
American anomalist and author (1874–1932). Summoned at the Saturday seance by Jane Chantal's incantation. "Charles Fort, or his evocation or ghost, reached up and scratched" his head. Explains the Fortean Universe ("No, I didn't create a universe, I discovered one"), the 109-year locusts, and the interior of atoms. Born in the Bronx: "Jews, Irish, Italians, Blacks, and Germans coexisted with each other" there.
Charles Fort in America
Denis Lollardy claims: "In the twentieth century I projected Charles Fort in America"—suggesting Fort was one of Denis's pantographic projections.
Charley
Informal name for Charles Fort. See Charles Fort.
Charley Fort
See Charles Fort. From the incantation: "Abra dabra ookie ort / Come and visit, Charley Fort."
Chestertonian
In the manner of G.K. Chesterton (1874–1936). Used to describe certain "talismanic verses" in the novel—apt given Lafferty's acknowledged debt to Chesterton's paradoxical Catholic imagination and love of paradox.
Chian
Wine from the Greek island of Chios. Gorgonius lists it among his favorites: "the Clazomenian, the Chian, the Lesbos which Horace called Innocent Wine but he lied when he so called it."
China Seas Charley Wong
One of the colorfully named Ocean lottery winners: "Mediterranean Susie Swing, China Seas Charley Wong, Caesar Oceano, Thousand-Fathom Thiessen." The names were chosen by "a Computer with perhaps a touch of drollery."
Chinaman
The Chinese seaman who arrives at Evenrood Manor "looking as if he had been walking for several hours, possibly from Brighton." Bears news of Atrox's death and the Hsiang Giant's desire for a replacement.
Chinese
Of or from China. "A Chinese seaman came to them" at Evenrood Manor to offer Drusilla the Hsiang Giant position.
Chorasmii and Massagetae
Ancient Central Asian peoples/regions. According to Alexander the Great: "In middle Asia, everything north of the Chorasmii and Massagetae regions was unreal (the desert border and limit again)." Marks another boundary of the "real" ancient world.
Christ
Jesus Christ. Referenced in the Armenian Gospel of the Childhood of Jesus Christ (forged by Denis) and the Laughing Christ of Creophylus. Denis claims: "I buried him alive, at his request"—one of his more startling assertions.
Christ of Creopas
Variant of Christ of Creophylus. See Laughing Christ of Creophylus.
Christ of Creophylus
See Laughing Christ of Creophylus. Denis Lollardy's greatest work, "which he had done only short months ago."
Christian Roman Emperor
Philip the Arab (r. 244–249 AD), "the first Christian Roman Emperor," who "had a lion at his court that was famous for its discourses." The lion was believed to be "an angel unaware."
Church
The Catholic Church. Saint Faunus was "canonized by the Church as Saint Faunus the patron of merriment, and I am still honored that way on the local calendar."
Cigar Store Indian
Subject of one of Denis Lollardy's exquisite forgeries: "Mockman's splintering Cigar Store Indian." Listed among the "exquisite fakeries" at the Lecco estate.
Cipriano
Italian flutist from Lecco. His surname is Settiflauti ("Seven Flutes"). When asked which instrument, he replies: "Flutes, and seven of them." He and six friends perform Saturday at Lecco for Seven Flutes: "Was there ever a day when things were so exactly right!"
Classical
Classical Greek language. Hieronymous notes that Demotic Greek "is much easier than the Classical which is the reason it became the universal language in the Hellenistic World where the Classical couldn't make a dent."
Clazomenian
Wine from Clazomenae (ancient Greek city in Asia Minor). Listed by Gorgonius among his favorite ancient wines: "the wonderful red Pramnian, the Clazomenian, the Chian, the Lesbos."
Coconut-Island Pat Silber
One of the Ocean lottery winners, listed with "Blue-Fish Harry Miller, Coconut-Island Pat Silber, Dead-Calm Doremus Pacifica, and nine hundred and ninety-one other names."
Colliers Magazine
American magazine (1888–1957). Charles Fort says: "I tried to sell it to Colliers Magazine, but they wouldn't touch it. They said that my reputation was against me." Refers to his journal from inside an atom.
Colonel Ruppert
Jacob Ruppert (1867–1939), owner of the New York Yankees and Ruppert Brewery. Charles Fort asks for "Ruppert beer" but is told "that beer has not been made for a long time. Colonel Ruppert has been dead for a long time." Fort replies: "I see the Colonel now and then... and he doesn't know whether his New York Yankees team is still in existence or not."
Commercial Fisherman's License
Permit required to fish commercially in Oklahoma. Hilary Ardri "did not have a Commercial Fisherman's License to operate on Lake Tenkiller nor on any other lake, stream, river, pond, or reservoir in Oklahoma." Yet his computer-run fish business thrives—proof the world is unreal.
Commercial Fisherman's Licenses
"Quite rare and very hard to obtain. The only really good way to get such a license was to be born with it." Those who have them rarely fish since "there were no longer any fish to be caught" in Oklahoma waters.
Company
See Strange Cargoes Worldwide Shippers Company. "Which you two now own"—referring to Caesar Oceano and Leonardo the Great.
Compelle ut Intrare
Latin: "Compel them to come in" (Luke 14:23). One of the Latin tags Denis Lollardy can forge. Jane Chantal suspects him: "Illo Tempore or Vir Autem Quidem or Et Compelle ut Intrare? Everybody thinks that the Pope wrote them. I think you did."
Complete Rewriting of Human Biology, A
Work by Hieronymous Talking-Crow concerning the Shoga: "The very fact that Shoga do sometimes mate and reproduce in this larva state, and that they produce apparently normal human infants, necessitates a complete rewriting of human biology."
Computer
Referenced in Intimations of Immortality in Early Computer Science by Diogenes Pontifex. Also: the Ardri computers (Hilary's fish-business computer and Jane Chantal's Joyeuse Vice-Reine), each inhabited by sprites.
Constabulary
Police force. Sandra Ott, new Giantess, howls: "Call the Constabulary, call the Police, call the Yard." Drusilla tells her to simply write it: "Oh, write in your journal that they are already called and already here."
Constabulary, Call the
See Constabulary.
Constantinople
Ancient city (now Istanbul). Denis Lollardy forges in "Ladino (the tongue of the Jews of Constantinople)."
Convince Me
Mary Brandy's response to the Morning Giant's proposal: "Tell me more, good Giant. Convince me. I want to be convinced." Part of the courtship/recruitment of new giants.
Cooling
Describes Atrox's corpse after his resurrection into flesh: "Cooling and dead flesh, but not quite cold yet. Strange." The eerie state between life and death that characterizes the novel's liminal moments.
Copley Watson and the Shark
Painting by John Singleton Copley (1778). One of Denis Lollardy's masterwork forgeries: "the Goya Third of May 1808; the Copley Watson and the Shark; the Gainsborough Robert Andrews and His Wife."
Coptic
Egyptian Christian language. One of Denis Lollardy's forgery languages: "Demotic Greek, Coptic, Arabic, Ladino."
Copyright
"Designs and Patents Act 1988." Publishing information in the novel's front matter.
Corn
Slang for something corny or hokey. Solomon teases Denis: "You are the King of Corn now, for having the lamps"—referring to Denis's ownership of Aladdin's Original Lamp.
Cornelius
Ship Captain Cornelius, Laughter-Lynn's "second drowned husband." A house ghost at the Oosterend sea-house. Present when Saint Joseph built the Circular Stairway: "It was Saint Joseph who did it. I knew him by the pipe that he had in his mouth." Laughter-Lynn consults his ghost for judgement.
Coronation Day of the Giant Sequence
Part of Gorgonius Pantera's Giant Suite. "They're playing the Coronation Day of the Giant Sequence from my great Giant Suite now. In all modesty, I love it!" Accompanies Solomon's self-promotion as the Riant Giant.
Countess
Countess Maude Grogley, "a sometimes-drinking lady" who maintains Gaire Castle. See Countess Maude Grogley.
Countries and the United States
"The Low Countries and the United States"—places where Countess Maude Grogley worked as a foreign correspondent before her marriage.
Country Estate of Drusilla Evenrood in East Sussex
Evenrood Manor. "They all went to the Country Estate of Drusilla Evenrood in East Sussex. The Thursday dawn was just beginning to whiten the eastern sky." Setting for Chapter 7.
Courbet's The Stone Breakers
Painting by Gustave Courbet (1849, destroyed 1945). One of Denis Lollardy's masterwork forgeries: "Bouguereau's Youth; Courbet's The Stone Breakers; so many of the better-than-the-originals forgeries."
Creophylus
Supposed ancient Greek sculptor of the Laughing Christ statue. Atrox denies being Creophylus: "No. I am no Creophylus, no sculptor. The Christ was carved by another. And that you only imagined you had carved the statue." The attribution is mysterious—possibly another Denis Lollardy creation.
D
Dame Meara
Title of address for Mary Brandy Manx, Mayor of Port Saint Mary. Sean McEnglish threatens: "Or perhaps, Dame Meara, we will hang you also just to let you be an example to yourself."
Dame of the Realm
British honorific. Sandra Ott is described as "Dame of the Realm and possessor of other honors and titles." Leo asks her if she would recognize Atrox—and then reveals he has just walked through the door.
Daniel Delany
Irish scientist quoted in the Dublin Docket. Self-describes as "the renowned Daniel Delany, top scientist and scholar, jabbering such nonsense as this in print." Warns that when survival waters are "more than arse-deep, forget your science! Latch onto something" else. Leo Parisi notes drily: "In all truth, that Daniel Delany was never really a top scientist."
Danish and the English
The Danish and English invasions of Ireland. Leo notes that the modern world terminal at Gaire Castle "dates from the eighth century, precedes both the Danish and the English invasions." Laughter-Lynn agrees it is "older than either of those vulgarities."
Danube North of Thrace
Geographical boundary of the ancient "real" world. According to Alexander the Great: "In Europe everything across the Danube North of Thrace was unreal."
Darwinians
Followers of Darwin's evolutionary theory. The Ifrit explains: "The Darwinians have for a long time been searching for missing links between monkey-apes and humans, which they believe will prove their notions true. We Ifrits are the real 'missing links' between monkey-apes and humans, and we prove the strange notions false."
Daughter of Gorgonius
Perpetua Parisi. See Parisi, Perpetua. "The Seventh Daughter of Gorgonius."
Day Star
Venus, the morning star. From the Introit of Saint Faunus's mass: "In the Laughter of the Saints, before the Day Star, I begot thee." Echoes Psalm 110:3 in the Vulgate.
Dead-Calm Doremus Pacifica
One of the colorfully named Ocean lottery winners: "Blue-Fish Harry Miller, Coconut-Island Pat Silber, Dead-Calm Doremus Pacifica, and nine hundred and ninety-one other names."
Delaney in the Dublin Docket
See Daniel Delany. His article is read aloud by the Mayor of Port Erin.
Delany
See Daniel Delany. "Read out loud" to the citizens of the three towns.
Demiourgikos Pneuma Apatelos
Greek: "Spirit of Creative Fraud" or "Creative Deceit." Denis Lollardy's explanation for his forgery genius: "It is not really myself but the Demiourgikos Pneuma Apatelos, the Spirit of Creative Fraud, who does my creative forging. I am always seized by this rapture, and then I create."
Demotic Greek
Popular Greek of the Alexandrine period, as opposed to Classical Greek. One of Denis Lollardy's forgery languages. Hieronymous notes it is "much easier than the Classical which is the reason it became the universal language in the Hellenistic World."
Denis Lollardy at Lecco
Denis at his estate in Lombardy. See Lollardy, Denis and Lecco.
Denis Lollardy's
Possessive form. "The greatest of Denis Lollardy's forgeries, of course, was his Laughing Christ of Creophylus."
Designs and Patents Act 1988
British copyright law referenced in the novel's publication information.
Diogenes Pontifex
Author of Intimations of Immortality in Early Computer Science, quoted in the novel. The passage distinguishes between the living and the dead: "That is the main difference between them."
Dismiss
"Dismiss your companion now if you wish, Lector. If you have survived, then you have survived the most horrible part of the symbiotic account." The narrator's address to the reader after describing Solomon Izzersted's grotesque origin.
Do Futures
Solomon Izzersted's business motto. His final sign reads: "SOLOMON IZZERSTED THE PATAGONIAN GIANT. I DO FUTURES." Suggests both fortune-telling and futures trading—fitting for the son of the Trickster Angel.
Docket
See Dublin Docket and Dublin Morning Docket.
Domdaniel Castle
Undersea castle "whence the Ocean is ruled." "The Nine Hundred Governors of the Ocean, meeting in deep Domdaniel Castle," decided to use a lottery to distribute ocean wealth. From Arabic folklore—the legendary underwater hall of evil magicians.
Donohoe
Dublin grogshop owner with a "saw voice." Recognizes John Barkley Towntower from his music-hall act: "I remember John Barkley Towntower there and his talking belly-button. They did their act at the Caladium Music Hall up the street." Gives the Group drinks while they wait for Tuesday to arrive in "twenty-two minutes... and worth every penny of it."
Donohoe's Groggery
Dublin drinking establishment run by the saw-voiced Donohoe. Located in the built-over castle-keep of Gaire Castle, which "cannot be seen from any of the five streets that encircle it."
Doubting Castle
From Bunyan's Pilgrim's Progress—the castle of Giant Despair. "The bleak refusal 'We will not serve' is not the right answer. And Giant Despair who lives in Doubting Castle is not the right answer." Used to contrast false despair with the true calling to be a Giant.
Dream, Beckman's The
Painting by Max Beckmann. One of Denis Lollardy's masterwork forgeries: "Bosch's The Ship of Fools; Honore's David and Goliath; Beckman's The Dream; Chagall's I And The Village."
Drexler
Author quoted on the nature of great fortunes: "The absolute anonymity, irresponsibility, and ruthlessness of a near majority of the great fortunes is as shocking as anything that can be imagined." The Ifrit notes Drexler "wrote correctly from the human viewpoint"—many great fortunes are held by invisible Ifrits.
Drowned Man Shoal
Level of Laughter-Lynn's Oosterend sea-house, "perhaps three levels below the booming sea." Inhabited by drowned men and women who beg visitors: "Stay and talk with us for a while. Nobody ever stops to talk with us anymore."
Drusilla and Laughter-Lynn
See Evenrood, Drusilla and Casement, Laughter-Lynn. Two of the female members of the Group of Twelve.
Drusilla and Mary Brandy and Jane Chantal
Three women of the Group who become Scribbling Giants: Drusilla (Hsiang), Mary Brandy (Illacrove), Jane Chantal (El-Khatar).
Drusilla's Manor
"House in Sussex, England." Evenrood Manor. Jane Galatea works to plague the false "casual English Intellectual" giants there: "I'm giving them boils now, and turning their drinking water into blood."
Dublin
Capital of Ireland. "Oh Baile Atha Cliath of the Irish! Oh Dublin of the Danes!" Location of Gaire Castle in "the inner suburb of Lastoir de Gaire." Also home to Dunsink Observatory and the Dublin Docket newspaper.
Dublin Docket
Irish newspaper. Contains articles by scientists Hennessee, Delaney, and Monroney about the world crisis. "Rather discouraging" in its assessment. Read aloud by the mayors of the three Isle of Man towns during their Old Cow Stew breakfast.
Dublin in the Gaire Castle
Laughter-Lynn "was born in Dublin in the Gaire Castle of her mother." The castle is located in the inner suburb of Lastoir de Gaire.
Dublin Morning Docket
Morning edition of the Dublin Docket. Delivered to Port Saint Mary by a mysterious man in a fast jolly-boat: "The regular boat that usually brings the Dublin Morning Docket won't be here for three hours yet." Contains articles about the dire situation of the world.
Dunsink Observatory in Dublin
Irish astronomical observatory. One of the institutions from which the casual English Intellectuals hail: "the Royal Observatory at Edinburgh, Dunsink Observatory in Dublin, the University Observatory at Oxford."
Dürer Pinakothek-Munich Self-Portrait
Self-portrait by Albrecht Dürer (1500), housed in the Alte Pinakothek, Munich. One of Denis Lollardy's masterwork forgeries: "There were the Durer Pinakothek-Munich Self-Portrait; the Goya Third of May 1808."
Dutch
Of or from the Netherlands. Laughter-Lynn's father is Dutch-Friesian. Countess Maude speculates her daughter missed "total reality" due to "having a Dutch father."
Dutch-Friesian
Of the Dutch-Friesian Islands (Wadden Islands). Laughter-Lynn's father lives "on the Dutch-Friesian Island of Terschelling in the Town of Oosterend." Also: "a big Dutch-Friesian breakfast"—"Eat a banging-big Dutch breakfast early in the morning, and be soggy all day."
E
Eagle
See Alpenadler. The Alpine Eagle whose sinistral wing-bone must be torn out to fashion a key: "wake Wife Number Three from death again" to make it.
Early Childhood
Leo Parisi "did give Intimations of Transcendent Intellect in Early Childhood. He did come into the world trailing clouds of glory when he came." Echoes Wordsworth's "Intimations of Immortality."
Earth and Ocean and Sunshine
One of Laughter-Lynn Casement's great paintings, part of her "Earth and Ocean" sequence: "Earth and Ocean and Sunshine, Earth and Ocean and Mist, Earth and Ocean and Sea-and-Storm-Wrack, Earth and Ocean and People, Earth and Ocean and Drowned People and a hundred others."
Earthquakes and the Land-Slides
Natural disasters commanded by the killer giants. During the Saturday night catastrophe at Lecco: "Who is this that even the Earthquakes and the Land-Slides obey him?" Echoes Christ stilling the storm (Mark 4:41).
East of Joy Garden
Location of the Eighth Day of the Week. "We know that the Eighth Day of the Week is East of Joy Garden, and there is the warden of Joy Garden now!" The Warden is the Archangel Isradel with the Flaming Sword—connecting to Eden's eastern gate.
East of Laughter
The novel's title. Derives from the Dublin suburb Lastoir de Gaire, "which might be Englished as East Laughter but more correctly as East of Laughter." The Group is "marooned East of Reality, and you are questing to find your way back to Reality. So you have come to the Castle originally named East of Laughter." Parallels "East of Eden"—Gaire (Laughter) being the Little People's Eden.
East Sussex
English county. Location of Drusilla Evenrood's manor house. "On the new day today, Mary Brandy"—Thursday dawns over East Sussex as the Group arrives at Evenrood Manor.
East Sussex Giant
One of the regional giants. "The East Sussex Giant was rumored to have died when I was a little girl," Drusilla recalls, "but I believe I remember the spot we decided was his grave." Audrey insists: "There's only one giant... He says he uses different names when he goes to different towns."
East Sussex Lady
Drusilla Evenrood's descriptor in the novel's character list: "Drusilla Evenrood, an East Sussex Lady."
East Sussex to the Estate of Drusilla
The Group's Thursday destination. See Evenrood Manor.
Eden Legend
The Little People had "their own version of the Eden Legend." A present-day Lamia told Leo Parisi that "the founding and ornamentation of their own Eden (its name was Gaire) and their being driven out from it, all happened eleven years before the establishment and the exiling from the human Eden." Eden in Hebrew means "delight"; Gaire in Shelta means "Laughter."
Edinburgh
Scottish capital. The casual English Intellectuals come from "the Royal Observatory at Edinburgh, Dunsink Observatory in Dublin, the University Observatory at Oxford."
Egypt
Ancient land. Jane Galatea plagues the false giants with "the ten plagues of Egypt if they don't get out of the world-writing business." Also: according to Alexander, "everything beyond three days march south of Thebes in Egypt was unreal."
El-Khatar Giant
One of the Seven Scribbling Giants, stationed in Arabia/the Middle East. "The El-Khatar Giant, whom I serve, says that he is weary and wishes to die." Jane Chantal eagerly accepts: "Yes, all right, I will, I'll be glad to be his replacement"—surprising the messenger who expected reluctance. Jane Chantal High-Queen becomes his successor.
Elizabethan Dramas and Dostoyevsky Novels
Among Denis Lollardy's forgeries: "And the Elizabethan Dramas and Dostoyevsky Novels. Aye, and the forged checks, big ones, resounding ones." Denis understands that "when a check is large enough the borderline between the genuine and the forged disappears."
Emperor Barbarossa
See Barbarossa. Frederick I, "buried in a cavern sitting at a table with his red beard grown clear" through the table.
End of Rome
The fifth century collapse. "There were some amazing mechanisms made at the End of Rome, in the murky days of the fifth century, such things as have not been made since then even till today." Atrox Fabulinus was "a fifth century Irish Giant" who lived through this era.
England
Part of Great Britain. Evenrood Manor is located in East Sussex, England, "twenty-one miles from Scotland" (an exaggeration for comic effect—East Sussex is far from Scotland).
England and in Lowland
"Scotland and Ireland, in the Scandinavias and the Germanies"—part of the Sioga-Kobald Belt where Little People dwell.
English
Of or from England. The "casual English Intellectuals" and their "English women" who claim to be the new Scribbling Giants.
English and of the Twelve
"So far at variance"—tension between the casual English Intellectuals and the legitimate Group of Twelve.
English Garden
One of the themed gardens at Denis Lollardy's Lecco estate: "Italian Garden, Moravian Garden, Aragonese Garden, Armenian Garden, Persian Garden, Arabian Garden and Japanese Garden all in high style."
English Gardens
"Of his wonderful estate at Lecco." Gorgonius walks "in the Italian Gardens of the wonderful Lollardy Estate."
English Intellectual
Member of the "casual English Intellectuals" who claim giant-status. One "took exception" to the Group's legitimacy. See Casual English Intellectuals.
English Intellectual Roderick
Roderick Outreach, who "shouted" his claims about the Charlemagne Episode being fictional. See Outreach, Roderick.
English Intellectuals
See Casual English Intellectuals. Myrtle Mobley "quickly set forty-two more places at breakfast" for them.
Englishman
A man from England. Generic reference to the casual English Intellectuals.
Englishmen
Men from England. The casual English Intellectuals include both men and women.
Enniscorthy Chronicle
Irish newspaper from County Wexford. Contains a dialogue about the Sioga: "'I forget it, Milligan. Look it up, boy. 'Twill do you good, and then you'll remember it, as I do not.'" Reports on the Sioga digging through the earth to emerge in the Americas and Australias.
Epirus in Greece
Northwestern Greek region. Part of the Sioga-Kobald Belt: "Transylvania in the Balkans, Huesco in Spain, Epirus in Greece, Esh Sharqi in Syria, Nazanderan in Persia or Iran."
Epistle of Paul to the Hebrews
New Testament book. Atrox quotes it: "In the Epistle of Paul to the Hebrews are the words 'Forget not to entertain strangers, for some have thus entertained angels unaware.'" He notes an early Greek text that included "dogs or wilder beasts" as possible angel-forms, later stricken by a redactor.
Equator to the North Pole
Geographic reference indicating vast distances or scope.
Erasthenos of Patmos
Author of Of Wanton Giants, source of the Chapter 2 epigraph about giants with camel noses: "The trouble with giants is not their stealing and eating whole herds of cattle... They come with their long moist camel noses that can smell every detail and they learn every private thing about the people of a place."
Erin, Haggerty of Port
See Haggerty, Meara Timothy. Mayor of Port Erin who "chimed in" with demands for hangings.
Esh Sharqi in Syria
Syrian region. Part of the Sioga-Kobald Belt: "Epirus in Greece, Esh Sharqi in Syria, Nazanderan in Persia or Iran." Esh Sharqi means "the Eastern" in Arabic.
Estate at Lecco in Italy
Denis Lollardy's property in Lombardy. See Lecco. "And the Irish Garden was" among its many themed gardens.
Estate House at Lecco
See Estate at Lecco in Italy.
Europe
The continent. According to Alexander, "In Europe everything across the Danube North of Thrace was unreal." The "real" ancient world was a "small portion of Africa, Holy Ireland of course" and limited Mediterranean regions.
European
Of or from Europe. "European history"—the Charlemagne Episode "fits illy into European history."
Eveningish
Informal time designation. Hilary asks Mary Brandy what time it is: "Eveningish, Mary Brandy. Eveningish by Oklahoma Time, this evening. Have you been shot today, Mary Brandy?"
Evenrood
Family name of Drusilla, Penelope, and Audrey. See individual entries.
Evenrood Manor
Drusilla Evenrood's country estate "in East Sussex." Setting for Chapter 7 (Thursday). The casual English Intellectuals take it over and claim to be the new Scribbling Giants. Jane Galatea plagues them with boils and blood.
Evenrood Manor in East Sussex
See Evenrood Manor. "And we thought" it a safe haven, until the false giants arrived.
Evenrood Manor in East Sussex and the
Partial reference to Evenrood Manor's connection to other locations in the novel's geography.
Evenrood, Audrey
"Little girl" who puts flowers on Drusilla's grave and later helps Jane try to resurrect Atrox by describing him. Her aunt Penelope removes her from the manor when "some of the things that are happening" become too dangerous.
Evenrood, Drusilla
"East Sussex lady of Evenrood Manor." Member of the Group of Twelve. "A British person" and "biologist in a wider sense." Offered the Hsiang Giant position by a Chinese seaman; eventually accepts. Successor to the Hsiang Giant. Her voice "always had enough edge to it to cut through other voices."
Evenrood, Miss
Formal address for Drusilla Evenrood. Myrtle Mobley cries: "You gave me a horrible start, Miss Evenrood."
Evenrood, Penelope
"Sister of Drusilla." Removes Audrey from Evenrood Manor when danger mounts: "I do not like some of the things that are happening at your manor, Drusilla."
Ewigerjude-Tand
German: "Eternal Jew trinket" or "Wandering Jew toy." The Alpine Giant's dismissive name for Solomon Izzersted: "a bouncing comic Zappelphilipp, and Ewigerjude-Tand, a jumping toy to amuse the old giant in his dying hours." Solomon retorts: "Before the morning stars sang together I was already wound up."
Extraordinaries
Exceptional beings—giants, fauns, and the like. "The world would never make it without its extraordinary citizens. When the numbers of the Extraordinaries is diminished only by several of them, and only for several days, the difference is manifest." The novel's crisis stems from too many Extraordinaries dying at once.
F
Fabulinian
In the manner of Atrox Fabulinus. A "Fabulinian" treatment of history prepares the reader for the fantastic: "which history, being Fabulinian in its treatment, prepared him for the event"—namely, a nubile young girl emerging from a giant goose egg.
Fabulinus
See Atrox Fabulinus. "The Roman Rabelais, once broke off the account of his hero Raphaelus in the act of opening a giant goose egg to fry it in an iron skillet of six yards' span."
Fabulinus, Atrox
"Roman Rabelais, scribbling giant, author" of the world's history. See Atrox Fabulinus.
Falernum
Celebrated ancient Roman wine from Campania. Gorgonius's first love: "I love the Falernum, the Vina Horna, Fugacia, Surrentine, Aminean."
Fathach
Irish/sea goblin word for "giant." Tuama no Fathach means "Giant's Tomb" in sea goblin language—the tomb hollowed out in the granite slab at Oosterend where Atrox is buried.
Father Joseph Kirkpatrick
Scottish priest who "came originally from the nearby Scottish Coast." Drinks brandy with Mary Brandy after John Barkley Towntower's burial. Explains "These Apprehensions, which are sometimes known as the Nine Day Wonders, are frequent in history or at least in shadow-history."
Faunus
See Saint Faunus. Ancient Roman deity of wild nature; in the novel, a canonized faun. "And nothing untoward can happen to you now," Gorgonius tells him, but Faunus clarifies he is safely dead only in one form—his faun form can still be terminated.
Flat Earth
See Flat Earth Society. Saint Brandon explains he believed not in a flat earth but "the lens-shaped earth"—a real, limited disc floating on a less-real spherical world.
Flat Earth Society
Organization in the United States that has made Saint Brandon "the patron saint of the Flat Earth Society." Hieronymous Talking-Crow notes: "That doesn't seem fair. You who have travelled so far, you never believed in the Flat Earth, did you?"
Flattery
Solomon asks to use Gorgonius's Giant Suite. "Flattery will get you nowhere, Solomon," Gorgonius replies, "but plain old-fashioned flim-flam will. Sure you can use them."
Floridas and the Mexicos and the Antilles
Regions where ancient Irish settlers founded communities. "They founded especially in Newfoundland and Nova Scotia, in the Floridas and the Mexicos and the Antilles, and in Hi Brasil. And everywhere that they set up settlements and fishermen's villages they found that a Kabouter was already there running a store."
Flutes
Instrument of Cipriano Settiflauti and his six friends. See Saturday at Lecco for Seven Flutes.
Foinse na n'Óg
Irish: "Fountain of Youth." A "very small-throated fountain" in the Irish Gardens of the Lollardy Estate. "For one to receive its gift one must be totally immersed in its full depths. But no person could possibly be immersed into the depths of that small-throated fountain, no person who was not as small as a—" Solomon, baseball-sized, plunges in. Later, Countess Maude changes into a snake to fit through the narrow throat, and emerges with "her youth renewed."
Folletti
Italian: "sprites" or "hobgoblins." Timore belongs to "the Folletti people, to the Magi people." Leo Parisi explains: "Timore here... they both belong to the hobgoblin people, to the gnomes, the eldritch-elves, the puka people. They believe all sorts of strange things. They have no grasp on reality." Yet Timore's prophecies of terremoti e sdruccioli (earthquakes and landslides) prove accurate.
Forger, Denis the
See Lollardy, Denis. Mayor Haggerty addresses him: "Oh, just for the everlasting fun of it, Denis the Forger." Denis's shadow is "his brother who was no brother of his"—"the Forger of the Forger" who hawks forgeries on the streets of Lecco at night.
Form
Shape-shifting capability. Countess Maude "changed back into her Countess Form, and by the sparkle on her she left no doubt" her youth was renewed. The Sioga and other Little People have multiple forms.
Fort
See Charles Fort. "Or his evocation or ghost, reached up" and scratched his head at the seance.
Fortean Universe
Charles Fort's cosmology. "I didn't create a universe, I discovered one. I named it the Fortean Universe when I found that it was unnamed." In this universe, "the sky could be as high as twenty-seven miles and as low as seven feet," and "people are almost small enough and the atoms are almost big enough" for personal visits to atomic interiors. The Fortean Universe "coexisted with other universes in the same parts of space."
France
European nation. Gorgonius wonders about "some of the modern wines of Hungary or France or California." Also: Future France, where Denis projected Rabelais in the sixteenth century.
French
Of or from France. Perpetua sets out "French journals that she strewed about the breakfast table" to predict Leo's behavior through behavioristic logic.
French Garden
One of the themed gardens at Denis Lollardy's Lecco estate. "An Arabian sort of man came up to Jane Chantal as she walked in her new sorrow in the French Garden." Listed with "English Garden, Italian Garden, Moravian Garden, Aragonese Garden, Armenian Garden, Persian Garden, Arabian Garden, and Japanese Garden all in high style."
Fugacia
Ancient wine variety. One of Gorgonius's favorites: "the Falernum, the Vina Horna, Fugacia, Surrentine, Aminean."
Future France
France of the sixteenth century, as seen from Atrox's fifth-century perspective. "I did create a character named Rabelais and I did set him to writing in Future France in the sixteenth century. But this Rabelais was perverse. Instead of writing about his own day, he turned backwards to me and wrote about myself and my father and our family of giants."
Future, Hybridizing the
See On Hybridizing The Future, And The Pitfalls of It.
G
Gaire
Irish/Shelta: "Laughter." The name of the Little People's Eden, established "eleven years before the establishment and the exiling from the human Eden." "Gaire in Shelta, the language of the Tinkers as well as of the Little People, meant Laughter so they are surely aspects of the same place" as Eden (Hebrew: "delight").
Gaire Castle
"Castle rendezvous and running set piece." Located in Lastoir de Gaire, Dublin. Home of Countess Maude Grogley. "Cannot be seen from any of the five streets that encircle it, nor from the air above it." Houses "the oldest world terminal in the world" dating from the eighth century—non-instantaneous and "jerky" but functional. Also called East of Laughter Castle or Caislean Sciotail (Giggle Castle). Setting for Chapter 5 (Tuesday).
Gaire Castle in Ireland
Laughter-Lynn lives "half of every year in Gaire Castle in Ireland and half of every year with her father" on Terschelling Island.
Gaire in Shelta
See Gaire. "The language of the Tinkers as well as of the Little People."
Gaire Tramway
Dublin tram line. "The Gaire Tramway there is still running, and it stops at midnight." Serves as a temporal marker for the Group's arrival—if the tramway is running, it's still Monday.
Galatea
See Jane Galatea. The resurrected Jane Chantal's name for herself: "My name is Jane Galatea." Like Pygmalion's statue brought to life, she is newly created and discovering herself through "Who am I?" games.
Galilean
Of or from Galilee. "Those Galilean carpenters will not waste a thing"—referring to Saint Joseph who built the Circular Stairway. They "smoke a mixture of nine parts aromatic redwood sawdust and one part of strong shag tobacco."
Galilee
Region of ancient Israel. The steam calliopes for Wednesday at Oosterend required repairs by "Saint Joseph the Carpenter from Galilee arriving."
Garden
See Joy Garden. "The Eighth Day of the Week is East of Joy Garden, and there is the warden of Joy Garden now!"
Gardens of the Lollardy Estate
"One very" extensive collection of themed gardens at Lecco: French, English, Italian, Moravian, Aragonese, Armenian, Persian, Arabian, Japanese, and Irish. The Irish Garden contains the Foinse na n'Óg (Fountain of Youth).
Genies
"Denizens of the Ancient Arabian Empire of the low skies." Charles Fort lists them among his beloved anomalies: "Ifrits, Jinns, Genies... sea stallions, flying horses, birds that can gulp down elephants in a single gulp... Genies imprisoned in bottles for thousands of years."
Genii
"And other principalities and powers." Plural of genius in its original sense of guardian spirits.
German Alps
Mountain range. Location of Klavierschloss, home of Gorgonius "and his wife Monika Pantera." Also site of the Alpine Giant's cave.
Germanies and Scandinavias of Europe
Part of the Sioga-Kobald Belt: "in England and in Lowland Scotland and Ireland, in the Scandinavias and the Germanies."
Germans
People of Germany. Charles Fort notes the Bronx contained universes where "Jews, Irish, Italians, Blacks, and Germans coexisted with each other."
Germans and Italians
Denis Lollardy "forged music masterworks and operas of all the great Germans and Italians."
Ghees
Ge'ez, the classical Ethiopian language. One of Denis Lollardy's forgery languages: "Ladino (the tongue of the Jews of Constantinople), Ghees, Amharic, Middle Armenian."
Giant, Atrox the
See Atrox Fabulinus. Leo asks Sandra Ott: "Would you recognize Atrox the Giant if he walked through that door right now?"
Giant, Fabulinus the
See Atrox Fabulinus. "Roman Rabelais, sitting at a huge table" writing the world.
Giantess
Female giant. Sandra Ott becomes one: "Sandra Ott, New Giantess, howled."
Giants and Sioga
The two supernatural races most concerned with the novel's crisis. "What need have they for such" ordinary things as human affairs.
Giants and with Sioga
See Giants and Sioga.
Giants on the Isle of Man
"Island setting, maritime limen." The Isle of Man serves as a threshold space where giants and humans interact freely—setting for Chapter 8 (Friday) and Chapter 9 (Saturday).
Giant's Grave
Location in East Sussex. Drusilla tells Audrey: "Here is the Giant's Grave on this ridge." Audrey notes: "That has always been the Wolf Den, but nobody uses it now." Drusilla explains: "Wolves often dig graves for giants, and then they direct the people away from them so the giants won't be disturbed."
Giant's Tomb
See Tuama no Fathach. Granite slab at Oosterend, "in sea goblin language" called the Giant's Tomb. Atrox is buried there "three levels below the booming sea."
Gigantem
Latin: "Giant" (accusative). From the Ifrit's cry: "Habemus Gigantem, We Have a Giant"—echoing the papal election announcement.
Gioia
See Gioia di Sotto La Montagna. Italian: "Joy."
Gioia di Sotto
See Gioia di Sotto La Montagna.
Gioia di Sotto La Montagna
Italian: "Joy Under the Mountain." Old woman of the Lecco neighborhood who belongs to the hobgoblin people. Brings the nine-gallon cup for Atrox's wine. Warns the Group: "When Atrox is both sulky and furious, somebody always dies in a bloody scandal." Her prophecies prove accurate.
Gioioso Lecco
Italian: "Merry Lecco." Saint Faunus recalls: "Gioioso Lecco, Merry Lecco, was the name given to this region then, and I was a part of the merriment. Well, there was never a happier earth spirit than I was."
God
The Creator. Referenced throughout in various contexts: "God is jealous of that one, Denis" (of his Pine Tree forgery); the giants' "writing" of the world in cooperation with divine creation.
God and Mary
"Help us"—Irish exclamation of distress.
Golden Panther Leonardo the Great
See Leonardo the Great. "Had his own" distinctive concerns and melancholies.
Golden, Leonardo the Great the
See Leonardo the Great. "Panther said" his piece about the world's troubles.
Gollancz
British publisher. "eBook Copyright © 1988 by R" A. Lafferty. Victor Gollancz Ltd published East of Laughter.
Goodbye
Leo Parisi's last words before the rock-slide buries him: "Goodbye, Perpetua; every minute of it was fun." Addressed to his sister as he, Laughter-Lynn, and Saint Faunus are killed.
Goose Egg
The giant goose egg from which Laughter-Lynn Casement emerged as "a nubile young girl"—sixteen years after her actual birth. "How'd I get into this big goose egg anyhow?" she asks. Connection to her Kabouter blood and time spent in a Shoga boarding school. Also: Laughter-Lynn's painting series The World on the Inside of a Goose-Egg.
Gorgolanza
Charles Fort's affectionate nickname for Gorgonius Pantera: "No, Gorgolanza, I didn't create a universe, I discovered one."
Gorgonius
See Pantera, Gorgonius.
Gorgonius and Denis
"And Caesar were all strong diggers" during the search for buried survivors.
Gorgonius and Monika
"Leo and Perpetua, Drusilla and" others—the paired members of the Group.
Gorgonius Pantera and Jane Chantal
Two of the Group who become Scribbling Giants—Gorgonius succeeds the Alpine Giant, Jane Chantal the El-Khatar.
Gothic Kinglet
Flavius Placidius Valentinianus, a "Pannonian Gothic Kinglet" who purchased Atrox as a slave. "Delighted, and he told Atrox to sit down and write the history of the world." When Atrox said the history until now had been written, the Kinglet asked: "From the beginning of the world until doomsday?" and set him to writing the future.
Gouging Tool
Woodworking implement. Saint Joseph's pipe "was made with a Gouging Tool out of the very tag-end of a board. Those Galilean carpenters will not waste a thing."
Governors of the Ocean
"The Nine Hundred Governors of the Ocean, meeting in deep Domdaniel Castle whence the Ocean is ruled, decided to use a lottery to distribute somehow the scandalous unclaimed wealth of the Ocean."
Goya Third of May 1808
Painting by Francisco Goya (1814). One of Denis Lollardy's masterwork forgeries: "the Durer Pinakothek-Munich Self-Portrait; the Goya Third of May 1808; the Copley Watson and the Shark."
Grand Rome
The glorious Rome of legend. Sandra Ott explains the mythos: "when fallen Rome had become squalid and ruined and overgrown, many of the people believed that the memory of a Grand Rome was not based on any reality, that it was based entirely on a fable that the Giant Atrox wrote."
Great, Alexander the
See Alexander the Great.
Great, Gorgonius the
"Somewhat overblown and musical-comedyish"—Gorgonius avoids this title though entitled to it as husband of Princess Monika.
Great, Leonardo the
See Leonardo the Great. "Strangely indwelt Golden Panther."
Great, Leonardo the (hanging)
"Hanging on his gibbet-gallows"—Leonardo's temporary execution on the Isle of Man before his resurrection.
Great, Monika the
"But only to very close personal friends, less than two of them in the world." Monika signs her letters with this title only to intimates.
Greek
The Greek language. Atrox has "an early Greek text in which the wording was 'Forget not to entertain strangers whether men or giants or waifs or even dogs or wilder beasts.'"
Greek of the Alexandrine
Demotic Greek of the "Alexandrine period"—the popular Greek that spread through the Hellenistic world. See Demotic Greek.
Greek Tuttleburg
See Jimmy the Greek Tuttleburg. "Wrote: Some of the very largest fortunes in the world have owners whom I can only describe as 'Lords of Smoke'"—referring to Ifrits.
Greeks and Phoenicians
"Sailed to the Americas" in ancient times, founding early settlements.
Green Pasture Counselling Service
Leonardo the Great's charitable enterprise. "He arranged it so that he would be a soothing voice speaking out of the soft darkness to the sound of gently falling waters. And he did ease many tired and troubled souls, but he seemed not to ease his own."
Green Tree
Title of a work by Auctore: "In A Green Tree." Precedes the explanation of the Eighth Day of the Week: "After Sunday in the regular sequence, the next day is Monday. But in special cases for special persons, Sunday is followed by the Eighth Day of the Week."
Gregory
See Gregory O'Growley.
Gregory O'Growley
"The Political Opposition to Mary Brandy Manx in Port Saint Mary." Lawyer who helps John Barkley Towntower sign papers. Notes the world crisis: "The world is dying of anemia, you know, for lack of input." Also suggests "penny-whistles" for Friday at Port Saint Mary for Three Penny-Whistles.
Grogley
Family name of Countess Maude and (by birth) Laughter-Lynn.
Grogley, Laughter-Lynn
Laughter-Lynn's maiden name before taking her father's surname Casement. See Casement, Laughter-Lynn.
Grogley, Maude
See Countess Maude Grogley. "Mother of Laughter-Lynn, aristocratic" Dublin lady, former foreign correspondent, owner of Gaire Castle. Can change into "a large and rather attractive gold-and-green snake" to fit through the Fountain of Youth.
Group of the Flexible Number Twelve
The novel's central protagonists. "These Fifteen persons are known as the Group of Twelve. Some of them are spares." The Group has "somehow generated at least fifteen shadows, persons, manifestations, or powers." See individual character entries.
H
Habemus
Latin: "We have." From Habemus Gigantem.
Habemus Gigantem
Latin: "We have a Giant." The Ifrit's proclamation when Solomon Izzersted becomes the new Top Giant: "Habemus Gigantem, We Have a Giant." Echoes the papal election announcement Habemus Papam. Marks the moment "everything from the magnetism and gravitation of the world to the efflux of Helium-4 was once more right with the world."
Haggerty of Port Erin
See Haggerty, Meara Timothy. "Port-town setting and civic hinge." Mayor of Port Erin who demands hangings and reads the Dublin Docket article by Delany.
Haggerty the Mayor of Port Erin
See Haggerty, Meara Timothy.
Haggerty, Meara Timothy
"Honorable Meara Timothy Haggerty," Mayor of Port Erin. "Chief howler" for the western crowd at Spanish Head. Rails at Mary Brandy: "It's about time you were getting home, joy-traveling woman!" Defends the gallows: "This gallows was set up anciently to serve all three towns." Later laughs at Denis: "Coming from the stoney-faced people of Italy, you could never understand this. We have to make a noise in the morning."
Hank 'Great' Banks
One of the colorfully named Ocean lottery winners: "Caesar Oceano, Thousand-Fathom Thiessen, Hank 'Great' Banks, South-Seas Crispin O'Toole."
Head College of Royal Penny-Whistlers
Proposed musical institution. "To avoid rivalry between the three towns, you could call it the Spanish Head College of Royal Penny-Whistlers." Mary Brandy notes skeptically: "If a boy learns one tune on the penny-whistle, then he is forever spoiled for all other tunes."
Heaven
"He who is throned in Heaven laughs" (Psalms). Chapter 10 epigraph paired with the Irish Song about "Laughing Kelly"—establishing the cosmic dimension of the novel's laughter theme.
Helium-4
Noble gas. Its "efflux into the atmosphere" is one of the cosmic processes disrupted by the Giants' deaths. When Solomon becomes the new Giant, "everything from the magnetism and gravitation of the world to the efflux of Helium-4 was once more right with the world."
Hellenistic World
The Greek-influenced Mediterranean civilization after Alexander. Demotic Greek became the universal language "in the Hellenistic World where the Classical couldn't make a dent."
Hennessee
Irish scientist whose article appears in the Dublin Docket. Mary Brandy reads his article "out loud": "The World is being strangled to death by lack of input. It's as simple as that."
Henry
See Hilary Henry Ardri. One of the computer-named Ardri children: "Hilary Henry, Jane Chanteclaire, Marie Rieuse, Anne Auclaire."
Henry, Hilary
See Hilary Henry Ardri.
Here is Pillar of Little toy
Fragmentary glossary reference.
Hi Brasil
Legendary island west of Ireland. Ancient Irish settlers "founded especially in Newfoundland and Nova Scotia, in the Floridas and the Mexicos and the Antilles, and in Hi Brasil." A mythical western paradise sometimes identified with Brazil or the Fortunate Isles.
Hieronymous Talking-Crow
See Talking-Crow, Hieronymous. "Said" many things about the ancient world's unreality and the lens-shaped earth.
High King
"Specifically the High King of Ireland in the old days." Ard-Rí in Irish. Jane Chantal's married name "Ardri" derives from this title.
High King of Ireland
"In the old days." Jane Chantal explains: "Ard-Ri meant High King, specifically the High King of Ireland in the old days. But I shall change my name to Ard-ban-rion or High Queen."
High Queen
See Jane Chantal High-Queen. Title Jane adopts after Hilary's death: "Ard-ban-rion or High Queen. I was born to be named 'Queen'. Isn't everything working out perfectly!"
High-Queen
See Jane Chantal High-Queen. She and Gorgonius "both asked a question at exactly the same time."
Hilary and Jane
"Of-the-strange-situation, Caesar Oceano" and others—the married couple at the center of the Group of Twelve.
Hilary Henry Ardri
Eldest son of Hilary and Jane Chantal Ardri. "Computer-named." Their "man in New York"—"they maintained a sort of business relationship with him." On the Eighth Day he reports directly without equipment: "Solomon has become very busy in New York. The problem of the world is now understood by the common people here."
History of Rome the Great
"One of the great Lost Books of Atrox." Many believed "the memory of a Grand Rome was not based on any reality, that it was based entirely on a fable that the Giant Atrox wrote in a huge book named The History of Rome the Great."
Holiest of Centuries
The thirteenth century. "The Thirteenth, the Holiest of Centuries, was spared the apprehensive sickness"—the only century in the 109-year locust cycle not afflicted by the Strangle-Death epidemic.
Holland
The Netherlands. "Beer brought down to the sea goblins to consecrate the burial"—five kegs of "the best Holland beer" for Atrox's funeral at Oosterend.
Honorable Meara Timothy Haggerty
See Haggerty, Meara Timothy.
Honorable Sean McEnglish
See McEnglish, Sean. "Meara of Castletown."
Honoré's David and Goliath
Painting. One of Denis Lollardy's masterwork forgeries: "Bosch's The Ship of Fools; Honore's David and Goliath; Beckman's The Dream."
Horace
Roman poet (65–8 BC). Called Lesbian wine "Innocent Wine but he lied when he so called it." Gorgonius knows his wines and his classical critics.
Hsiang Giant
One of the Seven Scribbling Giants, stationed in China/East Asia. A Chinese seaman brings word: "The Hsiang Giant says that he is weary and wishes to die also as soon as he can find a replacement." Later dies in his sleep. Drusilla Evenrood becomes his successor. Hsiang (象) means "elephant" in Chinese—perhaps suggesting great wisdom or memory.
Huesco in Spain
Spanish region (Huesca, in Aragon). Part of the Sioga-Kobald Belt: "Transylvania in the Balkans, Huesco in Spain, Epirus in Greece."
Humankind
"Cannot bear very much reality." T.S. Eliot's line from Four Quartets, used as Chapter 6 epigraph. Applies directly to the novel's themes of reality, unreality, and the human inability to perceive the world's true nature.
Hundred Governors of the Ocean
See Nine Hundred Governors of the Ocean. "And it is on Ocean" wealth that the lottery is based.
Hundred Holy Snakes of Ireland
"One of the most exclusive societies in the world." Countess Maude Grogley belongs to the were-snake families: "I am a member of one of the most exclusive societies in the world, The One Hundred Holy Snakes of Ireland." Despite the legend that St. Patrick drove out the snakes, this secret society persists.
Hundred-and-One Tests of Atrox to Determine When One is Dreaming
Atrox Fabulinus's method for distinguishing dreams from reality, presented in his chapter "The Web of Validity." Hilary tests himself: "Of the one-hundred-and-one tests, I have put myself to thirty of them, the ones that can be performed easily and mentally." Some tests "require materials or devices that are not commonly to be found around the house." Others "seem to be spoofs." The Group worries: "What if we are all dreaming in accord with the one-hundred-and-one tests of Atrox for it, and there is nothing at all beyond the dreaming?"
Hungary
European nation. Gorgonius wonders about "the modern wines of Hungary or France or California."
I
Icelandic
Language of Iceland. One of Denis Lollardy's forgery languages: "Old High Dutch, Icelandic, Demotic Greek, Coptic, Arabic, Ladino."
Ifrit
Powerful Arabian spirit. "I am an Ifrit from the Jinns of our Lord Solomon the King," the creature declares when Monika rubs the true lamp. "You have called me up by rubbing the ancient talismanic lamp. Now I will grant you anything that you want." Monika wants nothing material—only that he "bide with us for a while and tell us all about Ifrits and Jinns and Genii and other principalities and powers." The Ifrit later proclaims Habemus Gigantem when Solomon becomes the new Top Giant.
Ifrit of the Jinns
See Ifrit. "There has to be something you need, or I have lived in vain. I have crossed ten thousand years and a hundred million miles to serve you."
Ifrits
Powerful Arabian spirits. Charles Fort greets their evocation: "Ifrits, Jinns, Genies, denizens of the Ancient Arabian Empire of the low skies, sea stallions, flying horses, birds that can gulp down elephants in a single gulp... my kind of people!"
Ifrits and Jinns
"And Genii and other principalities and powers." Monika asks the Ifrit to explain all the Arabian supernatural beings.
Ike's Chilli Parlor
Painting by Esterhazy, one of Denis Lollardy's exquisite forgeries: "Ewigman's murky The Sun At Midnight; of Esterhazy's Ikes Chilli Parlor; of Jonquil's The Face At The Bottom of The Well."
Illacrove
See Illacrove Giant. "Giant died during the night just past."
Illacrove Giant
One of the Seven Scribbling Giants, stationed in Ireland. A messenger reports: "The Illacrove Giant, whom I serve, says that he is weary and wishes to die also as soon as he can get a replacement." Mary Brandy Manx becomes his successor. The name may derive from Irish Iolra Crobh ("many-clawed") or a place name.
Illo Tempore
Latin: "In that time." Opening phrase of liturgical readings. Jane Chantal suspects Denis forged papal encyclicals: "What do you make of such writings as In Illo Tempore or Vir Autem Quidem or Et Compelle ut Intrare? Everybody thinks that the Pope wrote them. I think that Denis wrote them."
India
Asian subcontinent. According to Alexander the Great: "everything to the east of the Indus River complex, and that includes most of India itself, is unreal."
Indian
See Cigar Store Indian. "Of Randall's mysterious It Isn't What You Think; of Mary Morehouse's Nine Ducks"—among Denis's forgeries.
Indians
Native Americans. Referenced in connection with the totem poles of British Columbia.
Indonesian Island
Morotai, "on the other side of the globe." Jane Chantal writes birds into existence and tries to send them there: "Then I wrote that they should go out and populate Morotai, an Indonesian Island on the other side of the globe. But they fly off a little ways and then they come back. They don't seem to have any idea how to get to Morotai Island."
Indus River
Major river of South Asia. According to Alexander the Great: "everything to the east of the Indus River complex, and that includes most of India itself, is unreal."
Infestation of the Sussex Wraiths
"A Friday Night feature of the disease" in the North Sea region. "It is said that they take their bat-flights from the ancient Evenrood Manor in England." The wraiths are "small pipe-smoking, squeaking bats, who claim that they are giants"—manifestations of the failed casual English Intellectuals. See Sussex Wraiths.
Inner Wadden Sea and the Outer
"Wadden Sea, for Terschelling Island was only a mile and a quarter wide at their place." The Dutch island where Laughter-Lynn's father lives sits between the two bodies of water.
Innocent Wine
Horace's ironic name for Lesbian wine: "the Lesbos which Horace called Innocent Wine but he lied when he so called it."
Intellectual
See Casual English Intellectuals. "Named Sandra Ott"—one of the fake giants.
Intellectuals
See Casual English Intellectuals. Myrtle Mobley "quickly set forty-two more places at breakfast" for them.
Intimations of Immortality in Early Computer Science
Work by Diogenes Pontifex, quoted in the novel. "That is the main difference between them"—distinguishing the living from the dead. The title echoes Wordsworth's "Intimations of Immortality."
Intimations of Transcendent Intellect in Early Childhood
Description of Leo Parisi's gifts: "He did give Intimations of Transcendent Intellect in Early Childhood. He did come into the world trailing clouds of glory when he came." Echoes Wordsworth's "Intimations of Immortality."
Intrare
See Compelle ut Intrare.
Intrepid Three
"Laughter-Lynn Casement, Leo Parisi," and Saint Faunus. The trio who climb the mountainside at Lecco "striking new springs of mountain water out of new-splitting rocks." All three are killed in the Saturday night rock-slide: "Then the voice of the rock-tumble turned into thunder, and the Intrepid Three were buried."
Introit
Opening prayer of the Mass. "In the Laughter of the Saints, before the Day Star, I begot thee is the beginning passage of the Introit of my mass of Saint Faunus."
Iofel
"Sometimes known as the Trickster Angel." Solomon Izzersted's claimed father. "He used to impregnate women of the goyim quite unknown to them, just for the laughs everybody would have when such women bore indubitably Jewish children. Iofel is the only angel known for certain to be Jewish. He is the most ethnic of the angels." Solomon goes to New York "to be about my father's business, to be about the business of my father Iofel."
Iofel the Trickster Angel
See Iofel. Solomon's divine parentage gives him "that multi-depth face that he had to have from his natural father Iofel."
Ireland
Island nation. Location of Gaire Castle and the Illacrove Giant. Laughter-Lynn lives "half of every year in Gaire Castle in Ireland." Also: "Holy Ireland of course" was part of the real ancient world according to Alexander.
Irish
Of or from Ireland. The Bronx contained universes where "Jews, Irish, Italians, Blacks, and Germans coexisted with each other." Also: the Irish language is identical to Manx—"only Irish spoken in a brandy voice."
Irish and Scotch-Gaelic
Languages related to Manx. "Books will tell you that it is related to Irish and Scotch-Gaelic. As a matter of fact the Manx language is identical to the Irish language."
Irish Garden
One of the themed gardens at Denis Lollardy's Lecco estate. Contains the Foinse na n'Óg (Fountain of Youth). "Prominent in them" on the Eighth Day.
Irish Gardens
"And there" the Fountain of Youth is found. "Among the many fountains and sources and springs and wells in the Irish Gardens of the Lollardy Estate was one very small-throated fountain."
Irish Giant
Atrox Fabulinus was "a fifth century Irish Giant who sailed with pirates in his youth." Later captured by Roman-Goths and sold into slavery.
Irish Scientists
Authors of articles in the Dublin Docket "about the dire situation of the world." Include Hennessee, Delaney, and Monroney.
Irish Song
Chapter 10 epigraph: "Oh we buried Laughing Kelly in a box without a top. / 'You are dead now, man,' we told him, 'and that laughing's got to stop.'" Countess Maude whistles this tune.
Isaiah
Hebrew prophet. "Says" things about giants and the cosmic order.
Islands and the Scandinavias
"And all shores of the North Sea"—regions affected by the Sussex Wraiths on Friday nights.
Isle of Man
Island in the Irish Sea. Home of Mary Brandy Manx. "Twenty-nine miles from Ireland, thirty-one miles from England, and twenty-one miles from Scotland. But the miles to Scotland are very long miles because of the treacherous currents and the howling winds." In "sympathetic miles, the Isle of Man is nearest to Ireland." Setting for Chapters 8 and 9 (Friday and Saturday). "The Giants on the Isle of Man are very shy."
Isradel
Archangel who guards the gates of Gaire/Eden. "Oh, Isradel, it is so good to see you again," Laughter-Lynn greets him. Perpetua echoes: "Now I'm oriented and at home in the place called The Eighth Day of The Week." The museum catalog says he is "a Bronze Statue of an Angel with a Flaming Sword, Property of the City of Dublin. But he is not bronze. He is of Archangel flesh, and he is alive. Angels commonly move so slowly that people don't realize that they're alive."
Italian
Of or from Italy. The Lecco region has "marl-and-loam very near to" the surface.
Italian Garden
One of the themed gardens at Lecco. Listed with "Moravian Garden, Aragonese Garden, Armenian Garden, Persian Garden, Arabian Garden and Japanese Garden."
Italian Gardens
"Of the wonderful Lollardy Estate." Gorgonius walks there while composing.
Italians
People of Italy. The Bronx contained "Jews, Irish, Italians, Blacks, and Germans" coexisting. Also: Denis forged "music masterworks and operas of all the great Germans and Italians."
Italy
European nation. Location of Lecco, Sora, and the Lollardy Estate. Countess Maude was "a foreign correspondent in Italy and Palestine."
Italy and Palestine
"As well as in the Low Countries"—places where Countess Maude worked as a journalist before her marriage.
Izzersted
See Izzersted, Solomon. Surname of the "best mathematician in the world."
Izzersted, Solomon
"World-best mathematician, sometimes" ventriloquist's dummy. See Solomon Izzersted.
J
Jacob
Father of Saint Joseph. Sea Captain Cornelius recognizes the Galilean carpenter: "I noticed the name on his small package, Joseph Jacobson, so then I knew for sure that he was Saint Joseph; for the father of Saint Joseph was named Jacob."
Jacobson
See Joseph Jacobson. "So then I knew for sure" it was Saint Joseph by his patronymic.
Jane Chantal
See Ardri, Jane Chantal. "An artist in all the arts." Her computer is housed in a hunting-horn. Murdered by a nine-foot feather, she is resurrected as Jane Galatea and eventually becomes Jane Chantal High-Queen, successor to the El-Khatar Giant.
Jane Chantal and Hilary
"Ardri and Hieronymous" Talking-Crow—members of the Group of Twelve. The Ardris are the central couple.
Jane Chantal High-Queen
Jane's title after becoming the El-Khatar Giant. Adopts the name after Hilary's death: "Ard-Ri meant High King... But I shall change my name to Ard-ban-rion or High Queen." She invokes Charles Fort: "Abra dabra ookie ort / Come and visit, Charley Fort." Listed with "Perpetua Parisi, Gorgonius" as the surviving members.
Jane Galatea
The resurrected Jane Chantal's name for herself. "My name is Jane Galatea. I love 'Who am I?' for a morning game." Like Pygmalion's statue brought to life, she is newly created: "I am nine years old, and I am Jane Galatea, not Jane the-other-name." Gradually recovers her memories and identity.
Jane Galatea Chantal
"Spoke sorrowfully." The transitional identity between Jane Galatea (the newly resurrected being) and Jane Chantal High-Queen (the fully restored Scribbling Giant).
Jane High-Queen
See Jane Chantal High-Queen. Shortened form of her title.
Jane Hunting-Horn
Solomon's name for Jane: "You are Jane Hunting-Horn. And you have your hunting-horn hanging around your neck now." Her computer is housed in the horn. She is "adept at doing that jackass laugh without using an instrument at all. She was truly the artist of all the arts."
Jane Hunting-Horn Chantal
Full version of the hunting-horn epithet. Jane asks Father Kirkpatrick: "What happened to 1235?"—the century without the Strangle-Death epidemic. "Do you believe in giants?" she asks. "I mean the Writing Giants who write the world?"
Jane Whatever
"Cautioning again." The narrator's placeholder for Jane's uncertain identity during her resurrection: "Let us all stay very close together, people."
Jane What's-Her-Name
"Howled." Another uncertain identity marker during Jane's gradual recovery of herself.
Jane-
"Like." Fragment suggesting Jane's various identity states throughout the novel.
Janie
Diminutive of Jane. "How old are you now," Hilary asks the resurrected creature. Used affectionately by other Group members: "Let us all stay very close together," Janie counsels.
Japanese Garden
One of the themed gardens at Denis Lollardy's Lecco estate: "French Garden, English Garden, Italian Garden, Moravian Garden, Aragonese Garden, Armenian Garden, Persian Garden, Arabian Garden, and Japanese Garden all in high style."
Jeffres
Harold Jeffreys (1891–1989), British mathematician and geophysicist. Chapter 8 epigraph (attributed "1970"): regarding probability, "the conclusion would be that the system cannot exist." His skepticism about statistical inference resonates with the novel's themes of reality and unreality.
Jewish
Of the Jewish people. Iofel the Trickster Angel "used to impregnate women of the goyim quite unknown to them, just for the laughs everybody would have when such women bore indubitably Jewish children."
Jews
Jewish people. Charles Fort notes the Bronx contained coexisting universes of "Jews, Irish, Italians, Blacks, and Germans." Also: Denis forges in "Ladino (the tongue of the Jews of Constantinople)."
Jimmy the Greek Tuttleburg
Writer on mysterious fortunes. The Ifrit quotes him: "Some of the very largest fortunes in the world have owners whom I can only describe as 'Lords of Smoke'"—meaning Ifrits who hold vast wealth invisibly.
Jinns
Arabian spirits, from which the Ifrit comes. Charles Fort celebrates them: "Ifrits, Jinns, Genies, denizens of the Ancient Arabian Empire of the low skies." The Ifrit is "from the Jinns of our Lord Solomon the King."
John and Solomon
"Made a sort of truce with each other, though they never felt real fraternal love each for each." The ventriloquist and his belly-growth maintain an uneasy partnership.
John Barkley
See John Barkley Towntower. "Soon after he learned to talk with his own voice," the belly-growth Solomon was already showing superior intellect.
John Barkley Towntower
"The second best mathematician in the world, and the best ventriloquist." Born with "a dark and sullen growth on his belly"—Solomon Izzersted. His stage name is John Barkley Towntower, but Solomon compelled him to legally change his name to Solomon Izzersted. Performed at the Caladium Music Hall with "his talking belly-button." Killed by Leonardo biting out his stomach; buried on the Isle of Man.
John Barkley Towntower's
"Belly." Where Solomon Izzersted resided as a parasitic twin.
John Barkley's
"Belly." See John Barkley Towntower.
John How
Fragmentary reference in the narrative.
John's and Solomon's
The shared existence of the two personalities in one body.
Joseph
See Saint Joseph and Joseph Jacobson. "Named Jacob"—his father's name establishes his identity.
Joseph Jacobson
Saint Joseph the Carpenter's full name (incorporating his patronymic). Sea Captain Cornelius identified him by this name on his package. Laughter-Lynn greets him: "Oh, it is Saint Joseph, the carpenter from Galilee arriving. We are so glad to see you, Joseph Jacobson." He built the Circular Stairway and repairs the steam calliopes.
Josh Lantern's Secrets of the Seas Monthly
Periodical quoted in the novel, source of information about the Ocean lottery. "Ocean Captains, Ocean Captains, I had already guessed the secret of Caesar Oceano," Drusilla says after reading it.
Joyeuse Vice-Reine
French: "Joyful Vice-Queen." Name of Jane Chantal's computer: "Her joyous computer (it was named Joyeuse Vice-Reine and it was a female computer) never failed her." Inhabited by a sprite kindred to a poltergeist, "but less obtrusively adolescent." Produces Jane's art even in her absence.
Judas
The betrayer of Christ. Leo Parisi predicts: "Symmetry or floating justice or ultimate compensation or something almost requires that we should have a Judas in our group." Denis confirms after Leonardo's treachery: "Every Group of Twelve has its Judas, except that Leonardo stood a little bit outside of our strict count of twelve." The apostle Matthias replaced Judas: "With the Prototypical Group of Twelve, there was a second twelfth, to replace Judas, remember, who dropped from the twelve."
K
Kabouter
Dutch goblin or gnome. One of the supernatural "Little People, the Fairies, the Lamiae" with their own Eden legend. Laughter-Lynn's father is Fernand Kabouter Casement, and she is "partly of the Kabouter blood." During her fifty-five years in the goose egg, she "lived those fifty-five years in the deep underground as a Goblin, a Kabouter, a Shoga, a Kobald, a Troll, a Fairy, a Monkey-Face." Also: "everywhere that they set up settlements and fishermen's villages they found that a Kabouter was already there running a store."
King
"Of that master forger Denis." Also: Solomon Izzersted becomes "King of Corn" for owning Aladdin's Lamp, and the Ifrit serves "our Lord Solomon the King."
Kinglet
See Gothic Kinglet. Flavius Placidius Valentinianus, "delighted, and he told Atrox to sit down and write the history of the world."
Klavierholtz
German: "Piano-wood." "Gorgonius built his pianos from Klavierholtz and from nothing else, and this had become a problem. It was a slow-growing wood, and he had already plundered much of the German Alps for it." The "resounding music of the free-standing Klavier-trees in the howling crest-winds" gives the Alps their sound.
Klavierschloss
German: "Piano Castle." Home of Gorgonius and Monika Pantera in the German Alps. Has "one thousand and one rooms" with one thousand and one keys.
