Gorgonius loves "open doors banging in the wind" on "all eight sides" of the house. Contains the Wife Room where six previous wives are buried. Atrox has a writing room here. Setting for Chapter 10 (Sunday). The pianos play Sunday at Klavierschloss for Three-Hundred-and-Ninety-Nine Player Pianos.
Klee's Twittering Machine
Painting by Paul Klee (1922). One of Denis Lollardy's masterwork forgeries, listed with "Miro's The Harlequin's Carnival; Bouguereau's" works.
Kobald
German goblin. Laughter-Lynn lived underground as "a Goblin, a Kabouter, a Shoga, a Kobald, a Troll, a Fairy, a Monkey-Face." Part of the Sioga-Kobald Belt stretching across Europe.
Kobald Belt Iceland
See Sioga-Kobald Belt. The northern extent of the supernatural creatures' territory.
Kricketball
"Of a boy." Cricket ball, used to describe Solomon Izzersted's spherical shape.
L
Ladino
Judeo-Spanish language. One of Denis Lollardy's forgery languages: "Ladino (the tongue of the Jews of Constantinople)."
Lafferty
R.A. Lafferty (1914–2002), author of East of Laughter.
Lafferty All
"Rights reserved." Copyright notice.
Lake Como
Italian lake in Lombardy. "Denis did live in Lombardy in Italy, in the town of Lecco where the river Adda flows out of Lake Como."
Lake Tenkiller
Lake in Oklahoma. The Ardris live "on the Tenkiller Lake in Oklahoma."
Lamia of Italy
Italian supernatural creature. "A present-day Lamia of Italy (they are quite hard to interview, believe me) has told me that the founding and ornamentation of their own Eden (its name was Gaire)... happened eleven years before... the human Eden."
Lamiae
Plural of Lamia. "The Puka, the Sioga, the Goblins, the Kabouter, the Little People, the Fairies, the Lamiae, they all had their own version of the Eden Legend."
Land of Nod to the East of Eden
"Had its echo in advance of the fact." Genesis reference: "And the land of Nod where Cain dwelt in the Land of Nod to the East of Eden had its echo in advance of the fact."
Lastoir de Gaire
Irish: "East of Laughter." Inner suburb of Dublin where Countess Maude Grogley was born, "much older than Dublin which had engulfed it a few centuries ago. The people of this inner suburb were the original Irish who are older than the Irish." Location of Gaire Castle.
Latin
Classical language. One of Denis's forgery languages: "Low Latin, Tuscan, Old French, Old Italian, Spanish, Cataline."
Laughing Christ
See Laughing Christ of Creophylus. "Of Creophylus which he had done only" short months ago—Denis's greatest forgery.
Laughing Christ of Creophylus
"Perhaps the greatest of the forgeries of Denis Lollardy." The original disappeared from a Roman villa in AD 453. Denis's version "was better than the original"—"It worked miracles." Cures melancholy, changes a Roman lady's nose, makes a non-believer pray. Atrox claims Denis stole his original: "You stole from me the thing I most prized in my life, the thing that has authorized my strange continued life."
Laughing Kelly
Figure from Irish song (Chapter 10 epigraph): "Oh we buried Laughing Kelly in a box without a top. / 'You are dead now, man,' we told him, 'and that laughing's got to stop.'"
Laughter-Liffey, Maude Grogley
Countess Maude's full authorial name for her book Observations of Things Both Before and After the Beginning of the World. Combines "Laughter" (family name) with the River Liffey (Dublin's river).
Laughter-Lynn Casement at Oosterend
Shipping destination. "The manifest was for shipment to Laughter-Lynn Casement at Oosterend"—the seven steam calliopes.
Lecco
"Italian lake-town setting, site of 'seven flutes.'" Beautiful town in Lombardy "where the river Adda flows out of Lake Como." Home of Denis Lollardy's estate. "The great trees and breath-taking boscage and grass were so deep a green that they looked blue." Setting for Chapters 4 and 9 (Monday and Saturday). Site of Saturday at Lecco for Seven Flutes.
Lecco for Seven Flutes
See Saturday at Lecco for Seven Flutes. "And they went over the sound" of the performance.
Lecco in Italy
Location of Denis Lollardy's estate and the novel's Italian scenes.
Lector
Latin: "Reader." Addressee of Atrox's chapters.
Lector Delectus
Latin: "Chosen Reader." "If you are standing up, sit down for a moment"—Atrox addresses his select audience.
Ledger
"Has to say this day." Reference to cosmic accounting or divine record-keeping.
Leo and Perpetua
"Drusilla and Laughter-Lynn and Mary" Brandy—the paired members of the Group. Brother and sister, both teenagers.
Leo Parisi the Wonder-Boy
See Parisi, Leo. His epithet as a nuclear scientist prodigy.
Leo Parisi's
"Excellent laboratories." Where scientific work is done.
Leonardo
See Leonardo the Great. "Caesar's partner, Great the Golden Panther, princely" beast who becomes the Group's Judas.
Leonardo the Great
The Golden Panther, Caesar Oceano's partner. "For this particular manifestation of mine, Caesar, I am to be called by the name Leonardo the Great." Claims to be "a Black Panther who happens to have a golden mark on me everywhere except this one bar on my forehead." Sets up the Green Pasture Counselling Service. Becomes moody, attacks John Barkley Towntower, and is hanged on the Isle of Man gallows. Bears "the Mark of Cain"—the golden coloring that protects him. "Every Group of Twelve has its Judas."
Leonardo the Great the Golden
See Leonardo the Great. "Panther" combined with his full title.
Leonardo the Great the Golden Panther
See Leonardo the Great. Full title emphasizing both his greatness and his beast nature.
Lesbos
Greek island, source of Lesbian wine. "Which Horace called Innocent Wine but he lied when he so called it."
Lese Geant
French: "Injured Giant" (lèse-géant, on the model of lèse-majesté). "And it made her nervous"—offense against giants.
Likely Myrtle Mobley
"Maid of all functions spilled some of the" blood on Leonardo—explaining his bloody appearance.
Liri River
"In the foothills of the Apennine Mountains." Location of Sora, where the Ardris have their Italian villa.
Lollard
"Had once meant a forger." Historical term (originally for followers of Wycliffe) reinterpreted: "besides meaning a mumbler, the word Lollard had once meant a forger."
Lollardy
See Lollardy, Denis. "All-purpose forger" and family name.
Lollardy Estate
Denis Lollardy's magnificent property at Lecco with its themed gardens (French, English, Italian, Moravian, Aragonese, Armenian, Persian, Arabian, Japanese, and Irish).
Lollardy, Denis
See Denis Lollardy. "Most famous forger, Lollardy estate master."
Lombardy
Italian region. Denis lives there; motto: "Awaken to Laughter." Sometimes confused with "Lollardy."
Lombardy in Italy
"In the town of Lecco where the river Adda flows out of Lake Como."
Lombardy Poplar
"That he has on his coat-of-arms." Denis Lollardy's heraldic device.
London
British capital. Publisher location for Gollancz.
London Poly
London Polytechnic. "Have devised one-hundred-and-one tests by" which to determine dreaming.
Lord
"453." Reference to the year AD 453, when the original Laughing Christ disappeared "in the year of the Lord 453."
Lord Solomon the King
Biblical King Solomon. The Ifrit comes "from the Jinns of our Lord Solomon the King."
Lords of Smoke
Jimmy the Greek Tuttleburg's term for Ifrits: "Some of the very largest fortunes in the world have owners whom I can only describe as 'Lords of Smoke.'"
Low Latin
"Tuscan, Old French, Old Italian, Spanish, Cataline"—Denis's forgery languages.
Lydia
Ancient kingdom in Asia Minor. "And spied on all the people with his long ears and nose"—King Midas of Lydia.
Lynn
See Laughter-Lynn Casement. Shortened form of her name.
Lynn and Mary Brandy
"Hilary and Jane"—abbreviated reference to Group members.
M
Mayoral
"Residence at Port Saint Mary." Mary Brandy's official dwelling.
Magician, Mandrake the
See Mandrake the Magician.
Magicians
"But I believe" in them—discussion of supernatural practitioners.
Malta
Mediterranean island nation.
Manchester University of the Arts
British institution. Source of some of the casual English Intellectuals.
Mandrake the Magician
Play "purported to be by William Shakespeare" but actually forged by Denis Lollardy. "Old Shakes could never have attained such competence. The Mandrake, which is probably the greatest drama ever written could only have been crafted by Denis Lollardy, the greatest playwright who ever lived."
Manor in England
See Evenrood Manor. "Named reference in the narrative."
Manor in Sussex
See Evenrood Manor. "Give me no satisfaction at all this morning."
Manx
Language of the Isle of Man. "Which is still understood by one person in three on the Island... As a matter of fact the Manx language is identical to the Irish language. It is only Irish spoken in a brandy voice."
Manx, Mary Brandy
See Mary Brandy Manx.
Mark of Cain
The golden mark protecting Leonardo. Denis explains: "He was a black panther with the golden Mark of Cain all over him. How many bad men have been spared because they bore the beautiful golden Mark of Cain! Then the Lord gave Cain a mark so that no one finding him should kill him."
Maronean
Wine from Maroneia, Thrace. One of Gorgonius's ancient wines: "wonderful red Pramnian, the Clazomenian, the Maronean."
Mary Brandy
See Mary Brandy Manx. Her common name.
Mary Brandy Manx
"Mayor of Port Saint Mary on the Isle of Man." Got her middle name "because of her brandy voice"—"She wasn't a drinking woman. She had got that mellow and slightly strained voice from shouting at the gulls, terns, loons, and other sea-and-shore birds." "Mayor, hell, she was Meara of the town!" Becomes successor to the Illacrove Giant. One of the Group of Twelve.
Mary Brandy Manx in Port Saint Mary
"Port-town setting" for the Isle of Man chapters.
Mary Brandy's
"Place, leaving a Manor House full of" intellectuals—her residence on the Isle of Man.
Mary for Three Penny-Whistles
See Friday at Port Saint Mary for Three Penny-Whistles.
Mary MacWattin
"Best woman in the whole show, save only yourself." Mary Brandy's housemaid who serves as acting mayor. "Still it is better that I run it than to let the power fall into the hands of the political opposition in the form of Gregory O'Growley."
Mary Morehouse's Nine Ducks
Painting. One of Denis Lollardy's forgeries: "And also of her Seven Swans."
Mary, of Port Saint
"In the absence of Mary Brandy"—the town during Mary MacWattin's stewardship.
Masefield
John Masefield (1878–1967), English poet and novelist. Referenced in connection with sea literature.
Mass for the World Mortally Sick and Perhaps Dying
Liturgy said at Klavierschloss on Sunday. "When, three hours later, the priest of the Castle came to say the Mass Before Dawn it was not the designated Mass of Sunday of the Twelfth Week of Ordinary Time but was instead the Mass for the World Mortally Sick and Perhaps Dying."
Mass of Sunday of the Twelfth Week of Ordinary Time
The regular Sunday liturgy, replaced by the Mass for the dying world.
Maude
See Countess Maude Grogley. "And perhaps it is immortal"—reference to her membership in the One Hundred Holy Snakes of Ireland.
Maude Grogley the Countess
See Countess Maude Grogley.
Mayor, Madam the
Title for Mary Brandy Manx.
McEnglish of Castletown
See McEnglish, Sean. "Read out loud to the citizens" the article by Monroney.
McEnglish the Mayor of Castletown
See McEnglish, Sean. "Castle site" and civic leader.
McEnglish, Sean
"Honorable Meara of Castletown." Mayor of one of the three Isle of Man port towns. Reads the Dublin Docket article by Monroney. Forbids cutting down Leonardo from the gallows.
Meanwhile
"Gioia di Sotto La Montagna, the old lady of the neighborhood"—narrative transition.
Meara
Irish: "Mayor" or civic leader. "Of the town." Mary Brandy was "Meara of the town!"
Meara of Castletown
See McEnglish, Sean. "Castle site and recurring" civic presence.
Mediterranean Susie Swing
"China Seas Charley Wong, Caesar Oceano"—colorfully named Ocean lottery winners.
Merry Lecco
See Gioioso Lecco. Italian name for the region in Saint Faunus's golden age.
Merry Mariners Big Book of the Ocean
Nautical reference work quoted in the novel.
Middle Armenian
Medieval Armenian language. One of Denis's forgery languages: "Ghees, Amharic, Middle Armenian."
Midsummer Eve
"Snow was proverbially the last snow of the season." The novel's temporal setting—the week beginning Midsummer Eve.
Midsummer Night
"Of one of the very final years of the" twentieth century. The Saturday night/Sunday morning of the novel's climactic events.
Midsummer's Eve
"Last time that June 21 would fall on Sunday" in the twentieth century. The novel's opening timeframe.
Mighty Ocean Mill
"Which is powered by the tidal" forces. One of the wonders of the Ocean.
Milano
Italian: Milan. Referenced in the Lombardy setting.
Milky Way
"Candy bars." Humorous reference mixed with cosmic imagery.
Milligan
Irish surname. Referenced in the narrative.
Miro's The Harlequin's Carnival
Painting by Joan Miró (1924–25). One of Denis Lollardy's masterwork forgeries: "Bouguereau's" works listed alongside.
Miss Drusilla
"Even for you." Formal address for Drusilla Evenrood by her servants.
Miss Drusilla and to Miss Laughter-Lynn
"And to all the other ladies and gentlemen"—Mayor Haggerty's greeting.
Mistress Drusilla
"Not as dead as was earlier believed." Myrtle Mobley's note on the grave peg.
Moby Dick
Herman Melville's novel. "Has written: All the attending marvels of a thousand"—quoted for its ocean imagery.
Monica
Variant spelling of Monika.
Monika
See Monika Pantera.
Monika Pantera
"Who doesn't have to be anything except Monika." Wife of Gorgonius, Princess of the German Alps, keeper of "one thousand and one keys" to Klavierschloss. Seventh wife (previous six buried under the Wife Room). Rubs Aladdin's Lamp to summon the Ifrit. Signs letters "Monika The Great, but only to very close personal friends, less than two of them in the world."
Monroney
Irish scientist. "Out loud"—his Dublin Docket article is read by Mayor McEnglish.
Monroney in the Dublin Docket
"That Mayor" McEnglish reads aloud to the citizens.
Mont Blanc
Alpine peak. "Have just told me"—referenced in Alpine discussions.
Montagna
Italian: "Mountain." See Gioia di Sotto La Montagna. "Old lady of the neighborhood, had returned with the" nine-gallon cup.
Moravia
Central European region. Part of the Sioga-Kobald Belt: "Brittany in France, Transylvania in the Balkans."
Moravian Garden
"Aragonese Garden, Armenian Garden"—themed gardens at the Lollardy Estate. Denis doesn't remember the Moravian Garden at all.
Morning Ogre-Sioga
"Came in and found pleasant" company. One of the supernatural visitors to the Group.
Morotai Island
"Island setting, maritime limen." Indonesian island. Jane Chantal tries to send her written birds there but "they fly off a little ways and then they come back."
Mortimers Undertakers
Funeral service referenced on the Isle of Man.
Mother Maude
Laughter-Lynn's address for Countess Maude Grogley.
Mr
Title of address used throughout.
Muscle Man of the Seven Seas
Title or epithet for a sea-going strong man.
Muslims of the Left Hand of God
Religious group referenced in Alexander the Great's cosmology.
Myron McMasters
"From the State F&G Department asked" about Hilary's fish business. The official who wondered how Hilary operates without a Commercial Fisherman's License.
Myrtle
See Myrtle Mobley. "Mobley cried as Drusilla Evenrood led her own group."
Myrtle Mobley
"Simple woman easily impressed by casual English Intellectuals." Drusilla Evenrood's servant at the East Sussex manor. "So she quickly set forty-two more places at breakfast." Writes notes on grave pegs. Possibly spilled blood on Leonardo.
Mystery of Evil
"On him"—the inexplicable darkness in Leonardo the Great.
N
Napoleon
French emperor (1769–1821). Drusilla recalls: "In a side-show at a carnival I once saw the skull of Napoleon when he was nine years old. But there was something tricky about that, and there's something tricky about this"—comparing the sideshow fraud to the newly-resurrected Jane Galatea.
Napoleons
"And drivel." Reference to counterfeit coins or inflated claims.
Nazanderan in Persia
Mazandaran, northern Iranian province. Part of the Sioga-Kobald Belt: "Transylvania in the Balkans, Huesco in Spain, Epirus in Greece, Esh Sharqi in Syria, Nazanderan in Persia or Iran." These regions have "families who renew the rocks" in ritual arrangements.
New Chapters Found at Sora
Newly discovered writings of Atrox Fabulinus. "All of the recent ones seem to be major"—they arrive mysteriously "just before dawn-light, in a plain brown envelope."
Newfoundland and Nova Scotia
Canadian regions. Ancient Irish settlers "founded especially in Newfoundland and Nova Scotia, in the Floridas and the Mexicos and the Antilles."
North America
"Right on the same continent with Hilary." Solomon Izzersted lives in Broken Arrow, Oklahoma, "only fifty miles from the Ardris."
North American
"Of only a few years ago, but I forget his" name—reference to a recent authority.
North American Continent
"And pieces of the South." The Americas as settled by ancient Irish seafarers.
North Atlantic
"From the Equator to the North Pole." To the old North Sea People, "it was all the North Atlantic" that constituted their domain.
North Atlantic Ocean
The extended "North Sea" of the Island-Friesians' maritime world.
Nymphs
See Okeanoids and Nereids. Ocean spirits encountered in the underwater descent at Oosterend.
O
Observations of Things Both Before and After the Beginning of the World
Book by Countess Maude Grogley Laughter-Liffey. "She was my mother, a very intelligent woman," Laughter-Lynn explains. "Before she was married, she wrote for the Dublin newspapers and was a foreign correspondent."
Ocean Father Cristobol Colon
Christopher Columbus. Title used in the maritime mythology of the novel.
Ocean Nymphs
See Okeanoids. "As well as Okeanogigantoi, Ocean-Giants"—the supernatural sea beings encountered at Oosterend.
Oceano
"Oceano surname and maritime pun, tied to Caesar's" identity. His name suggests both the ocean and the ancient god Oceanus.
Oceano and Prince Leonardo the Great
"John" Barkley and others—the partnership that runs Strange Cargoes Worldwide Shippers.
Oceano Doesn't Know About
See Strange Cargoes That Even Caesar Oceano Doesn't Know About.
Oceano, Caesar
See Caesar Oceano. "Tycoon of Strange Cargoes World-Wide" Shipping Company.
Oceano, Cargo
Punning variant of Caesar Oceano's name.
Oceano, Cedric
"Had been called the Muscle Man of the Seven Seas." One of the Strange Cargoes sea captains.
Ogre-Siog
"Very intelligent person, began to give them his own" views on reality. An ogre variant of the Sioga. "There are two sides to the world, the inside and the outside. The inside is real and the outside is less than real. Mostly we Sioga live on the inside or real side of the world."
Ogre-Sioga
Morning visitor to Gaire Castle. "The Morning Giant will come, and the Morning Angel, and the Ogre-Sioga." Finds "pleasant accompaniment with Perpetua Parisi." Visits "to steal apples or, in my case, to visit with the Countess Maude Grogley whom I love."
Okeanogigantoi
Greek: "Ocean-Giants." Encountered at Oosterend: "They were surrounded by Okeanoids and Nereids, Ocean Nymphs, as well as Okeanogigantoi, Ocean-Giants. Oh, those were a ragged bunch!" They live at "a thousand fathoms deep or even deeper" where reality does not extend.
Okeanoids
Greek: "Ocean-Nymphs." Sea spirits: "Okeanoids and Nereids, Ocean Nymphs."
Okeanoids and Nereids
"Ocean Nymphs, as well as" Ocean-Giants. The supernatural inhabitants of the deep sea at Oosterend.
Oklahoma
U.S. state. Home of Hilary and Jane Chantal Ardri on Lake Tenkiller, and of Solomon Izzersted in Broken Arrow. "And he represents us as sketchy and silly"—Atrox's unflattering portrayal of the Ardris.
Oklahoma Hospital
"And she is still there thirty-eight years" later. Reference to long-term institutionalization.
Oklahoma Time
"This evening." Time zone reference for the Ardris' location.
Oosterend
"Dutch-Friesian settlement and recurring shoreward" setting. Town on Terschelling Island where Laughter-Lynn's father lives, "within the sound of both the Inner Wadden Sea and the Outer Wadden Sea." Site of Atrox's burial at the Tuama no Fathach (Giant's Tomb). Setting for Chapter 6 (Wednesday). The Circular Stairway descends to "the floor that was only two levels below the sounding sea" and then to "Drowned Man Shoal, three levels below the booming sea."
Oosterend for Seven Steam Calliopes
See Wednesday at Oosterend for Seven Steam Calliopes. "Sounded" gloriously once Saint Joseph repaired them.
Oosterend in the Frisian Island
"Of Terschelling." The precise location of Laughter-Lynn's second home.
Oosterend Sea-House
"And Evenrood Manor in East Sussex"—paired locations of the Group's adventures.
Oranges, Finnegan's Orange Period
"Of Mockman's"—one of Denis Lollardy's art forgeries.
Orion Publishing Group Ltd Orion House
Publisher information for the novel.
Other Side of Strange
Book by Peter Tompkinson, one of the sources quoted in the novel.
Otto
Servant of the Alpine Giant. "Who lived higher up on the mountain came to Gorgonius" with the message that the Alpine Giant wishes to die. "The Alpenriese, the Alpine Giant, whom I serve, says that he is weary." Otto announces: "It takes twelve hours for a giant to die... a Scribbling Giant dies best with an audience."
Outreach, Roderick
One of the casual English Intellectuals who becomes a false giant. Author of "On Hybridizing The Future, And The Pitfalls of It in the spring Futuristic Review." Dismisses Atrox's outline as "just a little bit of grave-reek or wrack." Proclaims: "We are the Seven Giants who will henceforth write the world!" Dies during the Strangle-Death night, becoming one of the Sussex Wraiths—"small pipe-smoking, squeaking bats, who claim that they are giants."
Overseas Edition
International publication referenced in the novel.
Oxford
"Cambridge University Observatory, the Royal Military" College—British institutions. Some of the casual English Intellectuals claim Oxford credentials.
P
Panic Marshals
Authorities who control communications during crises. Mary Brandy warns: "We're going to be jammed off the air instantly by the Panic Marshals. Let us close the conference now and meet in the flesh somewhere tomorrow."
Pannonian Gothic Kinglet Flavius Placidius
See Gothic Kinglet. Flavius Placidius Valentinianus, the ruler who purchased Atrox as a slave and commanded him to write the history of the world.
Pantera
"Probably the finest composer of fiddle music in the" Alps. Family name of Gorgonius, Monika, and Perpetua.
Pantera, Gorgonius
See Gorgonius Pantera. "Piano-maker of the German Alps."
Pantera, Monika
See Monika Pantera. "Pantera spouse, insists on being nothing but" Monika.
Panteras
"Had seen any of them before." The Pantera family: Gorgonius, Monika, and their daughter Perpetua.
Panther, Leonardo the
See Leonardo the Great. "Rigid in death, hanging by the" neck on the Isle of Man gallows.
Panther, Leonardo the Golden
See Leonardo the Great. "Gave the answer" to questions about the Strange Cargoes business.
Panther, Leonardo the Great the Golden
See Leonardo the Great. Full title.
Panthers
"Rampant on hind legs filling the doorway." Leonardo claims to be "the titular ruler of all the Black Panthers in the world."
Panther's Teeth
Solomon Izzersted was "torn from the navel of John Barkley Towntower by the ravening teeth of Prince Leonardo; so I am truly born From the Panther's Teeth. If there isn't a prophecy-and-legend connected with that, there will be."
Paris
"Of France in the nineteenth century." Referenced in discussions of art forgery.
Paris of France
"In the nineteenth century." The art world center.
Parisi
"Boy Wonder and Nuclear Scientist, and his wife Perpetua" Parisi. Family name of Leo and Perpetua.
Parisi at Sora in Italy
The Parisi villa location "in the middle mountains of Italy."
Parisi, Leo
"Boy wonder nuclear scientist, proposes" investigating the unreality of the world. Sixteen years old, married to Perpetua. "A nuclear scientist who knows that the atoms are no more than empty boxes." Author of The Problem of the Flimsiness of the Atoms. "He did give Intimations of Transcendent Intellect in Early Childhood." One of the Intrepid Three killed in the Saturday night rock-slide. His last words: "Goodbye, Perpetua; every minute of it was fun."
Parisi, Perpetua
"Pantera daughter, Parisi spouse, family tie to" both households. Nineteen years old, "a forever person" as her name indicates. Daughter of Gorgonius and Monika Pantera, seventh daughter and "special." A logician practicing Behavioristic Logic. Owns thirteen pianos from her father—"the minimum number for a piano orchestra." Widowed when Leo is killed in the rock-slide.
Patagonia
"Solomon, the Alpine Giant said." South American region. "The Land of Attending Marvels, as the whale Moby Dick has written: All the attending marvels of a thousand Patagonian sights and sounds helped to sway me to my wish."
Patagonian Giant
Solomon Izzersted's adopted title. His business card reads: "SOLOMON IZZERSTED THE PATAGONIAN GIANT. I DO FUTURES."
Patents Act
"1988." Copyright legal reference.
Patrick
Saint Patrick of Ireland. Despite his legend of driving out snakes, the One Hundred Holy Snakes of Ireland persist.
Paul the Python Pemmican
Colorfully named sea captain in the Strange Cargoes fleet.
Perpetua and Jane Chantal
"And all of them railed" at the Ifrit's corny entrance. The women of the Group.
Persian Garden
"Arabian Garden, and Japanese Garden all in high style." One of the themed gardens at the Lollardy Estate.
Peter Tompkinson
Author of The Other Side of Strange, quoted in the novel.
Peterhouse and Corpus Christi and Magdalene
"Of Cambridge." Cambridge University colleges from which the casual English Intellectuals claim to come, along with "Balliol and Merton and All Souls and Somerville of Oxford."
Pforte
German: "Gate" or "Door." From the key-verse Monika uses to open the special room in Klavierschloss: "Machen die Pforte auf immer für mich!" ("Open the gate forever for me!"). Warning: "Persons who try to open other stubborn doors with that key-verse will usually sicken and die soon afterwards."
Philosopher Polycarp
Ancient thinker. "The Philosopher Polycarp was of the opinion that reality did not extend more than nine fathoms deep into the ocean, and he was right." The Ocean-Giants live far below this depth in total unreality.
Piano Castle of Gorgonius
See Klavierschloss. "And Monika Pantera in the" German Alps.
Pillars of Righteousness
"First of the Pillars" that sustain the world. Twenty-one pillars in three groups of seven: the Seven Sustaining Saints, the Seven Sustaining Technicians, and the Seven Scribbling Giants. Monika's wish to the Ifrit: "Of the twenty-one Pillars of Righteousness that support the world, one of them is still missing. Replace it before the world itself collapses." The seventh giant position, replacing Atrox, is the crucial "head member of the leading or stress seven."
Pine Tree
"Forgery from life." Denis Lollardy's living masterpiece. Caesar Oceano says: "I bet God is jealous of that one." Denis replies: "Pine trees are among the few things, among the very few things, that God does badly."
Pirate
"Price-Cut-Throat of the Seven Seas." Caesar Oceano's former advertising slogan: "I will not be undersold on any item."
Pitfalls of It
See On Hybridizing The Future, And The Pitfalls of It. Roderick Outreach's article "in the spring Futuristic Review."
Pnigmophobia
Greek: fear of choking or suffocation. Father Kirkpatrick explains the Nine Day Wonders: "They are characterized by Pnigmophobia, both for the individual person and the world." The Strangle-Death epidemic causes nightmares of choking—"and so they do choke to death, a few millions of them, in their violent sleep."
Political Opponent Gregory O'Growley
See Gregory O'Growley. "The Political Opposition to Mary Brandy Manx in Port Saint Mary."
Port Erin
"Port Saint Mary"—one of the three Isle of Man port towns. Mayor Haggerty's jurisdiction. Has black mules rather than Castletown's white mules.
Port Saint Mary
"Manx port-town and mayoral home base." Town on the southern part of the Isle of Man "known as Spanish Head." Mary Brandy Manx is Mayor (Meara). Setting for Chapter 8 (Friday). Site of the gallows where Leonardo is hanged. "There were political malcontents in Port Saint Mary, persons who sometimes became wrathy against that she-outcast on the hill."
Port Saint Mary on the Isle of Man
"Port-town setting" for the Isle of Man chapters.
Port, Haggerty of
"Erin." See Haggerty, Meara Timothy.
Portrait
"Goya Third of May 1808; the Copley Watson"—Denis's masterwork forgeries.
Pramnian
Ancient Greek wine. Gorgonius loves "the wonderful red Pramnian, the Clazomenian, the Chian, the Lesbos." At Sora they "exuberated in the wonderful air that was itself like wine, specifically like the wonderful red Pramnian wine."
Presence of the Lord
"And dwelt in the Land of Nod to the East of" Eden. Genesis reference: Cain went out "from the presence of the Lord."
Price-Cut-Throat
Caesar Oceano's advertising epithet: "Caesar Oceano, Pirate, the Price-Cut-Throat of the Seven Seas."
Princess, and
"And they are entitled to use The Great with their" given names. Gorgonius and Monika are Prince and Princess of the German Alps.
Problem of the Flimsiness of the Atoms
"Of the" universe. Leo Parisi's paper on the essential emptiness of matter: "the atoms of which the universe and its furniture were made were empty boxes."
Producers
Those who create the world's substance, contrasted with the Scribbling Giants who write its narrative.
Property of the City of Dublin
The museum catalog's description of Isradel: "a Bronze Statuette of an Angel with a Flaming Sword, Property of the City of Dublin."
Property of the City of the Eighth Day
Isradel's second identification on the Eighth Day: "Property of the City of the Eighth Day."
Prototypical Group of Twelve
"There may not be a" thirteenth. The Twelve Apostles, prototype for the novel's Group. "But with the Prototypical Group of Twelve, there was a second twelfth, to replace Judas, remember, who dropped from the twelve."
Psalms
"He who is throned in Heaven laughs" (Psalm 2:4). Chapter 10 epigraph establishing the divine dimension of laughter.
Publications Building
Location referenced in the novel's journalism subplot.
Purgatory
Catholic doctrine of post-mortem purification. Referenced in discussions of the afterlife and resurrection.
Q
Queen
"Laughed." See Jane Chantal High-Queen. Jane adopts the title Ard-ban-rion (High Queen) after Hilary's death: "I was born to be named 'Queen'. Isn't everything working out perfectly!"
R
Rabelais
François Rabelais (c. 1494–1553), French Renaissance writer. Atrox Fabulinus is "the Roman Rabelais." Denis "projected Rabelais out of my Sixteenth Century mind" into Future France, but "He perversely wrote in the opposite direction from that which I projected and he didn't write about the future at all. He wrote about me, Atrox, but he gave it out that it was fiction."
Raphael Sancho
"Painting is discovered." Likely one of Denis Lollardy's forgeries.
Raphaelus
Hero of Atrox's writings. "In the act of opening a giant goose egg to fry it in an" iron skillet—the episode that prompts Atrox to recount "the history of the world up to this point." The egg contains "a nubile young girl."
Residence at Port Saint Mary
"And the great Estate" of Mary Brandy Manx.
Review
See Futuristic Review. Publication where Roderick Outreach's article appeared.
Rhine
"Wine, and asked them how they wanted their eggs." Myrtle Mobley serves "hock, or perhaps some cheaper Rhine wine" to the English Intellectuals.
Riant Giant
French: "Laughing Giant." Solomon Izzersted's title as the new Top Giant. "His demotic name will be the Riant Giant or the Laughing Giant. And his hieratic name must remain secret." Called "the Eighth Wonder of the World." His projection at the rally was "a hundred feet high, and as round and ruddy as the full moon itself."
Rieuse, Marie
"Ardri child, computer-named, laughter-marked." One of the five Ardri children: "Hilary Henry, Jane Chanteclaire, Marie Rieuse." Rieuse is French for "laughing woman."
Roderick Outreach
See Outreach, Roderick. "Same" man throughout the narrative—the arrogant English Intellectual who leads the false giants.
Roman
"Lady and made it a thing of joy instead of a thing of horror"—the Laughing Christ miraculously changed her nose.
Roman Connection
"Last citizen of the Old Roman Empire." Atrox's link to ancient Rome.
Roman Rabelais
Epithet for Atrox Fabulinus. "Scribbling Giant" who writes the world's narrative. Atrox is Rabelais's prototype—or rather, Rabelais wrote about Atrox in fictional form.
Roman-Goths
"In a salt-water scuffle off the coast of Spain." Atrox was "captured by Roman-Goths" and sold into slavery.
Rome
"In Italy." Ancient city whose grandeur may have been written by Atrox: "the memory of a Grand Rome was not based on any reality, that it was based entirely on a fable that the Giant Atrox wrote."
Royal Military College
"At Sandhurst." British military academy from which some casual English Intellectuals claim to come.
Royal Observatory
"At Edinburgh, Dunsink Observatory in" Dublin. Institutions whose data confirms the world's unreality.
Ruben the Rubberneck
Vaudeville performer. Solomon's candidate for giant "can make it by stretching his neck. He is very good at that. He used to substitute for Ruben the Rubberneck in vaudeville whenever Ruben had too sore a neck to go on. He was better than Ruben at neck-stretching."
Ruppert
See Colonel Ruppert. "Beer"—the Yankees owner's beverage.
Rupperts
"Favorite of mine also." Charles Fort's affection for Ruppert's beer.
Ryhfiaiit
"System." Obscure term, possibly a transliteration error or esoteric reference.
S
Saints in Heaven
"Now." Those who have passed through the laughter of the saints to eternal joy.
Samuel Butler
English author (1835–1902). "It has been said, by Samuel Butler, that although God cannot alter the past, historians can. So the historians' is no mean calling." Applied to the Scribbling Giants who write history itself.
San Francisco
"And every year in early summer I get lonesome" for it—Charles Fort's nostalgia.
Sandhurst
See Royal Military College. "From Peterhouse and Corpus Christi and Magdalene"—the elite institutions.
Sandra Ott
"One of the new giantesses." Dame of the Realm, casual English Intellectual who becomes a false Scribbling Giant. "The world may now move again. Whatever we write will be fulfilled." Learns to summon the Constabulary by writing in her journal. After the Strangle-Death night, the Sussex Wraiths have "the pipe-smoking faces of those neo-giants, the dead Roderick Outreach and the live Sandra Ott."
Sanrio Giant
One of the Seven Scribbling Giants, stationed in East Asia. "Weary of the world." Caesar Oceano becomes his successor—fitting because "have you ever looked at the eyes of Caesar Strange Cargo Oceano?" (slant-eyed, qualifying him for the Asian position).
Scandinavias and the Germanies
"Moravia, Brittany in France"—regions of the Sioga-Kobald Belt.
Science Fiction
"& Fantasy titles through the SF Gateway." Publisher category for Lafferty's work.
Sciotail
Irish: "Giggle" or "Tittering." "Or Giggle Castle"—another name for Gaire Castle (Caislean Sciotail).
Scorpions
"Size of horses." Part of Charles Fort's Fortean Universe menagerie.
Scotia
Nova Scotia. "In the Floridas"—ancient Irish settlements.
Scotland
"Or England nobody knew." The Isle of Man is twenty-one miles from Scotland, "but the miles to Scotland are very long miles because of the treacherous currents and the howling winds."
Scotland and Ireland
"In the Amorica"—ancient Celtic connections.
Scottish
"Coast) drank brandy with Mary Brandy." Father Kirkpatrick is "a tall Scottish priest."
Sea Captain Cornelius
See Cornelius. "Here" at Oosterend, telling his story of Saint Joseph building the Circular Stairway.
Sea Captain's
"Weeds, and he bowed to all of them." Cornelius in his formal attire.
Seamans
"Sand-lot team in San Francisco." Baseball team reference.
Second Article of Question 73 on Supplement to the Summa Theologica
Thomas Aquinas's theological work. "Saint Thomas decides that toward the time of the Judgement the Sun and Moon will in truth be darkened." Addresses how long the darkened interval lasts.
Secret Admirer
Unnamed character in the novel.
Settiflauti
Italian: "Seven Flutes." See Cipriano Settiflauti. "Or Seven Flutes"—performer at Lecco.
Seventh, George the
"That's good." Royal reference in humorous context.
Seventh, Perpetua the
"Daughter of Gorgonius." Perpetua is Gorgonius's seventh daughter, and Monika is his seventh wife—both "special."
SF Gateway
Digital publisher of science fiction and fantasy classics.
Shadow of Prince Leonardo the Great
"There at the" door. Every member of the Group of Twelve "has a shadow"—mysterious doubles or alternate aspects.
Shamus
See Shamus McJames.
Shamus McJames
"Mumbled as he tried, unsuccessfully, to" accomplish some task. Irish character.
Shepherdess
"Ruisdael The Jewish Graveyard; Caravaggio's"—paintings in Denis's forgery collection.
Ship Captain Cornelius
See Cornelius. Laughter-Lynn's drowned husband who returns as a ghost.
Shippers
"Which ocean enterprise he himself operated in"—Caesar Oceano's Strange Cargoes business.
Shippers Limited
See Strange Cargoes Worldwide Shippers Limited.
Shog
"Plural Shoga." Old form Siog. Human larva-stage beings. "The days and years spent as a Shog do not count against the allotted days and years of a life."
Shoga
"Human larvae, are kept" in special boarding schools. Plural of Shog. "Larva of Humans, that's what the Shoga are. They are the tadpoles, the caterpillars, the imagos of humans." Laughter-Lynn spent fifty-five years as "a Goblin, a Kabouter, a Shoga, a Kobald, a Troll, a Fairy, a Monkey-Face." Their mating produces "changelings."
Show-House Lane
Dublin street near Gaire Castle.
Sick and Perhaps Dying
See Mass for the World Mortally Sick and Perhaps Dying.
Sinners
Those in need of the world's redemption through laughter.
Siog and Sioga
Old forms of Shog and Shoga. Irish fairy/goblin beings.
Sioga
"Goblins, the Kabouter, the Little People, the Fairies, the" Lamiae. Irish supernatural beings living "on the inside or real side of the world." Part of the Sioga-Kobald Belt across Europe and the Middle East.
Sky Chamber
Elevated room or observatory, possibly at the Parisi villa.
Solar
"System are subject to serious objections." Scientific data showing the unreality of the world.
Solomon Izzersted and John
"Barkley Towntower." The two personalities sharing one body.
Solomon Izzersted Institute
Institution founded or named for Solomon.
Solomon Izzersted the Patagonian Giant
Solomon's business card reads: "SOLOMON IZZERSTED THE PATAGONIAN GIANT. I DO FUTURES."
Solomon Other-Person
"That John Barkley Towntower had" as his belly-growth. "It was as a cover for the Solomon Other-Person that John Barkley" developed his ventriloquist act.
Solomon the Talking Belly-Button
"Best" character in the Port Saint Mary Banner funny papers. "We like Solomon the Talking Belly-Button the best."
Somerville
"Of Oxford, and from Manchester University of the" Arts. Oxford college from which casual English Intellectuals claim credentials.
Somewhere in Scripture
"Such a time is described as when" the world needs giants. Biblical resonance.
Sora
"Italian locale used as day-stamped chapter setting." Town "in the foothills of the Apennine Mountains, sixty miles or ninety-nine kilometers east of Rome." Location of the Ardris' Italian villa and Leo Parisi's birthplace. "A place that had purposely been made hard to find." Setting for Chapter 4 (Monday).
Sora and Gaire Castle
"And Oosterend Sea-House, and" Evenrood Manor—the four recurring locations.
Sora in Italy
"Place that had purposely been made hard to find." Near the Liri River.
South-Seas Crispin O'Toole
"Blue-Fish Harry Miller, Coconut-Island Pat Silber"—colorfully named Ocean lottery winners.
Spain
"And he was handed on from slave market to slave market." Atrox was captured off the coast of Spain.
Spanish
"Cataline, Old High Dutch, Icelandic, Demotic Greek"—Denis's forgery languages.
Spanish Depths
"That she submerged, hung that dress on a rock"—Countess Maude's swim in the Fountain of Youth.
Spanish Head
"When the Group of Twelve arrived." Southern promontory of the Isle of Man. "There were bonfires burning at Spanish Head." Location of all three port towns: Port Erin, Port Saint Mary, and Castletown.
Special Fortean Universe
"Or in the larger General" Universe. Charles Fort's discovered cosmos within the greater creation.
Stage Irishmen
Stereotypical theatrical Irish characters. Denis asks "why are they all acting like a pack of Stage Irishmen?" Mayor Haggerty laughs: "Oh, just for the everlasting fun of it. We have to make a noise in the morning."
State F&G Department
See State Fish and Game Department.
State Fish and Game Department
"Spied on Hilary" Ardri. Myron McMasters from this department questioned how Hilary runs a fish business without a Commercial Fisherman's License—proof of the world's unreality.
Strange Cargo
"In the Epistle of Paul to the Hebrews are the" words about entertaining strangers. Also: the mysterious shipments of the Strange Cargoes company.
Strange Cargoes Worldwide Shippers
Shipping company owned by Caesar Oceano and Leonardo the Great. "Sky-ships, ocean-ships, every kind of ships." Leonardo arrived via this company "from the Exterior Darkness." Together they "took over the Strange Cargoes Worldwide Shippers Limited" and made it profitable.
Summa Theologica
"Aquinas." Thomas Aquinas's theological masterwork. The Second Article of Question 73 on the Supplement addresses the darkening of Sun and Moon "toward the time of the Judgement."
Summertime Boys
"Forever." Youthful members of the Group who remain perpetually young.
Superman
"Uses a telephone booth to change into his Superman" costume. Reference to the comic book hero's transformation, compared to the Group's use of world terminals.
Support the Solomon Izzersted Non-Partisan
Political movement backing Solomon as the new giant.
Surrentine
"Aminean." Ancient wine from Sorrento. One of Gorgonius's favorites: "the Falernum, the Vina Horna, Fugacia, Surrentine, Aminean."
Sussex
"England." County in southeastern England. Location of Evenrood Manor. "Named reference in the narrative."
Sussex Blood Pudding
"On him when she served him." Myrtle Mobley's cooking, possibly explaining the blood on Leonardo.
Sussex in England
County location of Evenrood Manor and setting for Chapter 7 (Thursday).
Sussex Song
Local folk music of East Sussex.
Sussex Wraiths
"In legend at least." "Small pipe-smoking, squeaking bats, who claim that they are giants." Manifestations of the failed casual English Intellectuals who "reached for giantism and hadn't the ability for it." "It is said that they take their bat-flights from the ancient Evenrood Manor." They claim: "We are angels or messengers sent out to effect the writs of the New Giants." But "Nah, they lied. They were bats."
Swiss
"Magazine says that nine of the twenty greatest fortunes in" the world belong to Ifrits—the "Lords of Smoke."
T
Talking-Crow
See Talking-Crow, Hieronymous. Surname of the pan-scientist.
Talking-Crow, Hieronymous
"Pan-scientist, polymathic" scholar. Member of the Group of Twelve. Author of A Complete Rewriting of Human Biology on Shoga reproduction. Leo Parisi insists Hieronymous is a separate person, not just his pen-name: "We are different persons, and we have met only once." Like all Group members, "he has a shadow." Lives in the United States. "He knows about communications."
Tally-Ho
Hunting cry. Used in connection with the hunt for the new giant.
Technicians
See Seven Sustaining Technicians. "To insure the technology of the world." The second Seven Pillars of Righteousness. "Certainly there is plenty of technology and gadgetry in the world."
Terschelling
Dutch-Friesian island in the Wadden Sea. Home of Laughter-Lynn's father Fernand Kabouter Casement.
Terschelling Island
"Only a mile" and a quarter wide at their place. Laughter-Lynn lives "half of every year in Gaire Castle in Ireland and half of every year with her father on the Dutch-Friesian Island of Terschelling in the Town of Oosterend."
Testimonial Memorial Ballroom
"Test-procedure or" venue. Location for some kind of examination or celebration.
Tests of Atrox
See Hundred-and-One Tests of Atrox. "Showed that they were not dreaming, not by" all the tests they could easily perform.
Tests of Atrox to Determine Whether One
Is dreaming. See Hundred-and-One Tests of Atrox to Determine When One is Dreaming.
Thasian
Wine from Thasos, Greek island. One of Gorgonius's ancient wines: "the Lesbos which Horace called Innocent Wine but he lied when he so called it, this Thasian."
Thebes in Egypt
"Unreal." According to Alexander the Great's cosmology, much of the ancient world was unreal, including Egyptian Thebes.
Theoretical Things That Could
"Be Effected by a" Scribbling Giant. The possibilities of giant-writing.
Thereupon the Golden Panther
Narrative transition when Leonardo reveals his name to Caesar Oceano.
Think-Small Tours
"Into the interiors of atoms." Solomon Izzersted's entrepreneurial scheme: "Who else but me will be able to conduct Think-Small Tours into the interiors of atoms?" Charles Fort explains the technique: "I think small till I'm wandering around in a cell there. Then I think still smaller till I'm wandering around inside a single molecule, and then a single atom."
Thomas
Saint Thomas Aquinas. "Decides that toward the time of the Judgement the Sun and Moon will in truth be darkened."
Thousand-Fathom Thiessen
"Hank 'Great' Banks, South-Seas Crispin O'Toole"—colorfully named Ocean lottery winners.
Thus Charles Fort
"Spoke, and then he sat down quietly with" his strange information about the Fortean Universe.
Timbuktu Giant
One of the Seven Scribbling Giants. "Weary of the world and its ways and wished to die." Sends to Denis Lollardy: "For the last four hundred years, the Timbuktu Giant has been in charge of necessary forgeries in writing the world." Denis becomes his successor—and thus becomes "Top Giant," not Solomon. "The successor to the Timbuktu Giant is the Top Giant now."
Timore
"Old man of the region." Belongs to "the Folletti people, to the Magi people"—the hobgoblin folk. Brings "a plate that was a plate, and also an imbuto (that was a sort of funnel to eat the eels through) and a rail-splitter to split the bear's bones" for Atrox. Warns: "Atrox is caught up in a paroxysm of anger all this day. He will boil over with blood murder."
Timothy
See Haggerty, Meara Timothy. Mayor of Port Erin.
Tinkers
Irish Travellers. Shelta is "the language of the Tinkers as well as of the Little People." Gaire "meant Laughter" in their tongue.
Townsperson Jane McBane
"At a City Commission" meeting. Source quoted on the Shoga: "Larva of Humans, that's what the Shoga are."
Towntower
"And this was still his stage name." See John Barkley Towntower.
Towntower, John Barkely
"Signed everything over to his" appendage Solomon Izzersted before dying.
Towntower, John Barkley
See John Barkley Towntower. "Second-best mathematician" in the world.
Traceries
"Of ice, millions of years old, forming on the surface"—mysterious natural phenomena in the Fortean Universe.
Trader Horn Hookers
Colorfully named sea captains or vessels in the Strange Cargoes fleet.
Transylvania
"In the Balkans, Huesco in Spain, Epirus in" Greece. Part of the Sioga-Kobald Belt where supernatural families "renew the rocks."
Trickster
"Angel." See Iofel the Trickster Angel.
Trickster Angel
See Iofel the Trickster Angel. Solomon's father.
Trickster Angel Iofel
See Iofel. "The most ethnic of the angels."
Troll
"Fairy, a Monkey-Face." One of the forms Laughter-Lynn lived as during her underground years: "a Goblin, a Kabouter, a Shoga, a Kobald, a Troll, a Fairy, a Monkey-Face."
True Atroculus
"I be the True Atroculus," the Atrox outline mumbles. Latin diminutive form of Atrox.
Tuama
"No Fathach." See Tuama no Fathach.
Tuama no Fathach
Irish/sea goblin: "Giant's Tomb." The granite slab burial site at Oosterend. "A very large tomb has been hollowed out there. The sea goblins have always called it Tuama no Fathach. Yes, that does mean Giant's Tomb in sea goblin language." Atrox is buried there "three levels below the booming sea" with "a five keg funeral at least" of Holland beer.
Tuesday's Guest
"Out there past noon on Tuesday, but we'll"—reference to Atrox's regular Tuesday visits to Gaire Castle.
Tuono Automobile
"And receive for his money a child's"—Italian automobile, possibly miniature or toy-sized.
Tuscan
"Old French, Old Italian, Spanish, Cataline, Old High" Dutch. One of Denis's forgery languages.
Twenty-First Pillar of Righteousness
The crucial missing pillar. Monika's wish to the Ifrit: "Replace it before the world itself collapses." Specifically, the head position among the Seven Scribbling Giants—the replacement for Atrox.
U
Unbreakable Dolls
"At a rowdy Castle party yesterday." Broken despite their name, suggesting the unreality of manufactured claims.
United States
North American nation. Home of the Ardris in Oklahoma. Countess Maude was "a foreign correspondent in Italy and Palestine as well as in the Low Countries and the United States." Hieronymous Talking-Crow lives there too.
University Observatory
"Royal Military College"—institutions whose scientific data confirms the world's unreality.
Unreal and Disgracefully Undetailed Modern World
The central problem of the novel. Leo Parisi, Solomon Izzersted, and John Barkley Towntower "were the ones who were most worried about the Unreal and Disgracefully Undetailed Modern World, though the whole group was worried about their own and the group's unreality."
Upper Saint Martin's Lane
"London, WC2H 9EA." Publisher address for Orion/Gollancz.
Urchin
See Urban Urchin. "Squeaking wheel, got a certain amount of attention from" his parents.
Urchin, Urban
"Ardri child, squeaking wheel who draws" attention. Youngest of the five Ardri children: "Hilary Henry, Jane Chanteclaire, Marie Rieuse, Anne Auclaire, and Urban Urchin." Computer-named. "Got a certain amount of attention from them simply because he was the squeaking wheel."
V
Valentinianus
See Gothic Kinglet Flavius Placidius Valentinianus. "Sent out his seneschal to buy two specified" giants at the slave market.
Village
"Klee's Twittering Machine; Miro's The Harlequin's" Carnival. Denis's forgery of a village scene.
Vina Horna
"Fugacia, Surrentine, Aminean." Ancient wine. One of Gorgonius's favorites: "I love the Falernum, the Vina Horna, Fugacia, Surrentine, Aminean."
Vir Autem Quidem
"Or Et Compelle ut Intrare." Latin phrases. Compelle intrare ("Compel them to come in") is from Luke 14:23, used historically to justify forced conversion.
Visit the SF Gateway
Publisher advertisement for the digital science fiction imprint.
W
Wadden Sea
Shallow sea between the Dutch Frisian Islands and the mainland. Oosterend is "within the sound of both the Inner Wadden Sea and the Outer Wadden Sea, for Terschelling Island was only a mile and a quarter wide at their place."
Waterbury Crystal
"That he forged." Denis Lollardy's mastery extends to cut-glass: "And the cut-glass and Waterbury Crystal that he forged!"
WC2H 9EA An Hachette UK Company
"CIP catalogue." Publisher postal code and corporate affiliation.
Web of Validity
"Gives one-hundred-and-one tests to" determine dreaming. Chapter title from Atrox's writings: "Atrox Fabulinus, in a very curious new chapter The Web of Validity, gives one-hundred-and-one tests to determine whether one is dreaming or not." See Hundred-and-One Tests of Atrox.
Welsh Gardens
"Of the Denis Lollardy estate, but the upper" reaches. One of the themed gardens: "It was near dark where they sat in the big-treed Welsh Gardens of the Denis Lollardy estate, but the upper reaches of the little mountain opposite of them were still twilit."
What's-My-Name Jane
"Insisted." Jane Galatea's identity game after resurrection, gradually recovering her memories as Jane Chantal.
When One
"Dreaming." The tests of Atrox determine "when one is dreaming."
Whistlers' College
See Penny-Whistlers' College. Gregory O'Growley suggests Mary Brandy found "the Spanish Head College of Royal Penny-Whistlers." Mary replies: "It's my experience that if a boy learns one tune on the penny-whistle, then he is forever spoiled for all other tunes."
Whyever
Interrogative adverb used in Irish English dialogue.
William Shakespeare
"Appears, then I know" it's Denis's work. Jane Chantal says of Mandrake the Magician: "When Mandrake the Magician, purported to be by William Shakespeare, appears, then I know that it has to be Denis. Old Shakes could never have attained such competence."
Wonderful Gardens
"Of the enchanting Lollardy Estate at" Lecco. The ten themed gardens: French, English, Italian, Moravian, Aragonese, Armenian, Persian, Arabian, Japanese, Irish, and Welsh.
World
"Though the whole group was worried about their own" unreality. The central concern of the Group of Twelve.
World-Wide Publications Building
"And they were" gathered there. Media headquarters referenced in the novel.
X
[No entries]
The glossary contains no entries beginning with X.
Y
Yankees
"Team is still in existence or not." Colonel Ruppert's New York Yankees. Charles Fort says: "He doesn't know whether his New York Yankees team is still in existence or not. He's got one rule of existence to go by though. 'If the Yankees are in the second division,' he often says, 'then they've dropped out of it. They aren't.'"
Yesterday's Giant
"Also my regular Tuesday's Giant in this" Castle. Mary Brandy says: "I am angry at one giant though, at our Yesterday's Giant." The Countess replies: "I believe that your Yesterday's Giant is also my regular Tuesday's Giant in this Castle. The surly Giant Atrox."
Z
Zappelphilipp
German: "Fidgety Philip," character from Struwwelpeter (1845). The dying Alpine Giant dismisses Solomon: "What is that little antic Kricketball of a boy? Oh, it's a bouncing comic Zappelphilipp, and Ewigerjude-Tand, a jumping toy to amuse the old giant in his dying hours." Solomon retorts: "Before the morning stars sang together I was already wound up."
Zimmer
German: "Room." From Monika's key-verse: "Breche das Zimmer und breche ich dich!" ("I'll break the room and I'll break you!").

Dictionary complete. 830+ entries spanning the novel's characters, places, concepts, and allusions.

Timeline

Before the Journey (Chs. 1–3)

The Group of Twelve is introduced. Hilary discovers the world is unreal through his fish business. Leo finds a bloody nine-foot feather. Seven members are shot by their shadows. Prince Leonardo arrives in a crate.

Monday at Sora (Ch. 4)

The Group gathers at the Parisi villa. Thirteen player pianos play Monday at Sora. Atrox appears as an outline, drinks from a nine-gallon cup, warns the group. Leo and Hieronymous interview Alexander the Great's corpse/spirit.

Tuesday at Gaire Castle (Ch. 5)

Jane Chantal Ardri murdered—speared through the mouth by a nine-foot quill. The villa at Sora buried by earthquake. The Group escapes to Gaire Castle via the eighth-century terminal. Mythical guests arrive: the Morning Giant, the Morning Angel, the Ogre-Sioga, Saint Brandon. Drusilla carries phobic Atrox across the moat. Atrox attempts to "un-murder" Jane by rewriting her.

Wednesday at Oosterend (Ch. 6)

Jane returns as nine-year-old Jane Galatea. The Group visits the undersea realm via the Circular Stairway—meets Caesar's ships and the sea captains. Saint Joseph repairs steam calliopes for Wednesday at Oosterend. Atrox Fabulinus murdered in the Sky Studio—speared through the neck by his own quill.

Thursday at East Sussex (Ch. 7)

Hilary confronts the Strange Man at the murder scene—"young, handsome, fair, smiling... and covered with blood." The man vanishes. Jane and Audrey Evenrood evoke Atrox's outline. The "Seven New Giants" (Casual English Intellectuals with giant goose feathers) form. Roderick Outreach murdered by the Strange Man.

Friday at Port Saint Mary (Ch. 8)

Mary Brandy announces the world is dying from "lack of input." John Barkley Towntower murdered by Prince Leonardo (bitten stomach). Solomon survives as bouncing baseball-sized head. Leonardo hanged—revealed as the Strange Man, killer of Atrox and Jane. Night of Strangulation: "109-year locusts" cause plague of nightmares. Hieronymous Talking-Crow and Hilary Ardri die.

Saturday at Lecco (Ch. 9)

Sun and stars dimmed 12% from lack of Giant input. Jane writes/paints birds and a mahogany table into existence—accepts role as Scribbling Giant. Charles Fort evoked at seance. Denis reveals the Laughing Christ; Saint Faunus emerges. Solomon renews youth in Foinse na n'Og. Rock slide kills Laughter-Lynn Casement, Leo Parisi, and Saint Faunus.

Sunday at Klavierschloss (Ch. 10)

Nine members mourn at Klavierschloss. Sunday at Klavierschloss for 399 Player Pianos—Gorgonius's masterwork. Der Alpenriese asks to die; Gorgonius accepts replacement as Alpine Giant. Monika evokes the Ifrit, who discusses God and "Lords of Smoke." Solomon plans to use "vaudeville ballyhoo" to promote himself as Top Giant.

The Eighth Day (Ch. 11)

The dead and living mingle. Giant successions confirmed: Caesar (Sanrio), Denis (Timbuktu), Jane (El-Khatar), Mary (Illacrove), Drusilla (Hsiang). Monika rubs the true Aladdin's Lamp; the Ifrit drains two galaxies to find the replacement for Atrox. Solomon promotes himself as candidate for Top Giant. "Habemus Gigantem"—the Wave of Reassurance passes through all living people.

The Ninth Day (Ch. 12)

The Group enters the Ninth Day (accessible to ~1000 people). Caesar brings his fungo bat. Solomon projects himself via pantograph as the 100-foot "Riant Giant" in New York, claiming to be Top Giant. The Group confronts him. Gorgonius reveals the rotation paradox: the successor to the Top Giant becomes the Bottom Giant. Denis Lollardy is the true Top Giant. Atrox's ghost assigns Solomon as "the lowest and least"—the Patagonian Giant. Solomon keeps his billion-dollar business and his spherical grin spreads "until it included all of him."

Death Toll

  • Jane Chantal Ardri — murdered Tuesday (Ch. 5) by nine-foot quill through mouth; resurrected as Jane Galatea
  • Atrox Fabulinus — murdered Wednesday (Ch. 6) by his own quill through neck
  • Roderick Outreach — murdered Thursday (Ch. 7) by the Strange Man
  • John Barkley Towntower — murdered Friday (Ch. 8) by Prince Leonardo (stomach bitten out)
  • Prince Leonardo the Great — hanged Friday (Ch. 8) by townspeople of Port Saint Mary
  • Hieronymous Talking-Crow — Night of Strangulation, Friday (Ch. 8)
  • Hilary Ardri — Night of Strangulation, Friday-Saturday transition
  • Laughter-Lynn Casement — rock slide Saturday (Ch. 9)
  • Leo Parisi — rock slide Saturday (Ch. 9); last words: "Goodbye, Perpetua; every minute of it was fun"
  • Saint Faunus — rock slide Saturday (Ch. 9); terminated in his faun form
  • Der Alpenriese — dies Sunday (Ch. 10), voluntarily, with Gorgonius as replacement secured

Final Giant Succession

  • Top Giant (Timbuktu) — Denis Lollardy (via rotation paradox)
  • Alpine Giant — Gorgonius Pantera
  • El-Khatar Giant — Jane Chantal High-Queen
  • Sanrio Giant — Caesar Oceano
  • Hsiang Giant — Drusilla Evenrood
  • Illacrove Giant — Mary Brandy Manx
  • Patagonian Giant (Bottom/Lowest) — Solomon Izzersted

Survivors of the Group of Twelve

Nine members survive to the novel's end: Jane Chantal High-Queen (transformed), Solomon Izzersted (transformed), Perpetua Parisi (widowed), Gorgonius Pantera (Giant), Monika Pantera, Denis Lollardy (Top Giant), Caesar Oceano (Giant), Drusilla Evenrood (Giant), Mary Brandy Manx (Giant).

Geography of the Journey

The Group of Twelve travels across Europe and beyond during their week-long odyssey. Each location has its own character and resonance.

The Americas (Home Base)

  • Lake Tenkiller, Oklahoma: Hilary and Jane Chantal Ardri's home. Site of the Computerized Lake-Fish Company. Eastern Oklahoma—"recreational lake" country.
  • Broken Arrow, Oklahoma: Solomon Izzersted's home, "fifty miles from the Ardris." Home of the Broken Arrow Daily Ledger. Hieronymous complains Atrox portrays Americans as "sketchy and silly" because he "never even visited beautiful Down-Town Broken Arrow."

Italy

  • Sora: Town "in the middle mountains of Italy," "sixty miles or ninety-nine kilometers east of Rome," in the Liri River valley, foothills of the Apennines. Leo and Perpetua Parisi's villa. Site of Monday's feast. Contains "the best reference library in the world" with catacombs holding "the imperfectly dead." Buried by earthquake after Jane's murder; thirteen perpetual player pianos play Monday at Sora underground "forever." Wild bears, giant trout, and big eels in the Liri River.
  • Lecco: Town "where the river Adda flows out of Lake Como." Denis Lollardy's estate with gardens in eleven national styles (French, English, Italian, Moravian, Aragonese, Armenian, Persian, Arabian, Japanese, Welsh, Irish). Site of Saturday's chapter. Contains Foinse na n'Og (Fountain of Youth). Site of the rock slide that kills Leo, Laughter-Lynn, and Saint Faunus.

Ireland

  • Dublin / Lastoir de Gaire: The inner suburb "East of Laughter" (Lastoir de Gaire), "much older than Dublin which had engulfed it a few centuries ago." Home of Gaire Castle, ancestral seat of Countess Maude Grogley and birthplace of Laughter-Lynn. "The people of this inner suburb were the original Irish who are older than the Irish." Site of Tuesday's chapter. Contains the oldest working "modern world terminal" (8th century), a bronze statuette of Isradel the Archangel (once used as a hitching post), and a tram with the destination sign "Gaire."

The Netherlands

  • Oosterend, Terschelling Island: Laughter-Lynn's sea-house in the Dutch-Friesian Islands, "within the sound of both the Inner Wadden Sea and the Outer Wadden Sea"—the island "only a mile and a quarter wide at their place." Site of Wednesday's chapter. Features the Great Circular Stairway (built by Saint Joseph), running from the Monsters' Den (two levels below the ocean) through multiple sea-level floors to the unsupported Sky Studio. The stairway "seemed to be made of wood petrified into red-grained marble." Cellars contain drowned-man ghosts and passages into the Ocean. Home of three drowned-husband ghosts.

England

  • East Sussex: Drusilla Evenrood's manor. Site of Thursday's chapter. Drusilla looks out daily "over the grey-green, South-of-England Ocean" and walks "over the red-and-russet-colored hills of East Sussex." Home of the "Sussex Wraiths" / Seven New Giants (casual English Intellectuals). Associated with the legend of the little girl who carried the giant on her back for sixpence.

Isle of Man

  • Port Saint Mary: Town on the southern part of the island, on Spanish Head. Mary Brandy Manx is Meara (Mayor). "Twenty-nine miles from Ireland, thirty-one miles from England, and twenty-one miles from Scotland"—but Scottish miles are "very long miles because of the treacherous currents and the howling winds." Site of Friday's chapter. Shares an ancient gallows-gibbet with Port Erin and Castletown. The three towns share Old Cow Stew at festivals. Home of the Spanish Head College of Royal Penny-Whistlers (founded Ch. 11). Site of Prince Leonardo's hanging and the Night of Strangulation.

Germany

  • Klavierschloss (Piano Castle): Gorgonius and Monika Pantera's home high in the German Alps. Contains over 1,001 rooms and nearly 700 player pianos. "The whole world might be seen from his high house" (Gorgonius works on curved light to make this literally true). Site of Sunday's chapter. The Alpine Giant (Der Alpenriese) lives nearby and dies here, replaced by Gorgonius. Features the Wife Room (six previous wives buried under floor-stones), rooms requiring eagle-bone keys or spoken verse passwords, and a secret room where Atrox writes new chapters.

Mythic/Otherworldly Locations

  • The Eighth Day: Not a place but a time—"a day outside time." Site of Chapter 11. The dead speak; Solomon's business empire is revealed; newspapers from the Eighth Day (including Wall Street Journal, Eighth Day Edition) report cosmic matters.
  • The Ninth Day: Site of Chapter 12. The Riant Giant appears; the Top Giant paradox is resolved; Solomon accepts his role as Patagonian Giant.
  • Foinse na n'Og (Fountain of Youth): Located on Denis's estate at Lecco. A "natural wellspring" with "a very narrow throat"—only someone "about the size of a baseball" can enter. Solomon renews his youth there; Countess Maude enters in snake form.
  • The Exterior Darkness: Where Prince Leonardo claims to have come from. "I come from the Exterior Darkness, and the carrier was the Strange Cargoes Worldwide Shippers."

Intertextual References

François Rabelais (c. 1494–1553)

Atrox Fabulinus as "The Roman Rabelais"

Rabelais was a French Renaissance writer whose satirical giants Gargantua and Pantagruel combined bawdy humor with theological depth and encyclopedic learning. Atrox Fabulinus is explicitly called "the Roman Rabelais," suggesting he is Rabelais's classical predecessor—a giant who writes the world while indulging in vast appetites (the nine-gallon drinking cup) and intemperate behavior.

Like Rabelais, Atrox mixes the sacred and profane, the cosmic and the scatological. His chapter "The Web of Validity" with its 101 tests is a parody of scholastic methodology—much as Rabelais parodied medieval learning. The novel's overall structure—a group journey punctuated by feasts, music, and theological digressions—echoes the episodic, carnivalesque form of the Gargantua and Pantagruel books.

Charles Fort (1874–1932)

The Fortean Universe

Charles Fort was an American writer who catalogued anomalous phenomena that science couldn't explain—rains of frogs, spontaneous combustion, mysterious disappearances. He coined terms like "teleportation" and speculated that we might be "property" of extraterrestrial beings.

In Chapter 9, Fort himself is evoked at Denis's estate, 66 years after his death. He explains the "Fortean Universe" where atoms are "like a circus or carnival" and the world's troubles are caused by "the hundred-and-nine-year locusts—invisible decapods that feed on the daily-life-elixir." This is classic Fortean speculation: an explanation that is no less strange than the phenomenon it explains.

Lafferty was deeply influenced by Fort's method of cataloguing the impossible, and Fort appears as a character in several Lafferty works. The idea that reality itself is anomalous—that the "unreal" world is the normal condition—is fundamentally Fortean.

Herman Melville (1819–1891)

"The whale who wrote the book"

The Alpine Giant quotes Moby-Dick: "All the attending marvels of a thousand Patagonian sights and sounds helped to sway me to my wish." When corrected that the human author wrote the book, the Giant replies: "Advise me not so, woman, for you are mistaken. I am a Scribbling Giant and I know something about the scribblers' trade, of sources and of authorship, of true hands and of false. I say that it was the whale who wrote the book."

This jest contains a serious point about authorship and authority. The Scribbling Giants write the world; who is to say what they have or have not written? If the world is unreal, then authorship attributions are equally arbitrary. Melville's whale—the White Whale as symbol of inscrutable cosmic meaning—may indeed be the true author of the novel that bears his name.

G.K. Chesterton (1874–1936)

"Multiplex of wing and eye"

When the Ifrit appears, Solomon quotes "a Chestertonian talismanic verse": "Multiplex of wing and eye / Whose strong obedience broke the sky / When Solomon was King." This is from Chesterton's poem "A Song of Gifts to God."

Chesterton's Catholic paradoxes—that humility is the path to greatness, that orthodoxy is the true adventure—pervade Lafferty's work. The novel's climax, where the smallest man becomes a giant but only the bottom giant, while the humble forger becomes the Top Giant, is pure Chestertonian inversion.

Thomas Aquinas (1225–1274)

The Summa Theologica epigraph

Chapter 9's epigraph—"Whether toward the time of the Judgement the Sun and Moon will be darkened in very truth?"—comes from the Supplement to the Summa Theologica, Question 73, Article 2. Aquinas discusses whether the eschatological darkening of the heavenly bodies will be literal or figurative.

The novel literalizes this question: the sun and stars have actually dimmed by 12% due to lack of Giant input. Theological speculation becomes empirical crisis. Lafferty frequently dramatizes scholastic debates in this way, making abstract questions urgently material.

Saint Brendan the Navigator (c. 484–c. 577)

Saint Brandon and the lens-shaped earth

The historical Saint Brendan was an Irish monk famous for his legendary voyage to the "Isle of the Blessed." Medieval texts (Navigatio Sancti Brendani) describe his journey across the Atlantic, encountering sea monsters, mysterious islands, and possibly North America.

In the novel, "Saint Brandon" appears at Gaire Castle and explains his cosmography: the "lens-shaped real earth" floating on the "spherical unreal earth." He describes sailing to "the very edge of the lens-shaped world" and gazing into the void. This transforms the historical legend into a meditation on the geography of reality itself—the real is an island floating in an ocean of unreality.

The Little People Traditions

Kabouters, Sioga, Puka

The novel draws on multiple European traditions of "Little People":

  • Kabouters: Dutch/Flemish household spirits, similar to brownies
  • Sioga/Sidhe: Irish fairy folk, inhabitants of the hollow hills
  • Puka/Púca: Shape-shifting spirits in Irish folklore
  • Lamiae: Classical Greek spirits, sometimes serpentine

Lafferty unifies these traditions by giving the Little People their own Eden—"Gaire" (Laughter)—eleven years before the human Eden. This suggests they are an older, more authentic creation than humanity, living on the "inside" of the world where humans live on the "outside."

Biblical Allusions

Structural and thematic echoes
  • The Group of Twelve: Echoes Christ's twelve apostles, with similar ambiguity about membership (was Paul one of the Twelve? was Matthias?)
  • Seven days + Eighth Day: The seven days of creation plus the eschatological "Eighth Day" of Christian tradition (the day outside time, the eternal Sabbath)
  • Solomon: Named for the biblical king famous for wisdom; son of a "Trickster Angel," echoing the Nephilim (giants born of angels and humans)
  • "Habemus Gigantem": Echoes "Habemus Papam" (We have a Pope), the announcement of papal election
  • The Ten Plagues: Jane gives the Sussex Wraiths "all the ten plagues of Egypt" to drive them out
  • The Fountain of Youth: Echoes the Fountain of Life in Eden; only the smallest can enter

The Patagonian Giants

Historical allusion

When Magellan's expedition reached Patagonia in 1520, they reported encountering giants—people so tall that the Europeans only reached their waists. Antonio Pigafetta wrote: "One day we suddenly saw a naked man of giant stature on the shore of the port, dancing, singing, and throwing dust on his head."

For centuries, "Patagonian Giants" were a fixture of European maps and travel literature. The Alpine Giant quotes Moby-Dick: "Patagonia is the Land of Attending Marvels." Solomon's fate—to become the Patagonian Giant, "the lowest and least"—plays on this history: he becomes a giant associated with the remote, the marvelous, and the possibly-mythical.

Samuel Butler's Dictum

"Historians can alter the past"

The Broken Arrow Daily Ledger quotes Samuel Butler: "although God cannot alter the past, historians can." This is from Butler's Erewhon Revisited (1901).

The novel extends this to the Scribbling Giants: they don't merely record history, they write it. Their "input" creates the world's narrative flow. When their number is reduced, history itself falters—"the world is aimless and arrant when it has no narrative flow or way or direction or impetus to move it."

Percy Bysshe Shelley (1792–1822)

"The Earth and Ocean seem / To sleep in one another's arms"

The Chapter 7 epigraph quotes Shelley's "Epipsychidion" (1821): "Day and night, aloft, from the high towers / And terraces, the Earth and Ocean seem / To sleep in one another's arms, and dream / Of waves, flowers, clouds, woods, rocks, and all that we / Read in their smiles and call reality."

This Romantic vision of reality-as-dream perfectly captures the novel's metaphysics. What we "read in their smiles and call reality" is precisely what the Scribbling Giants write. Shelley's image of Earth and Ocean dreaming together echoes Laughter-Lynn's art series (Earth and Ocean and Sunshine, etc.) and the novel's concern with the interpenetration of the real and unreal.

T.S. Eliot (1888–1965)

"Humankind cannot bear very much reality"

Also in the Chapter 7 epigraph, from Eliot's "Burnt Norton" (the first of Four Quartets, 1935). The full passage: "Go, go, go, said the bird: human kind / Cannot bear very much reality."

This line serves as counterpoint to the novel's premise. If the world is unreal, and humans struggle even with what little reality exists, what happens when Giants stop writing and reality must be "earned"? The "rarified ones" who perceive the world's unreality die from the Night of Strangulation—they cannot bear even the dream of reality.

Tocquet

"Life cannot be completely identified with the physical world"

The Chapter 7 epigraph also quotes: "It appears, therefore, that life cannot be completely identified with the physical world around it."

Robert Tocquet (1898–1985) was a French writer on parapsychology and anomalous phenomena. This quotation aligns with the novel's Fortean sensibility—the insistence that official scientific categories do not exhaust reality.

Erasthenos of Patmos

Of Wanton Giants

The Chapter 2 epigraph quotes a work called Of Wanton Giants by "Erasthenos of Patmos," describing how a giant spied on a deme in Lydia with his "long elephant ears" and "long moist camel nose," wrote all the people's details on clay, dried it, then "broke the piece of clay into very small pieces with a hammer. And all the people in that place were thereby broken into small pieces."

This is likely a Lafferty invention—a mock-classical source describing the same metaphysics of writing-as-creation that governs the novel. The giant's power to create and destroy through writing prefigures Atrox's ability to murder Jane Chantal and then "un-murder" her by rewriting her description.

Arpad Arutinov

The Back Door of History

A fictional work quoted multiple times. Describes "families who renew the rocks" and "families of giants who renew the tales... who maintain the giant writing on the cliffs: but in truth they introduce new giant writing which all the people will have to obey." Also provides the sardonic observation: "An Englishman will lounge about and stare and smoke his pipe for a thousand years with apparently no thought in his mind at all. Then he will get an idea in his mind and he will strike in an instant, and the whole world will reel from the force of his blow. And the idea that galvanized him to sudden action will always be a mistaken idea."

This invented source lends pseudo-scholarly authority to the novel's mythology while allowing Lafferty to satirize both the Sioga-Kobald traditions and the casual English Intellectuals.

The Auctore Fragment

The Fall of Rome

Another fictional source quoted in Chapter 2: "Atrox Fabulinus, the Roman Rabelais, once broke off the account of his hero Raphaelus in the act of opening a giant goose egg to fry it in an iron skillet of six yards' span. Fabulinus interrupted the action with these words: 'Here it becomes necessary to recount to you the history of the world up to this point.'"

This describes Atrox's digressive narrative style (echoing Rabelais and Sterne) and introduces the giant goose egg motif that proves crucial to Laughter-Lynn's double birth.

Puzzles & Mysteries

The Paradox of Fifteen in Twelve

Why are fifteen persons "known as the Group of Twelve"?

The opening roster lists fifteen members yet calls them the "Group of Twelve" with "some of them spares." By novel's end, deaths reduce the group: Jane is murdered but resurrected; John Barkley, Leonardo, Hieronymous, Hilary, Laughter-Lynn, and Leo all die permanently. The "spares" might refer to those destined for death—or the paradox may simply reflect Lafferty's delight in absurdist arithmetic, echoing Christ's twelve apostles with their various configurations.

Possible interpretations: The number twelve has cosmic resonance (twelve months, twelve tribes, twelve apostles); the "extras" may represent mortality's surplus; or the Group functions as a self-organizing entity that maintains its essential "twelve-ness" regardless of actual membership.

The Concerned Circus

Who operates the "Concerned Circus for Distribution of New Atrox Chapters"?

New chapters by a giant dead 1,500 years continue to appear, distributed by this mysterious organization. A related "Concerned Circus" notified the Group of Twelve that they had been "selected to provide extraordinary and onerous service to the world without thought of personal comfort."

Theories: The Circus may be administered by the other Scribbling Giants; it may be a self-perpetuating artifact of Atrox's world-writing; or it may represent the infrastructure of unreality itself—the mechanisms by which the dream-world maintains its own continuity.

Prince Leonardo's Nature and Motive

What exactly is the Golden Panther, and why did he kill?

Leonardo arrives "from the Exterior Darkness" in a crate supposedly from the Panteras (who deny sending it). He claims to be "a Black Panther who happens to have a golden mark" and "the titular ruler of all the Black Panthers in the world." He sets up the "Green Pasture Counselling Service" to ease "tired and troubled souls" yet murders Atrox, Jane Chantal, John Barkley, and Roderick Outreach.

Two women wait beneath his gallows: a golden-dark lady and a female black panther. "She is my sister," the lady explains. "We were born twins. We are of the changing cat-clan. Each of us was brided to him, I in the human and she in his cat form. But the Mystery of Evil was on him and we could do nothing."

The puzzle: Was Leonardo an angel or devil "unaware"? His good works (counseling troubled souls) seem genuine, yet so do his murders. Lafferty seems to suggest that certain beings are simply agents of chaos, necessary to the world's operation but ultimately incomprehensible.

The Shadows and the Skulkers

What are the fourteen or fifteen "shadows" that follow the Group?

Hilary notes: "The fourteen or fifteen entities that are shadowing our Group of Twelve are alien to us and are surely organized. So there is organization out there. And there is alienism outside of our dream." These shadows shoot seven members in Chapter 3 (none fatally). Leonardo has his own shadow—"a scraggly black panther... an astute and deadly shadow. Deadly, deadly, deadly!"

Unresolved: The shadows suggest a counter-organization, perhaps agents of whatever lies outside the Giants' written world. Their role in the novel's cosmology is never fully explicated.

The Night of Strangulation

Why do Hieronymous and Hilary die while others survive?

The "hundred-and-nine-year locusts"—invisible decapods that "feed on the daily-life-elixir"—cause suffocating nightmares that kill "a few millions" worldwide. Father Kirkpatrick warns that "the fifth night is usually the worst."
